recipe.title: Persian Shirazi Salad
recipe.summary: Finely diced cucumber, tomatoes and onion brightened with lime, dried mint and olive oil.
ingredients: 3 Lebanese cucumbers, cut into 1 cm dice
4 tomatoes, cored and cut into 1 cm dice

stages.title: Prepare the vegetables
steps: Cut the cucumbers into 1 cm dice and place them in a large bowl.
Cut the tomatoes in half, scoop out the watery seeds and cores with a teaspoon, then dice the flesh into 1 cm pieces and add to the bowl.
Finely chop the red onion and add it to the bowl.

stages.title: Mellow the onion
steps: Sprinkle the onion and vegetables with the salt and toss gently.
Leave the bowl to stand at room temperature for 10 minutes so the onion softens and loses its harshness.
Tip off any liquid that has pooled at the bottom of the bowl.

stages.title: Dress and serve
steps: Whisk the lime juice, olive oil and dried mint in a small bowl, rubbing the mint between your fingers as you add it to release its flavour.
Pour the dressing over the vegetables and toss to coat.
Season with black pepper and extra salt if needed, then serve straight away while the vegetables are still crisp.

tips: Scooping out the tomato seeds keeps the salad from turning watery and diluting the dressing.
Dicing everything to the same small size means each spoonful has a balance of cucumber, tomato and onion.
Rubbing the dried mint between your fingers warms it and releases more aroma into the dressing.
Dress the salad just before serving, because salt and acid draw water out of the vegetables and soften them.
variations: Swap the lime juice for lemon juice, or add 1 tsp sumac for a more tart finish.
Stir through a handful of chopped fresh mint or parsley in place of the dried mint.
recipe.storage: Best eaten straight away. Leftovers can be kept in an airtight container in the fridge for up to 1 day, though the vegetables will soften and release liquid; drain before serving.

recipe.title: German Apple Pancake
recipe.summary: Puffed oven-baked pancake with buttery apples, cinnamon and crisp golden edges.

stages.title: Heat the oven and make the batter
steps: Heat the oven to 220°C (200°C fan) and place a 25 cm heavy ovenproof frying pan inside to heat.
Whisk the eggs, plain flour, milk and salt in a bowl until smooth and thin, with no lumps of flour.
Rest the batter on the bench while you prepare the apples.

stages.title: Prepare the apples
steps: Peel, core and cut the apples into 5 mm thick slices.
Mix the white sugar and ground cinnamon in a small bowl.
Toss the apple slices with the cinnamon sugar until evenly coated.

stages.title: Cook the apples
steps: Carefully take the hot pan from the oven and place it over medium heat on the stovetop.
Add the butter and swirl until melted and foaming, about 30 seconds.
Add the apples in an even layer and cook, turning occasionally, for 4–5 minutes until just starting to soften and the sugar turns syrupy.

stages.title: Bake the pancake
steps: Whisk the batter once more, then pour it evenly over the apples in the pan.
Return the pan to the oven straight away and bake for 15–18 minutes until puffed, deep golden at the edges and set in the centre.
Serve immediately, cut into wedges, before it sinks.

tips: Heating the pan in the oven first makes the batter sizzle on contact, which helps the edges rise high and crisp.
Cut the apple slices thin and even so they soften in the pan and bake through under the batter.
Room-temperature eggs and milk give a smoother batter and a better rise, so take them out of the fridge before you start.
Keep the oven door shut for the first 15 minutes, as opening it lets heat escape and the pancake can collapse.
variations: Use pears instead of apples and add a pinch of ground nutmeg to the cinnamon sugar.
Serve with a dusting of icing sugar and a squeeze of lemon juice for a sharper finish.
recipe.storage: Best eaten straight away. Leftovers keep in an airtight container in the fridge for up to 2 days; reheat in a 180°C (160°C fan) oven for 8–10 minutes until hot through.

recipe.title: Portuguese Caldo Verde
recipe.summary: Velvety potato soup with ribbons of kale and smoky chouriço in a garlicky broth.
ingredients: 500 g potatoes, peeled and cut into 2 cm cubes
200 g kale, stems removed, leaves very finely shredded

stages.title: Prepare the vegetables and sausage
steps: Peel the potatoes and cut them into 2 cm cubes so they cook evenly.
Strip the kale leaves from the stems, stack the leaves and slice them as finely as you can.
Finely chop the onion and garlic, and slice the chorizo thinly.

stages.title: Soften the onion and garlic
steps: Heat the olive oil in a large heavy-based pot over medium heat.
Add the onion and 1/2 tsp salt and cook, stirring, for 5 minutes until soft and translucent.
Add the garlic and cook for 1 minute until fragrant, without letting it brown.

stages.title: Simmer the potatoes
steps: Add the potatoes, chicken stock and 750 ml water to the pot and bring to the boil over high heat.
Reduce to medium-low and simmer, partly covered, for 18–20 minutes until the potatoes fall apart when pressed with a spoon.

stages.title: Cook the chorizo
steps: While the potatoes simmer, heat a frying pan over medium heat with no extra oil.
Fry the chorizo slices for 4–5 minutes, turning once, until browned at the edges and the fat has run out.

stages.title: Blend and finish the soup
steps: Remove the pot from the heat and blend the soup with a stick blender until completely smooth.
Return the pot to medium heat, add the kale and simmer for 4–5 minutes until the kale is tender and bright green.
Stir in the chorizo and its fat, season with black pepper and extra salt if needed, and simmer for 1 minute until piping hot, then serve.

tips: Slice the kale as finely as possible; thin ribbons turn tender in minutes and stay bright green instead of tough and olive-coloured.
Choose a floury potato such as a Sebago or Desiree, because the starch thickens the blended soup without any cream.
Frying the chorizo separately renders its fat and browns it, so you can control how much paprika-rich oil goes into the soup.
variations: Drizzle a little extra olive oil over each bowl and serve with crusty bread, as is traditional in Portugal.
For a vegetarian version, use vegetable stock and replace the chorizo with a pinch of smoked paprika fried in the onion oil.
recipe.storage: Refrigerate in an airtight container for up to 3 days, or freeze for up to 2 months. Reheat in a pot over medium heat for 8–10 minutes until piping hot, adding a splash of water if it has thickened.

recipe.title: Jamaican Rice and Peas
recipe.summary: Fluffy coconut rice with kidney beans, thyme, spring onion and gentle allspice warmth.
ingredients: 400 g kidney beans, drained and rinsed
2 spring onions, bruised with the flat of a knife

stages.title: Prepare the rice and aromatics
steps: Rinse the rice in a sieve under cold running water until the water runs almost clear, then drain well.
Drain and rinse the kidney beans.
Bruise the spring onions with the flat of a knife and leave them whole.

stages.title: Simmer the coconut base
steps: In a medium saucepan over medium heat, combine the coconut milk, 300 ml water, spring onions, thyme, allspice and salt.
Bring to a gentle simmer, stirring once or twice, and cook for 5 minutes to infuse.
Stir in the kidney beans and simmer for 2 minutes more, until heated through.

stages.title: Cook the rice
steps: Add the rice to the pan and stir once to spread it evenly. Bring back to a simmer over medium heat.
Cover with a tight-fitting lid, reduce the heat to very low and cook for 15 minutes, until the liquid is absorbed and the rice is tender.
Turn off the heat and leave covered for 5 minutes to finish steaming.

stages.title: Fluff and serve
steps: Remove the lid and discard the thyme stems and spring onions.
Fluff the rice and beans gently with a fork, folding rather than stirring so the grains stay whole.
Taste and add a pinch more salt if needed, then serve hot.

tips: Rinsing the rice removes surface starch, so the grains cook up separate rather than gluey.
Keep the heat very low once the lid is on, because coconut milk scorches on the base of the pan easily.
Leave the lid on during cooking and resting, as the steam finishes cooking the rice evenly.
Use full-fat coconut milk for a richer, creamier flavour; light versions give a thinner result.
variations: Add 1 whole red chilli, pierced but left intact, with the thyme for gentle heat; remove it before serving.
Use 400 g cooked black beans in place of the kidney beans for a different flavour.
recipe.storage: Refrigerate in an airtight container within 1 hour of cooking and eat within 2 days. Reheat with a splash of water until steaming hot all the way through.

recipe.title: French Pear Belle Hélène
recipe.summary: Tender poached pears with warm dark chocolate sauce and vanilla ice cream.

stages.title: Make the poaching syrup
steps: Peel the pears, leaving the stems on, and slice a thin piece off each base so they stand upright.
Add 600 ml water, the white sugar and the vanilla extract to a medium saucepan just wide enough to hold the pears upright.
Stir over medium heat for 3–4 minutes until the sugar dissolves, then bring to a gentle simmer.

stages.title: Poach the pears
steps: Lower the pears into the syrup and reduce the heat to low so the surface barely bubbles.
Poach for 15–20 minutes, turning them occasionally, until a knife slides into the thickest part with no resistance.
Remove the pan from the heat and leave the pears to cool in the syrup for 20 minutes.

stages.title: Cool the pears
steps: Leave the pears in the syrup for 20 minutes off the heat, turning once, until just warm or at room temperature.
Lift the pears out with a slotted spoon and drain them on a plate, stem side up.

stages.title: Make the chocolate sauce
steps: Put the chopped dark chocolate in a heatproof bowl.
Heat the thickened cream in a small saucepan over medium heat for 2–3 minutes until steaming and small bubbles form at the edge, without boiling.
Pour the hot cream over the chocolate and leave for 1 minute, then stir until smooth and glossy.

stages.title: Assemble and serve
steps: Place a scoop of vanilla ice cream in each of 4 serving bowls.
Stand a drained pear beside or on top of each scoop.
Spoon the warm chocolate sauce over the pears and serve straight away.

tips: Firm, just-ripe pears hold their shape during poaching; soft ones turn grainy and collapse.
Keep the syrup at a bare simmer, as hard boiling breaks the pears apart before the centres soften.
Pour the cream over the chocolate off the heat so the sauce stays smooth and does not split or turn grainy.
Drain the pears well so syrup does not thin the chocolate sauce.
variations: Poach the pears in half water and half white wine for a more fragrant syrup.
Add a strip of orange zest to the syrup while poaching for a hint of citrus.
recipe.storage: Refrigerate pears in their syrup in an airtight container for up to 2 days. Store the sauce separately for up to 3 days and reheat gently in the microwave in short bursts, stirring between each, until pourable. Assemble with fresh ice cream just before serving.

recipe.title: Chinese Tomato Egg Stir Fry
recipe.summary: Soft scrambled eggs folded into juicy tomatoes with a lightly sweet, savoury sauce.
ingredients: 2 spring onions, thinly sliced, white and green parts separated

stages.title: Prepare the eggs and tomatoes
steps: Crack the eggs into a bowl, add 1/4 tsp of the salt and beat with a fork until no streaks of white remain.
Cut each tomato into 6–8 wedges, keeping them a similar size so they soften at the same rate.
Thinly slice the spring onions and keep the white and green parts in separate piles.

stages.title: Scramble the eggs
steps: Heat half the oil (1 tbsp) in a large frying pan or wok over medium-high heat until it shimmers.
Pour in the eggs and let them sit for 10 seconds, then push them gently from the edges to the centre for 1–2 minutes, until just set but still soft and slightly wet.
Tip the eggs onto a plate and wipe out the pan if any bits have stuck.

stages.title: Cook the tomatoes
steps: Return the pan to medium heat and add the remaining 1 tbsp oil and the white parts of the spring onions. Stir for 30 seconds until fragrant.
Add the tomatoes and the remaining 1/4 tsp salt. Cook, stirring often, for 3–4 minutes until the tomatoes release their juices and begin to collapse.
Stir in the sugar and soy sauce, then simmer for 2–3 minutes until the juices thicken slightly into a loose sauce.

stages.title: Combine and serve
steps: Return the eggs to the pan with any juices from the plate.
Fold gently over medium heat for 1 minute, until the eggs are heated through and coated in the sauce but still in large pieces.
Scatter over the green spring onion and serve straight away.

tips: Cooking the eggs first and removing them keeps them soft and fluffy, because they would turn rubbery if simmered in the tomato juices for long.
Ripe, soft tomatoes break down into a better sauce than firm ones. If yours are underripe, cook them an extra 2 minutes.
The small amount of sugar balances the acidity of the tomatoes rather than making the dish sweet, so don't skip it.
variations: For a richer sauce, stir 1 tbsp tomato paste in with the tomatoes and add 2 tbsp water if it gets too thick.
Add 1 clove of finely chopped garlic with the spring onion whites for a sharper savoury note.
recipe.storage: Refrigerate in an airtight container for up to 2 days. Reheat in a pan over medium heat until steaming hot throughout. The eggs will be firmer after reheating.

recipe.title: Mexican Arroz Rojo
recipe.summary: Fluffy tomato-red rice with onion, garlic and stock, a classic accompaniment to tacos.

stages.title: Blend the tomato sauce
steps: Put the tomatoes, half the onion and the garlic in a blender and blend until completely smooth.
Finely chop the remaining onion half and set aside.
Measure the rice into a bowl, rinse under cold running water until the water runs mostly clear, then drain very well.

stages.title: Toast the rice
steps: Heat the vegetable oil in a large deep frying pan with a lid over medium heat.
Add the drained rice and the chopped onion, and stir often for 6–8 minutes, until the rice is pale golden and smells nutty.
Keep the heat at medium so the rice colours evenly without scorching.

stages.title: Fry the sauce
steps: Pour the blended tomato mixture into the pan, stirring to coat the rice.
Cook over medium heat for 4–5 minutes, stirring, until the sauce thickens and the raw tomato smell fades.
Add the salt.

stages.title: Simmer and rest
steps: Pour in the chicken stock and stir once, then bring to a boil over medium-high heat.
Scatter the frozen peas over the top without stirring, cover with the lid and reduce the heat to low.
Cook for 15–18 minutes, until the liquid is absorbed and the rice is tender when you taste a grain.
Turn off the heat and rest covered for 5 minutes, then fluff with a fork and serve.

tips: Rinsing the rice removes surface starch, so the grains stay separate rather than gluey.
Toasting the rice in oil before adding liquid coats the grains, which helps them stay fluffy and gives a nutty flavour.
Frying the blended tomato until it thickens stops the rice turning out watery and sharpens the tomato flavour.
Resting the rice covered lets the steam finish cooking the top layer evenly.
variations: Add 1 tsp ground cumin and 1/2 tsp paprika with the tomato sauce for a smokier flavour.
Swap the chicken stock for vegetable stock to make it vegetarian, checking the stock label.
recipe.storage: Cool quickly and refrigerate in an airtight container for up to 2 days. Reheat until steaming hot throughout, adding a splash of water if dry.

recipe.title: Argentinian Chimichurri Steak
recipe.summary: Juicy grilled steak sliced against the grain and topped with punchy parsley, garlic and red-wine-vinegar chimichurri.
ingredients: 700 g beef steak, such as rump, about 3 cm thick
1 bunch parsley, leaves picked and finely chopped

stages.title: Make the chimichurri
steps: Combine the chopped parsley and garlic in a bowl with the red wine vinegar, 60 ml of the olive oil, the dried oregano, the chilli flakes and 1/2 tsp of the salt.
Stir well, then leave at room temperature for 20 minutes so the garlic mellows and the flavours blend.

stages.title: Season the steak
steps: Pat the steak dry with paper towel so it browns rather than steams.
Rub the steak all over with the remaining 1/2 tsp salt and the black pepper.
Leave the steak at room temperature for 15 minutes while the chimichurri sits.

stages.title: Cook the steak
steps: Heat a heavy frying pan or chargrill pan over high heat for 2–3 minutes until very hot, then add the remaining 1 tbsp olive oil.
Cook the steak for 4–5 minutes on one side without moving it, until deeply browned.
Turn and cook for another 3–4 minutes for medium-rare, until browned outside and still pink in the middle. Cook longer if you prefer it more done.

stages.title: Rest and serve
steps: Move the steak to a board and rest it, loosely covered with foil, for 10 minutes.
Slice the steak across the grain into 1 cm strips.
Spoon the chimichurri over the sliced steak and serve with the resting juices.

tips: Pat the steak dry before seasoning, because surface moisture stops a crust forming in the hot pan.
Resting the steak for 10 minutes lets the juices settle back into the meat, so they don't run out when you slice.
Chop the parsley by hand rather than blending it, as a food processor bruises the leaves and makes a muddy, pasty sauce.
Slicing across the grain shortens the muscle fibres, which makes rump tender to chew.
variations: Replace half the parsley with coriander for a brighter, more citrusy sauce.
Add 1 finely chopped red onion to the chimichurri for extra sharpness and crunch.
recipe.storage: Refrigerate the steak and chimichurri separately in airtight containers for up to 3 days. Eat the steak cold in sandwiches or salads, or reheat gently in a pan for 1–2 minutes so it doesn't overcook.

recipe.title: Filipino Chicken Inasal
recipe.summary: Chargrilled chicken marinated in calamansi-style citrus, vinegar, garlic and lemongrass with a golden annatto glaze.
ingredients: 1 lemongrass, white part only, bruised and finely chopped

stages.title: Make the marinade
steps: Pound the garlic and lemongrass with the salt to a rough paste using a mortar and pestle, or finely chop and crush with the flat of a knife.
Stir the paste with the lime juice, white vinegar, soy sauce and black pepper in a large bowl.
Add the chicken thighs and turn to coat well, working the marinade under the skin.

stages.title: Marinate
steps: Cover the bowl and refrigerate for 1 hour, turning the chicken once halfway.
Meanwhile, mix the paprika with the vegetable oil in a small bowl and set aside for basting.

stages.title: Cook the chicken
steps: Heat a barbecue grill plate or chargrill pan over medium heat and bring the chicken out of the fridge.
Cook the chicken skin side down for 12–15 minutes, until the skin is browned and releases easily.
Turn and cook for another 10–12 minutes, brushing with the paprika oil every few minutes, until the juices run clear and the thickest part reaches 75°C.

stages.title: Rest and serve
steps: Rest the chicken on a plate for 5 minutes, loosely covered.
Meanwhile, cook the rice according to the packet and serve it with the chicken and any pan juices.

tips: Bruising the lemongrass before chopping releases its oils, so the marinade tastes stronger.
Working the marinade under the skin seasons the meat directly, because the skin blocks the liquid.
Cooking skin side down first renders the fat slowly, giving crisp skin without burning.
Brush the paprika oil only in the later stages of cooking, since it can scorch over a long cook.
variations: Roast in a 220°C (200°C fan) oven on a rack over a tray for 35–40 minutes, until browned and cooked through, if you can't grill.
Add 1 tbsp of grated ginger to the marinade for a sharper, warmer flavour.
recipe.storage: Refrigerate in an airtight container for up to 3 days. Reheat in a 180°C (160°C fan) oven for 15 minutes, until steaming hot throughout.

recipe.title: Japanese Okonomiyaki
recipe.summary: Savoury cabbage pancakes with crisp edges, tender centres and a drizzle of tangy sauce and mayonnaise.
ingredients: 180 ml dashi stock, cooled (or 180 ml water)

stages.title: Prepare the vegetables and sauce
steps: Finely shred the cabbage and slice the spring onions, then pat both dry with paper towel.
Halve the bacon rashers crosswise.
Stir the barbecue sauce, soy sauce and tomato sauce together in a small bowl to make the okonomiyaki-style sauce.

stages.title: Make the batter
steps: Whisk the flour, baking powder and salt in a large bowl.
Add 2 of the eggs and the dashi and whisk until just smooth and thick, like a pancake batter.
Fold in the cabbage and spring onions until evenly coated. Beat the remaining egg and stir it through.

stages.title: Cook the pancakes
steps: Heat 1 tbsp of the oil in a large non-stick frypan over medium heat. Spoon in half the batter and shape into a round about 2 cm thick, without pressing it flat.
Lay 4 bacon pieces on top. Cook for 5–6 minutes until the base is deep golden brown.
Flip with a large spatula and cook for another 5–6 minutes until golden, the bacon is cooked and the centre is cooked through and firm when pressed.
Repeat with the remaining 1 tbsp oil, batter and bacon.

stages.title: Finish and serve
steps: Brush the top of each pancake with the sauce mixture.
Drizzle with the mayonnaise, cut each pancake into 4 wedges and serve hot.

tips: Keep the cabbage dry and shredded finely so the batter holds together and the pancake cooks through evenly.
Cooking over medium heat lets the thick centre set before the outside burns.
Leave the pancake unpressed when cooking, as squashing it makes it dense instead of fluffy.
variations: Replace the bacon with 150 g chopped raw prawns, laid on top and cooked until pink.
For a vegetarian version, omit the bacon and use water instead of dashi, and check the label on the barbecue sauce.
recipe.storage: Refrigerate in an airtight container for up to 3 days. Reheat in a frypan over medium heat for 2–3 minutes per side until piping hot.

recipe.title: Brazilian Moqueca
recipe.summary: Tender white fish gently poached in a fragrant coconut, tomato and pepper stew with lime and coriander.
ingredients: 650 g white fish fillets, cut into 4 cm chunks
1 bunch coriander, leaves and stems chopped

stages.title: Marinate the fish
steps: Place the fish in a bowl and add the lime juice and 1/2 tsp of the salt.
Toss gently to coat, then cover and refrigerate for 15 minutes.
Meanwhile, slice the onion and capsicum, chop the garlic and tomatoes, and chop the coriander.

stages.title: Cook the vegetable base
steps: Heat the olive oil in a large deep frying pan or wide saucepan over medium heat.
Add the onion and capsicum and cook, stirring occasionally, for 6–7 minutes until soft.
Add the garlic and cook for 30 seconds until fragrant.
Add the tomatoes, the remaining 1/2 tsp salt and a good grind of black pepper. Cook for 5 minutes until the tomatoes start to break down.

stages.title: Simmer the sauce
steps: Pour in the coconut milk and half the chopped coriander and stir well.
Bring to a gentle simmer over medium-low heat and cook for 8–10 minutes until slightly thickened.

stages.title: Poach the fish and serve
steps: Nestle the fish and its marinade juices into the sauce in a single layer, spooning some sauce over the top.
Cover and cook over low heat for 6–8 minutes until the fish is opaque and flakes easily.
Taste the sauce and add more salt or pepper if needed.
Scatter over the remaining coriander and serve straight from the pan.

tips: Cut the fish into large chunks so it holds together while poaching in the sauce.
Marinate the fish for no more than 15–20 minutes, as lime juice starts to turn the flesh firm and chalky.
Keep the heat low once the fish is in, because a hard boil breaks the fillets up and can split the coconut milk.
Use a firm fish such as barramundi, snapper or ling that won't fall apart.
variations: Add 300 g peeled raw prawns with the fish and cook until they turn pink and curl.
Stir 1 tbsp of tomato paste into the vegetables for a deeper, richer sauce.
recipe.storage: Refrigerate in an airtight container for up to 2 days. Reheat gently in a pan over low heat until steaming hot throughout. Not suitable for freezing.

recipe.title: Spanish Gambas al Ajillo
recipe.summary: Juicy prawns sizzle in garlic-infused olive oil with chilli, parsley and a squeeze of lemon.
ingredients: 500 g peeled prawns, tails left on if you like

stages.title: Prepare the prawns and garlic
steps: Pat the prawns very dry with paper towel, then toss them with the salt in a bowl.
Peel the garlic and slice it thinly so the slices cook evenly.
Finely chop the parsley and cut the lemon into wedges.
Slice the baguette so it is ready for mopping up the oil.

stages.title: Infuse the oil
steps: Pour the olive oil into a large frying pan or flameproof dish and add the garlic and dried chilli.
Heat over low-medium heat for 3–4 minutes, stirring now and then, until the garlic is fragrant and pale golden at the edges.
Take the pan off the heat briefly if the garlic starts to darken, as it turns bitter once browned.

stages.title: Cook the prawns
steps: Increase the heat to medium-high and add the prawns in a single layer.
Cook for 1–2 minutes, then turn and cook for another 1–2 minutes until the prawns are pink, curled and opaque all the way through.

stages.title: Finish and serve
steps: Remove the pan from the heat and scatter over the parsley.
Squeeze over the juice of half the lemon and serve straight away, sizzling, with the remaining lemon wedges and the baguette.

tips: Dry prawns sear and sizzle in the oil instead of steaming, which keeps them firm rather than watery.
Slicing the garlic rather than crushing it lets it flavour the oil without burning quickly.
Prawns overcook within minutes and turn rubbery, so pull the pan off the heat as soon as they are opaque.
variations: Add 1 tbsp dry sherry with the prawns and let it bubble for 30 seconds before serving.
Stir in 1 tsp smoked paprika with the garlic for a smokier oil.

recipe.title: Korean Gamja Jorim
recipe.summary: Tender baby potatoes glazed in a glossy sweet-salty soy sauce and finished with sesame seeds.
ingredients: 600 g baby potatoes, larger ones halved

stages.title: Prepare the potatoes
steps: Halve any potatoes larger than a golf ball so all pieces are a similar size.
Rinse the potatoes under cold water, then drain and pat dry with a clean tea towel so they brown rather than steam.

stages.title: Brown the potatoes
steps: Heat the vegetable oil in a large frying pan with a lid over medium-high heat.
Add the potatoes cut-side down and cook for 6–8 minutes, turning occasionally, until golden on the edges.

stages.title: Simmer until tender
steps: Reduce the heat to medium. Add 250 ml water, the soy sauce and the mirin, and stir to combine.
Cover and simmer for 12–15 minutes, stirring once or twice, until a knife slides easily into the largest potato.

stages.title: Glaze and serve
steps: Remove the lid, add the honey and increase the heat to medium-high.
Cook for 4–5 minutes, gently shaking the pan, until the liquid reduces to a sticky glaze that coats the potatoes.
Transfer to a serving dish, scatter with the sesame seeds and serve warm or at room temperature.

tips: Drying the potatoes after rinsing lets them brown in the oil, which gives the glaze a deeper flavour.
Add the honey only after the potatoes are tender, because it burns easily during a long simmer.
Shake the pan rather than stirring in the final stage so the softened potatoes stay whole and take on the glaze.
variations: Add 1 sliced red chilli with the water for gentle heat.
Use sweet potato cut into 3 cm chunks instead, simmering for about 10 minutes.
recipe.storage: Refrigerate in an airtight container for up to 3 days. Reheat in a pan over medium heat with a splash of water until steaming hot, or eat cold.

recipe.title: Moroccan Carrot Salad
recipe.summary: Tender carrots tossed with cumin, paprika, lemon, olive oil and fresh parsley.
ingredients: 600 g carrots, peeled and sliced into 5 mm coins

stages.title: Prepare the carrots and dressing
steps: Peel the carrots and slice them into 5 mm coins so they cook evenly.
Juice the lemon, crush the garlic and roughly chop the parsley.
In a large bowl, whisk the olive oil, lemon juice, garlic, ground cumin, paprika and salt until combined.

stages.title: Cook the carrots
steps: Bring a medium saucepan of water to the boil over high heat and add a pinch of salt from the 1/2 tsp.
Add the carrots, reduce the heat to medium and simmer for 6–8 minutes, until just tender when pierced with a knife but still holding their shape.
Drain well in a colander and let the steam escape for 1 minute.

stages.title: Dress the carrots
steps: Add the warm carrots to the dressing and toss to coat.
Gently press a few coins with the back of a spoon so they take up more dressing.
Stir through the parsley.

stages.title: Marinate and serve
steps: Leave the salad to stand at room temperature for 30 minutes, tossing once halfway, so the carrots absorb the dressing.
Taste and add a little more lemon juice or salt if needed, then serve at room temperature or chilled.

tips: Dress the carrots while they are still warm, as warm carrots absorb the garlic, cumin and lemon far better than cold ones.
Stop simmering while the carrots still have a slight bite, because they keep softening in the warm dressing.
Slice the coins to an even thickness so they all finish cooking at the same time.
variations: Add 1 tsp chilli flakes to the dressing for a spicy version.
Stir through 1/4 cup sultanas with the carrots for a sweeter salad.
recipe.storage: Refrigerate in an airtight container for up to 3 days. Serve chilled or bring to room temperature for 20 minutes before serving.

recipe.title: Turkish Cilbir
recipe.summary: Silky poached eggs over garlicky yoghurt with warm paprika butter and fresh dill.

stages.title: Make the garlic yoghurt
steps: Take the yoghurt out of the fridge and let it sit on the bench while you prepare the rest, so it is not cold when served.
Finely grate the garlic and stir it into the yoghurt with the salt.
Spread the yoghurt over four shallow bowls or plates, leaving a slight hollow in the centre of each.

stages.title: Poach the eggs
steps: Half-fill a wide saucepan with water, add the vinegar and bring to a gentle simmer over medium-low heat, with only small bubbles rising.
Crack each egg into a small cup, then slide the eggs one at a time into the water.
Cook for 3 minutes, until the whites are set and the yolks are runny, or 4–5 minutes until cooked through if you prefer.
Lift the eggs out with a slotted spoon and rest them on paper towel for 30 seconds to drain.

stages.title: Make the paprika butter
steps: Melt the butter in a small saucepan over medium-low heat, about 1 minute.
Stir in the paprika and chilli flakes and cook for 30–60 seconds, until the butter is deep red and fragrant.
Remove the pan from the heat straight away so the paprika does not burn and turn bitter.

stages.title: Assemble and serve
steps: Place a drained egg or two on the garlic yoghurt in each bowl.
Spoon the warm paprika butter over the eggs and yoghurt.
Scatter with the dill and serve with the bread, toasted if you like, for scooping.

tips: Room-temperature yoghurt stops the warm eggs and butter from cooling off quickly and keeps the dish pleasantly lukewarm.
Keep the poaching water at a bare simmer, because a rolling boil tears the whites and scatters the egg.
Take the paprika butter off the heat as soon as it turns red, since paprika scorches quickly and tastes bitter.
Draining the eggs briefly on paper towel keeps water from thinning the yoghurt.
variations: Replace the paprika and chilli flakes with 1 tsp sumac in the butter for a tangier finish.
Stir 1 tbsp chopped mint into the yoghurt along with the garlic for a fresher flavour.
recipe.storage: Best eaten straight away. The garlic yoghurt keeps covered in the fridge for up to 2 days, but poached eggs and paprika butter should be made fresh.

recipe.title: Turkish Simit
recipe.summary: Chewy sesame-crusted bread rings with a golden exterior, perfect with cheese, olives or tea.

stages.title: Make the dough
steps: In a large bowl, combine the plain flour, dried yeast, white sugar and salt.
Add 280 ml warm water and the olive oil, then stir until a shaggy dough forms.
Knead on a lightly floured bench for 8–10 minutes, until smooth and elastic and the dough springs back when pressed.

stages.title: Prove the dough
steps: Place the dough in a lightly oiled bowl and cover with a clean tea towel.
Leave in a warm spot for about 60 minutes, until doubled in size.

stages.title: Prepare the coating and tray
steps: Heat the oven to 220°C (200°C fan) and line two large baking trays with baking paper.
Whisk the honey with 100 ml water in a wide shallow bowl.
Spread the sesame seeds in a second wide shallow dish.
Tip the risen dough onto the bench and divide it into 8 equal pieces.

stages.title: Shape the rings
steps: Roll each piece into a rope about 60 cm long, using your palms and a little flour only if sticking.
Fold each rope in half and twist the two halves together into a single rope.
Pinch the ends together to form a ring, pressing firmly so it doesn't open during baking.
Dip each ring in the honey mixture, let the excess drip off, then press into the sesame seeds to coat both sides.

stages.title: Bake the simit
steps: Arrange the rings on the trays, spaced about 4 cm apart.
Bake for 18–20 minutes, swapping the trays halfway, until deep golden brown and the base sounds hollow when tapped.
Cool on a wire rack for 10 minutes before serving.

tips: Dipping in a honey and water mix gives the crust its glossy, deep golden colour, since the sugars brown quickly in a hot oven.
Pinch the ring join firmly and twist the rope tightly so the rings hold their shape and don't unravel as the dough expands.
Toast the sesame seeds in a dry frying pan over medium heat for 2–3 minutes before coating for a nuttier flavour, but cool them first.
variations: Traditional Turkish simit uses grape molasses (pekmez) in place of honey; use 3 tbsp diluted in the same way if you can find it.
Serve with sliced tomatoes, cucumber and feta for a Turkish-style breakfast.
recipe.storage: Best eaten the day they are baked. Store cooled simit in an airtight container for up to 2 days, or freeze for up to 1 month. Reheat in a 180°C (160°C fan) oven for 5–8 minutes until crisp.

recipe.title: Middle Eastern Mujadara
recipe.summary: Earthy lentils and rice topped with deeply caramelised onions, served with lemony yoghurt.

stages.title: Cook the lentils
steps: Rinse the brown lentils and place them in a medium saucepan with 750 ml water.
Bring to the boil over high heat, then reduce to medium-low and simmer for 18–20 minutes, until the lentils are almost tender but still holding their shape.
Drain the lentils in a sieve, reserving 400 ml of the cooking water in a jug.

stages.title: Brown the onions
steps: Heat 2 tbsp of the olive oil in a large frying pan over medium heat.
Add the sliced onions and 1/2 tsp of the salt, and cook, stirring every few minutes, for 25 minutes until deep golden brown and sweet.
Lift out about half the onions onto a plate for topping, leaving the rest in the pan.

stages.title: Cook the rice with the lentils
steps: Rinse the rice under cold water until the water runs mostly clear.
Add the remaining 1 tbsp olive oil and the ground cumin to the onions in the pan, and stir over medium heat for 30 seconds until fragrant.
Add the drained lentils, the rice, the remaining 1/2 tsp salt and the reserved 400 ml cooking water, and stir once.
Bring to the boil, then cover tightly, reduce to the lowest heat and cook for 15 minutes until the liquid is absorbed and the rice is tender.
Remove from the heat and rest, covered, for 5 minutes.

stages.title: Make the lemon yoghurt and serve
steps: Stir the greek yoghurt with the lemon zest, 1 tbsp of the lemon juice and a pinch of black pepper.
Fluff the mujadara with a fork and season with black pepper and extra lemon juice to taste.
Top with the reserved onions and serve with the lemon yoghurt.

tips: Rinsing the rice removes surface starch, so the grains stay separate instead of turning gluey.
Cooking the onions slowly over medium heat caramelises their sugars; turning the heat up makes them bitter before they colour.
Reserving the lentil cooking water adds earthy flavour to the rice that plain water would not.
variations: Stir 1/2 tsp ground cinnamon through with the cumin for a warmer, Lebanese-style flavour.
Replace the rice with 200 g bulgur and reduce the cooking time to about 10 minutes, until the bulgur is tender.
recipe.storage: Refrigerate the mujadara and yoghurt separately in airtight containers for up to 3 days. Reheat the mujadara with a splash of water until steaming hot.

recipe.title: Japanese Dorayaki
recipe.summary: Fluffy golden pancake sandwiches filled with sweet red bean paste, a classic Japanese treat.

stages.title: Make the batter
steps: Whisk the eggs, caster sugar and honey in a large bowl for 2–3 minutes until pale, thick and slightly foamy.
Add the water and whisk until the honey has dissolved.
Sift the plain flour and baking powder over the egg mixture and fold gently until just smooth, with no dry flour left.
The batter should fall from the whisk in a thick ribbon; if it is stiff, add 1 tbsp more water.

stages.title: Rest the batter
steps: Cover the bowl and rest the batter for 20 minutes so the flour hydrates and the pancakes cook up tender.
Meanwhile, divide the red bean paste into 4 portions and loosely shape each into a flat disc about 6 cm wide.

stages.title: Cook the pancakes
steps: Heat a large non-stick frying pan over low–medium heat for 2 minutes. Wipe it with a little of the vegetable oil on a paper towel, leaving only a thin film.
Pour 3 tbsp batter into the pan to form a round about 8 cm wide. Cook 3 at a time for 2–3 minutes, until bubbles form on the surface and the edges look set.
Flip and cook for 1 minute more, until the underside is golden and the pancake springs back when pressed. Transfer to a wire rack.
Repeat with the remaining batter to make 8 pancakes, re-oiling the pan lightly between batches and adjusting the heat if they colour too quickly.

stages.title: Fill and serve
steps: Let the pancakes cool for 3–4 minutes so the bean paste doesn't melt.
Spread a portion of red bean paste over the paler side of a pancake, leaving a 1 cm border.
Top with a second pancake, golden side up, and press the edges gently together. Repeat to make 4 dorayaki.

tips: Resting the batter lets the flour absorb the liquid, giving a softer, more even crumb.
Low–medium heat gives an evenly golden surface; a hotter pan browns the outside before the centre cooks.
Cooking the pancakes in a thin film of oil, wiped almost dry, gives the smooth tan finish dorayaki are known for.
variations: Fill with sweetened chestnut paste instead of red bean paste.
Spread the pancakes with a thin layer of lightly whipped cream before adding the bean paste.
recipe.storage: Wrap each dorayaki in plastic wrap and refrigerate for up to 3 days. Bring to room temperature or warm for 10 seconds in the microwave before eating.

recipe.title: Italian Zabaglione
recipe.summary: Light, foamy egg-yolk custard whisked over gentle heat with sugar and sweet Marsala wine.

stages.title: Prepare the berries and water bath
steps: Divide the strawberries among 4 serving glasses.
Pour 250 ml water into a medium saucepan and bring to a gentle simmer over medium-low heat, so the water sits well below the base of a heatproof bowl set on top.
Place the egg yolks and caster sugar in a large heatproof bowl.

stages.title: Whisk the base
steps: Whisk the egg yolks and sugar with a balloon whisk for 2–3 minutes, until pale and slightly thickened.
Whisk in the marsala until combined. Use pasteurised eggs if serving young children, pregnant or elderly people.

stages.title: Cook over the water
steps: Set the bowl over the barely simmering water, making sure the base does not touch the water.
Whisk constantly and vigorously for 8–10 minutes, until the mixture triples in volume, is thick, foamy and warm, and leaves a ribbon trail on the surface for a few seconds.
If the edges start to look scrambled, lift the bowl off the heat and whisk hard for 10 seconds before returning it.

stages.title: Serve
steps: Lift the bowl off the pan as soon as the zabaglione is thick and airy.
Spoon it over the strawberries in the glasses and serve straight away while warm.

tips: Keep the water at a bare simmer, because direct or fierce heat cooks the yolks into scrambled egg before they build volume.
Whisk right into the curve of the bowl, as yolks catch and set first at the edges.
Cooking until the mixture holds a ribbon trail gives a stable foam that stays airy when spooned over fruit.
variations: Swap the strawberries for blueberries or sliced poached pears.
Use sweet white wine or sweet sherry in place of the marsala for a lighter flavour.

recipe.title: Indian Gulab Jamun
recipe.summary: Soft milk-solid dumplings soaked in fragrant cardamom and rose syrup until tender and glossy.

stages.title: Make the syrup
steps: Lightly crush the cardamom pods with the flat of a knife.
Combine the white sugar, 300 ml water and the cardamom in a medium saucepan over medium heat, stirring until the sugar dissolves.
Simmer over medium heat for 6–8 minutes, until the syrup is slightly sticky but still runs freely from a spoon.
Stir in the rosewater, then turn the heat to the lowest setting to keep the syrup warm.

stages.title: Make the dough
steps: Whisk the milk powder, plain flour and baking powder in a large bowl until evenly combined.
Rub the butter into the dry ingredients with your fingertips until the mixture looks like fine crumbs.
Add the milk 1 tablespoon at a time, bringing the mixture together gently into a soft, slightly tacky dough.
Rest the dough, covered, for 10 minutes so the milk powder hydrates.

stages.title: Shape the balls
steps: Lightly grease your palms with a little of the vegetable oil.
Divide the dough into 16 equal pieces.
Roll each piece between your palms into a smooth ball with no cracks, as cracks open up when frying.

stages.title: Fry the gulab jamun
steps: Heat the vegetable oil in a deep, heavy-based saucepan over low-medium heat until it reaches about 140°C, or until a small piece of dough sinks and rises slowly with gentle bubbles.
Fry 5–6 balls at a time, gently swirling the oil around them, for 8–10 minutes, until deep golden brown all over and puffed.
Test one ball: it should feel light and firm, and a skewer pushed into the centre should come out clean with no raw dough.
Lift the balls out with a slotted spoon and drain on paper towel for 30 seconds. Repeat with the remaining balls.

stages.title: Soak in syrup
steps: Make sure the syrup is warm, not boiling hot, then add the fried balls to it.
Leave the balls to soak off the heat for at least 30 minutes, until they swell and are soft right through.
Serve 4 balls per person, warm or at room temperature, with some syrup spooned over.

tips: Keep the oil at about 140°C so the centres cook through before the outsides darken; hotter oil gives a dark shell and a raw middle.
Add the milk gradually, as milk powder brands absorb differently. A dough that is too wet spreads and splits when frying.
Add the balls to warm syrup, not hot syrup, so they absorb it evenly instead of shrinking and going tough.
Knead the dough only until it comes together; overworking makes the gulab jamun dense and chewy.
variations: Press a flaked almond or a few pistachio slivers into the centre of each ball before rolling.
Replace the rosewater with a pinch of saffron threads steeped in the warm syrup.
recipe.storage: Refrigerate in the syrup in an airtight container for up to 5 days. Warm gently in the microwave in 20-second bursts, or serve cold.

recipe.title: Mexican Arroz con Leche
recipe.summary: Creamy cinnamon-scented rice pudding simmered with milk, vanilla and a little condensed milk.
ingredients: 1 orange, zest removed in 2 wide strips

stages.title: Prepare the rice and flavourings
steps: Rinse the rice in a sieve under cold running water until the water runs mostly clear, then drain well.
Peel 2 wide strips of zest from the orange with a vegetable peeler, avoiding the white pith.
Measure the milk, condensed milk and vanilla extract so they are ready beside the stove.

stages.title: Cook the rice in water
steps: Put the 250 ml water, cinnamon stick and salt in a medium heavy-based saucepan and bring to the boil over medium-high heat, about 3–4 minutes.
Stir in the rinsed rice and return to a simmer, then reduce the heat to low and cover.
Cook for 15 minutes, stirring once or twice, until the water is almost fully absorbed and the rice is nearly tender.

stages.title: Simmer the rice in milk
steps: Pour in the milk, add the orange zest strips and bring to a gentle simmer over medium heat, stirring.

Reduce the heat to medium-low and cook uncovered for about 20 minutes, stirring every 2–3 minutes and scraping the base, until the rice is tender and the mixture is creamy and thick enough to coat a spoon.

stages.title: Sweeten, rest and serve
steps: Stir in the condensed milk and vanilla extract and simmer over low heat for 5 minutes, stirring constantly, until the pudding is glossy and slightly looser than you want it to be at the table.
Remove the cinnamon stick and orange zest strips and take the pan off the heat.
Rest for 10 minutes, during which the pudding will thicken, then spoon into bowls and dust with the ground cinnamon. Serve warm or chilled.

tips: Rinsing the rice removes surface starch, so the grains stay distinct while the pudding still turns creamy from the starch released during cooking.
Cooking the rice in water first softens it without the milk catching on the base, so the milk stage only has to thicken.
Stop cooking while the pudding is still a little loose, because the rice keeps absorbing liquid as it rests and cools.
Stir often and scrape the base in the milk stage, as milk sugars scorch easily and a burnt layer will taint the whole pot.
variations: Stir in 1/3 cup sultanas with the condensed milk so they plump in the final simmer.
Swap the orange zest for a strip of lime zest for a sharper, more floral flavour.
recipe.storage: Refrigerate in an airtight container for up to 3 days. The pudding firms up when cold, so stir in a splash of milk when reheating gently in a saucepan over low heat until hot, or serve it chilled.

recipe.title: Turkish Sutlac
recipe.summary: Creamy baked rice pudding with a delicate vanilla aroma and lightly caramelised tops.

stages.title: Prepare the rice and slurry
steps: Rinse the arborio rice in a sieve under cold running water for 1 minute, until the water runs mostly clear, then drain.
Whisk the cornflour with 100 ml of the milk in a small jug until smooth, and set aside.
Measure the caster sugar and vanilla extract and leave them next to the stove.
Set four 250 ml heatproof ramekins on a baking tray.

stages.title: Cook the rice
steps: Put the rinsed rice and 250 ml water in a medium saucepan and bring to the boil over medium-high heat.
Reduce the heat to medium-low, cover and simmer for 10–12 minutes, until the rice is tender and almost all the water has been absorbed.
Stir once or twice during cooking so the rice does not stick.

stages.title: Simmer in the milk
steps: Pour the remaining 800 ml milk into the rice and bring to a gentle simmer over medium heat, stirring often.
Add the caster sugar and stir until dissolved.
Cook over medium-low heat for 20–25 minutes, stirring every couple of minutes and scraping the base, until the rice is very soft and the mixture has thickened slightly.

stages.title: Thicken
steps: Stir the cornflour mixture again, then pour it into the pan while stirring.
Cook over medium heat for 3–4 minutes, stirring constantly, until the pudding is thick and coats the back of a spoon.
Take the pan off the heat and stir in the vanilla extract.
Divide the pudding evenly among the ramekins.

stages.title: Grill the tops
steps: Heat the grill to high and position the rack about 10 cm from the element.
Grill the ramekins for 3–5 minutes, watching closely, until the tops are speckled with golden-brown patches.
Carefully remove the tray from the grill.

stages.title: Cool and chill
steps: Leave the puddings on the bench for 30 minutes to cool to room temperature.
Refrigerate for at least 2½ hours, until completely cold and set, then serve.

tips: Rinsing the rice removes surface starch, so the grains stay distinct while the milk still turns creamy.
Cooking the rice in water first softens it fully before the milk goes in, which prevents the milk from catching and reducing too far.
Scraping the base of the pan while stirring stops the sugary milk from sticking and scorching.
The pudding thickens a lot as it chills, so stop cooking while it is still slightly looser than you want it.
variations: Dust the chilled puddings with ground cinnamon just before serving.
Stir 1 tbsp of finely chopped pistachios or walnuts over each serve for crunch.
recipe.storage: Cover and refrigerate for up to 3 days. Serve cold; the puddings are not suited to freezing.

recipe.title: Sri Lankan Dhal Curry
recipe.summary: Golden red lentils simmered in coconut milk with curry leaves, turmeric and toasted mustard seeds.
ingredients: 2 onions, 1 finely sliced and 1 finely chopped
2 green chillies, 1 slit lengthways and 1 finely chopped

stages.title: Rinse and prepare
steps: Rinse the red lentils in a sieve under cold running water until the water runs almost clear, then drain.
Finely slice 1 onion and finely chop the other onion.
Slit 1 green chilli lengthways and finely chop the second one.
Finely chop the garlic and cut the lime into wedges.

stages.title: Simmer the lentils
steps: Put the lentils, chopped onion, slit chilli, garlic, turmeric, half the curry leaves (6 leaves) and 750 ml water in a medium saucepan.
Bring to the boil over high heat, skimming off any foam.
Reduce to medium-low heat and simmer, stirring occasionally, for 15–18 minutes until the lentils are soft and falling apart.
Stir in the salt.

stages.title: Add the coconut milk
steps: Pour in the coconut milk and stir well.
Warm over low heat for 4–5 minutes, stirring, until hot and creamy; do not let it boil hard.
Add a splash of water if the dhal is thicker than a loose porridge.

stages.title: Temper and serve
steps: Heat the oil in a small frying pan over medium heat for 1 minute.
Add the mustard seeds and cook for 30–60 seconds until they pop.
Add the sliced onion and chopped chilli and cook, stirring, for 4–5 minutes until golden.
Add the remaining 6 curry leaves and cook for 30 seconds until crisp and fragrant.
Pour the tempering over the dhal, stir through lightly and serve with lime wedges.

tips: Rinsing the lentils removes surface starch, so the dhal cooks with less foam and a cleaner flavour.
Adding coconut milk after the lentils are soft stops it splitting and keeps the dhal creamy.
Fry the curry leaves last and briefly, as they turn bitter if they brown too much.
Salt added once the lentils are soft prevents the skins from toughening.
variations: Stir 100 g baby spinach through with the coconut milk and cook for 2 minutes until wilted.
Add 1 tsp chilli flakes to the tempering oil for a hotter dhal.
recipe.storage: Refrigerate in an airtight container for up to 3 days or freeze for up to 2 months. Reheat in a saucepan over low heat with a splash of water until steaming hot.

recipe.title: Georgian Lobio
recipe.summary: Creamy red beans stewed with walnuts, coriander and garlic, served with crusty bread.
ingredients: 600 g cooked kidney beans, drained and rinsed

stages.title: Prepare the aromatics and walnuts
steps: Finely dice the onion and crush the garlic, keeping the garlic in a small bowl.
Toast the walnuts in a dry frying pan over medium heat for 4–5 minutes, shaking the pan often, until fragrant and lightly browned.
Tip the walnuts onto a board, cool for a few minutes, then chop them very finely or pound them to a coarse paste.
Drain and rinse the kidney beans and leave them in a colander.

stages.title: Soften the onion
steps: Heat the olive oil in a medium saucepan over medium-low heat.
Add the onion and 1/4 tsp of the salt and cook for 12–15 minutes, stirring often, until soft and golden.
Stir in half the garlic and the ground coriander and cook for 1 minute until fragrant.

stages.title: Simmer the beans
steps: Add the kidney beans and 250 ml water to the pan and bring to the boil over medium-high heat.
Reduce the heat to low, partly cover and simmer for 30 minutes, stirring now and then, until the beans are very tender and the liquid has thickened.
About 20 minutes in, mash roughly a third of the beans against the side of the pan with a wooden spoon so the stew turns creamy.
If the stew looks dry at any point, add 60 ml water and stir.

stages.title: Add the walnuts and rest
steps: Stir in the chopped walnuts, the remaining garlic and the remaining 1/2 tsp salt.
Simmer over low heat for 5 minutes, stirring, until thick and spoonable.
Season with black pepper, take off the heat and rest for 5 minutes before serving warm.

tips: Mashing a third of the beans releases their starch, which thickens the stew without flour or cream.
Adding half the garlic early and half at the end gives both a mellow base and a sharp, fresh finish.
Toasting the walnuts first brings out their oils and stops the stew tasting raw and bitter.
Cooking the onion slowly until golden builds sweetness that balances the earthy beans.
variations: Stir in 1 tbsp red wine vinegar with the walnuts for a tangy finish, and serve with a sprinkle of chopped coriander.
Add 1/2 tsp chilli flakes with the ground coriander for a spicier lobio.
recipe.storage: Refrigerate in an airtight container for up to 3 days. Reheat gently in a saucepan over low heat with a splash of water until steaming hot. It also freezes well for up to 2 months.

recipe.title: Greek Galaktoboureko
recipe.summary: Crisp buttered filo pastry enclosing creamy semolina custard, soaked in fragrant lemon syrup.

stages.title: Prepare the pan, butter and lemon
steps: Heat the oven to 180°C (160°C fan).
Melt the butter and use a little to grease a 20 x 25 cm baking dish.
Remove the zest from the lemon in wide strips with a vegetable peeler, then juice the lemon.
Cover the filo sheets with a damp tea towel so they don't dry out.

stages.title: Cook the custard
steps: Combine the milk, semolina and 75 g of the sugar in a medium saucepan.
Cook over medium heat, whisking constantly, for 8–10 minutes until the mixture is thick and coats the back of a spoon.
Remove from the heat, stir in the vanilla extract and cool for 5 minutes.
Whisk in the eggs until smooth.

stages.title: Assemble the pie
steps: Lay 5 filo sheets in the dish one at a time, brushing each with melted butter and letting the edges overhang.
Pour in the custard and spread it evenly.
Fold the overhanging filo over the custard, then layer the remaining 5 sheets on top, brushing each with melted butter.
Tuck in the edges, brush the top with the remaining butter and score the top layers into squares with a sharp knife, cutting only through the filo.

stages.title: Bake and make the syrup
steps: Bake for 35–40 minutes until the pastry is deep golden and the custard is set with only a slight wobble in the centre.
While it bakes, combine the water, the remaining 75 g sugar, the lemon zest strips and 1 tbsp of the lemon juice in a small saucepan.
Simmer over medium heat for 8 minutes until slightly syrupy, then remove the zest and leave to cool to room temperature.

stages.title: Soak and rest
steps: Pour the cooled syrup evenly over the pastry as soon as it comes out of the oven.
Rest for at least 30 minutes so the syrup soaks in and the custard firms up.
Cut along the scored lines and serve warm or at room temperature.

tips: Pour cool syrup over hot pastry so the filo stays crisp instead of turning soggy.
Whisk the semolina constantly as it heats so it doesn't form lumps and the custard stays smooth.
Let the custard cool for 5 minutes before adding the eggs, or they may scramble.
Scoring the top before baking lets you cut neat portions without shattering the crisp filo.
variations: Replace the lemon zest in the syrup with strips of orange zest and add a pinch of ground cinnamon to the custard.
Add a cinnamon stick to the syrup for a spiced finish.
recipe.storage: Refrigerate, covered, for up to 3 days. Bring to room temperature before serving, or warm at 150°C for 10 minutes; the filo will soften.

recipe.title: Greek Lemon Chicken Orzo
recipe.summary: Tender chicken and orzo simmered in lemony broth with oregano, spinach and a silky finish.
ingredients: 600 g chicken thigh, boneless and skinless

stages.title: Prepare the chicken and aromatics
steps: Finely zest the lemon, then juice it, keeping the zest and juice separate.
Finely dice the onion and crush the garlic.
Trim any excess fat from the chicken thighs and pat them dry with paper towel.
Toss the chicken with the oregano, 1/2 tsp of the salt and the black pepper.

stages.title: Brown the chicken
steps: Heat 1 tbsp of the olive oil in a large deep frying pan with a lid over medium-high heat.
Add the chicken and cook for 4–5 minutes per side, until deeply golden. It will not be cooked through yet.
Transfer the chicken to a plate.

stages.title: Cook the orzo
steps: Reduce the heat to medium and add the remaining 1 tbsp olive oil to the same pan, then cook the onion for 4 minutes, until soft and translucent.
Add the garlic and lemon zest and stir for 30 seconds, until fragrant.
Add the orzo and stir for 1 minute to coat it in the oil.
Pour in the chicken stock and the remaining 1/4 tsp salt, scraping up the browned bits from the base of the pan, and bring to a simmer.

Nestle the chicken back into the pan along with any juices on the plate, cover and cook over medium-low heat for 12–14 minutes, stirring the orzo gently once or twice, until the orzo is tender and the chicken is cooked through with no pink in the centre.

stages.title: Finish and rest
steps: Move the chicken to a board and rest it for 5 minutes.
Stir the baby spinach and the lemon juice through the orzo over low heat for 1–2 minutes, until the spinach wilts and the orzo is creamy and saucy.
Slice the chicken, return it to the pan or serve it on top, and taste for salt and pepper.

tips: Browning the chicken first builds a savoury base in the pan, which flavours the stock the orzo absorbs.
Add the lemon juice at the end because long cooking dulls its brightness and can turn it bitter.
Stir the orzo only gently and rarely, as constant stirring releases starch and can make it gluey rather than creamy.
Resting the chicken keeps the juices in the meat so slices stay moist.
variations: Stir through 100 g crumbled feta and a handful of chopped dill just before serving.
Add 1 cup of halved kalamata olives with the spinach for a saltier, more briny finish.
recipe.storage: Refrigerate in an airtight container for up to 3 days. The orzo will thicken, so reheat with a splash of water or stock until steaming hot throughout. Not suitable to freeze.

recipe.title: Indonesian Soto Ayam
recipe.summary: Golden turmeric chicken soup with rice noodles, cabbage, lime and crisp fried shallots.
ingredients: 1 stalk lemongrass, bruised with the back of a knife

stages.title: Prepare the aromatics and toppings
steps: Crush the garlic, finely grate the ginger and bruise the lemongrass.
Finely shred the cabbage and thinly slice the spring onions.
Cut the limes into wedges and set aside with the cabbage and spring onions for serving.

stages.title: Fry the aromatics
steps: Heat the vegetable oil in a large pot over medium heat.
Add the garlic, ginger and lemongrass and cook, stirring, for 1–2 minutes until fragrant.
Stir in the ground turmeric and cook for 30 seconds until the oil turns golden.

stages.title: Simmer the chicken
steps: Add the chicken stock, 750 ml water and the salt, then bring to the boil over high heat.
Add the chicken thigh and reduce the heat to low so the broth barely bubbles.
Simmer, partly covered, for 25–30 minutes until the chicken is cooked through, no longer pink and tender when pulled with a fork.
Lift the chicken out onto a board and discard the lemongrass from the broth. Keep the broth hot over low heat.

stages.title: Shred the chicken and cook the noodles
steps: Shred the chicken into bite-sized pieces using two forks.
Cook the rice vermicelli according to the packet in a separate pot of boiling water, then drain and rinse under warm water to stop sticking.
Add the shredded cabbage to the hot broth and simmer over medium heat for 1 minute until just wilted.

stages.title: Assemble and serve
steps: Divide the vermicelli among four bowls and top with the shredded chicken.
Ladle over the hot broth and cabbage.
Scatter with the spring onions and serve with the lime wedges to squeeze over.

tips: Cooking the noodles separately keeps the broth clear and stops the noodles swelling and going soft.
Chicken thigh stays juicy during a gentle simmer, while a hard boil toughens it and clouds the broth.
Frying the turmeric briefly in oil removes its raw taste and gives the broth a deeper colour.
Salt the broth at the start, then taste before serving, as stocks vary in saltiness.
variations: Top each bowl with a boiled egg, cooked for 8 minutes then peeled and halved.
Serve with sambal or sliced red chilli on the side for heat.
recipe.storage: Refrigerate the broth, chicken and noodles in separate airtight containers for up to 3 days. Reheat the broth and chicken until steaming hot, and pour over the noodles.

recipe.title: Cuban Ropa Vieja
recipe.summary: Slow-braised shredded beef with sweet peppers, tomato, cumin and olives.
ingredients: 800 g beef chuck steak, in 3–4 large chunks
80 g kalamata olives, pitted and halved

stages.title: Prepare and season
steps: Pat the beef chunks dry with paper towels.
Season the beef all over with the salt and black pepper.
Thinly slice the onion and capsicums, and finely chop the garlic.

stages.title: Brown the beef
steps: Heat the olive oil in a large heavy-based pot over medium-high heat.
Brown the beef for 3–4 minutes per side, until deeply golden all over.
Transfer the beef to a plate, leaving the oil and browned bits in the pot.

stages.title: Build the sauce
steps: Reduce the heat to medium and add the onion and capsicums to the pot. Cook, stirring, for 6–7 minutes until softened.
Stir in the garlic, ground cumin, dried oregano and tomato paste and cook for 1 minute until fragrant.
Add the canned tomatoes, beef stock and bay leaves, then stir, scraping up the browned bits from the base of the pot.

stages.title: Braise until tender
steps: Return the beef and any resting juices to the pot and bring to a gentle simmer over medium heat.
Cover, reduce the heat to low and cook for 2 hours, turning the beef once halfway, until it shreds easily with a fork.
Remove the pot from the heat and discard the bay leaves.

stages.title: Shred and finish
steps: Lift the beef onto a board and shred it with two forks, discarding any large pieces of fat.
Return the shredded beef to the pot with the olives and red wine vinegar.
Simmer uncovered over medium heat for 10–15 minutes, stirring occasionally, until the sauce is thick and clings to the meat.
Taste, add a little more salt if needed, then stir through half the coriander and scatter the rest on top to serve.

tips: Chuck steak has plenty of connective tissue, which melts during a long, gentle braise and makes the shredded beef moist rather than dry.
Browning the beef well before braising builds a deeper, savoury base for the sauce.
Add the red wine vinegar at the end because it keeps its brightness and balances the richness of the beef.
Simmering uncovered at the end thickens the sauce so it coats the beef instead of pooling on the plate.
variations: Swap the olives for 2 tbsp drained capers for a sharper, saltier finish.
Use a pressure cooker or slow cooker after browning: about 1 hour on high pressure, or 8 hours on low.
recipe.storage: Refrigerate in an airtight container for up to 3 days or freeze for up to 3 months. Reheat in a pan over medium heat with a splash of water until steaming hot.

recipe.title: Syrian Muhammara
recipe.summary: Smoky roasted red pepper and walnut dip sharpened with pomegranate molasses.

stages.title: Roast the capsicums
steps: Heat the oven to 220°C (200°C fan) and line a baking tray with baking paper.
Place the whole capsicums on the tray and roast for 30–35 minutes, turning once, until the skins are blistered and blackened in patches and the flesh is soft and collapsing.
Transfer the hot capsicums to a bowl and cover tightly with a plate or plastic wrap to trap the steam.

stages.title: Toast the walnuts and peel the capsicums
steps: Reduce the oven to 180°C (160°C fan). Spread the walnuts on a clean tray and toast for 6–8 minutes, until fragrant and a shade darker, then cool for 10 minutes.
After the capsicums have steamed for at least 15 minutes, peel off the skins and discard the stems and seeds.
Drain the peeled capsicum flesh in a sieve for 5 minutes so the dip isn't watery.

stages.title: Blend the muhammara
steps: Add the walnuts and breadcrumbs to a food processor and pulse until coarsely ground.
Add the capsicum flesh, pomegranate molasses, garlic, salt, chilli flakes, cumin and lemon juice.
Blend until thick and spreadable but still slightly textured, scraping down the sides as needed.
With the motor running, drizzle in 1 tbsp of the olive oil, then taste and add more salt or lemon juice if needed.

stages.title: Finish and serve
steps: Spoon the dip into a shallow bowl and swirl the surface with the back of a spoon.
Drizzle with the remaining 1 tbsp olive oil and serve at room temperature.

tips: Draining the roasted capsicum keeps the dip thick enough to scoop rather than runny.
Toasting the walnuts releases their oils and removes bitterness, giving a rounder, nuttier flavour.
Steaming the hot capsicums under cover loosens the skins so they peel off easily.
Pomegranate molasses varies in sweetness and tartness, so add the lemon juice gradually and taste.
variations: Stir in 1 tsp ground Aleppo-style chilli or extra chilli flakes for more heat.
Replace half the walnuts with toasted almonds for a milder, sweeter dip.
recipe.storage: Refrigerate in an airtight container for up to 5 days. Bring to room temperature before serving. Freeze for up to 2 months and thaw in the fridge overnight.

recipe.title: Tunisian Brik
recipe.summary: Crisp pastry parcels filled with potato, parsley, tuna and a softly set egg.
ingredients: 2 potatoes, peeled and cut into 3 cm chunks
1 lemon, zested and cut into wedges

stages.title: Cook the potatoes
steps: Put the potatoes in a saucepan, cover with cold water and add the salt.
Bring to the boil over high heat, then reduce to medium and simmer for 12–15 minutes, until a knife slides in easily.
Drain well and leave in the colander to steam dry for 5 minutes.

stages.title: Make the filling
steps: Mash the potatoes coarsely in a bowl, leaving some small lumps.
Stir in the tuna, parsley, capers, lemon zest and black pepper.
Divide the filling into 4 portions.

stages.title: Fill and fold the pastry
steps: Lay 1 sheet of filo flat, keeping the others covered with a damp tea towel. Fold it in half to make a double-layer rectangle, or stack 2 sheets if yours are thin.
Spoon 1 portion of filling onto one half of the pastry, shaping it into a ring with a well in the centre.
Crack 1 egg into the well, being careful not to break the yolk.
Fold the pastry over to form a half-moon and press the edges firmly to seal, brushing with a little water if needed. Repeat with the remaining pastry, filling and eggs.

stages.title: Fry and serve
steps: Heat the oil in a large frying pan over medium-high heat for 2 minutes, until a pinch of pastry sizzles on contact.

Carefully slide in 1 brik and fry for 1–2 minutes on each side, spooning hot oil over the top, until the pastry is golden and crisp and the egg white is set and the yolk is runny, or cooked through if you prefer for a little longer.
Lift out onto paper towel to drain and repeat with the remaining briks, one at a time, reheating the oil briefly between batches.
Serve straight away with the lemon wedges.

tips: Seal the edges firmly and add the egg last, so the white stays inside the pastry as it fries.
Steam the potatoes dry before mashing, as wet mash makes the filling loose and the pastry soggy.
Fry one brik at a time so the oil stays hot and the pastry crisps instead of soaking up oil.
Shape the filling into a ring with a well so the egg sits in the centre and cooks evenly.
variations: Leave out the tuna and add 1 extra tbsp capers and a pinch of chilli flakes for a vegetarian brik.
Add 50 g crumbled feta to the filling for a saltier, creamier version.
recipe.storage: Best eaten straight away, as the pastry softens. Refrigerate leftovers in an airtight container for up to 1 day and reheat in a 200°C (180°C fan) oven for 8–10 minutes, until hot and crisp, and the egg is cooked through.

recipe.title: Japanese Kinpira Gobo
recipe.summary: Thin burdock and carrot strips stir-fried in soy, mirin and sesame until glossy.

stages.title: Prepare the burdock and carrots
steps: Scrub the burdock root under running water with a stiff brush to remove the dirt, leaving most of the skin on for flavour.
Cut the burdock into thin matchsticks about 5 cm long, then cut the carrots into matchsticks of the same size.
Fill a bowl with 1 litre water and stir in the white vinegar, then add the burdock as you cut it so it does not darken.

stages.title: Soak and drain
steps: Leave the burdock to soak in the vinegar water for 10 minutes to remove its bitterness.
Drain the burdock in a colander and pat it dry with a clean tea towel so it fries rather than steams.
Mix the soy sauce, mirin, white sugar and 1 tbsp water in a small bowl until the sugar dissolves.

stages.title: Stir-fry the vegetables
steps: Heat the vegetable oil and the sesame oil in a large frying pan over medium-high heat until the oil shimmers.
Add the burdock and stir-fry for 3–4 minutes, until it smells nutty and begins to soften at the edges.
Add the carrots and stir-fry for 2 minutes, until they are bright and just tender.

stages.title: Glaze and serve
steps: Pour in the soy sauce mixture and reduce the heat to medium.
Cook for 3–4 minutes, stirring often, until the liquid has almost evaporated and the vegetables look glossy.
Take the pan off the heat, stir through the sesame seeds and serve warm or at room temperature.

tips: Soaking the burdock in vinegar water stops it browning and draws out its earthy bitterness, so the finished dish tastes cleaner.
Cut the carrots and burdock to the same thickness so both are tender at the same time and keep a slight bite.
Drying the burdock before frying lets it brown lightly instead of steaming, which gives a deeper nutty flavour.
Leaving the burdock skin on keeps the most flavour; scrub it well rather than peeling it.
variations: Add 1/2 tsp chilli flakes with the carrots for the spicy version often served in Japan.
Use parsnip matchsticks in place of burdock when it is unavailable; skip the soaking and cook for about 1 minute less.
recipe.storage: Refrigerate in an airtight container for up to 3 days. Serve cold, or reheat in a frying pan over medium heat for 2–3 minutes until hot.

recipe.title: German Rotkohl
recipe.summary: Slow-braised red cabbage with apple, vinegar and warming cloves for a sweet-tart finish.

stages.title: Prepare the cabbage, apples and onion
steps: Remove the tough outer leaves from the red cabbage, cut it into quarters and cut out the core.
Shred the cabbage finely with a sharp knife and place it in a large bowl.
Peel, core and coarsely grate the apples, then toss them through the cabbage so they don't brown.
Peel the onion and slice it thinly.

stages.title: Soften the onion
steps: Melt the butter in a large heavy-based saucepan over medium heat.
Add the sliced onion and the salt, and cook, stirring often, for 5–6 minutes until soft and translucent but not browned.

stages.title: Braise the cabbage
steps: Add the cabbage and apple to the pan and stir for 2 minutes until the cabbage starts to wilt.
Add the apple cider vinegar, white sugar, whole cloves and 150 ml water, and stir to combine.
Bring to a simmer over medium heat, then reduce the heat to low and cover with a lid.
Cook for 35–40 minutes, stirring every 10 minutes, until the cabbage is very tender and deep purple-red.

stages.title: Reduce and season
steps: Remove the lid, increase the heat to medium and cook for 3–5 minutes, stirring, until most of the liquid has evaporated and the cabbage looks glossy.
Remove the cloves, then taste and add the black pepper, plus a little more sugar or vinegar if you want it sweeter or sharper.
Serve hot.

tips: Grate the apple straight into the cabbage so the acid in the vinegar and juices keeps the colour bright red-purple instead of dull blue.
Cook the onion without browning so it melts into the sauce and adds sweetness rather than a roasted flavour.
Braise covered on low heat so the cabbage softens in its own steam without scorching on the base of the pan.
Adding the sugar and vinegar together balances the sweet-sour flavour, and tasting at the end lets you adjust once the liquid has reduced.
variations: Stir through 2 tbsp of redcurrant jelly in the last 5 minutes for a fruitier, sweeter finish.
Add a bay leaf with the cloves and a splash of red wine in place of 50 ml of the water for a richer, deeper flavour.
recipe.storage: Refrigerate in an airtight container for up to 3 days, or freeze for up to 2 months. Reheat in a saucepan over low heat with a splash of water until steaming hot. The flavour improves after a day.

recipe.title: Korean Gyeran Bap
recipe.summary: Warm rice topped with a fried egg, sesame oil, soy sauce and toasted seaweed.

stages.title: Prepare the toppings
steps: Cut the nori sheets into thin strips with kitchen scissors.
Thinly slice the spring onions.
Mix the soy sauce and sesame oil in a small bowl.

stages.title: Warm the rice
steps: Place the cooked rice in a microwave-safe bowl, cover and heat on high for 2–3 minutes, stirring once, until steaming hot all the way through.
Divide the hot rice among 4 bowls and dot each with a quarter of the butter so it melts into the rice.

stages.title: Fry the eggs
steps: Heat the vegetable oil in a large non-stick frying pan over medium-high heat for 1 minute until shimmering.
Crack in the eggs, leaving space between them, and cook for 2–3 minutes until the edges are crisp and golden and the whites are set.
For runny yolks, remove the eggs at this point; for firmer yolks, flip and cook for another 30 seconds, until the yolks are cooked to your liking.
Slide one egg onto each bowl of rice.

stages.title: Finish and serve
steps: Spoon the soy and sesame oil mixture over the eggs and rice.
Scatter the nori strips and spring onions on top.
Break the yolk and stir everything together while the rice is still hot.

tips: Hot rice melts the butter and warms the yolk into a sauce, so reheat cold rice until steaming.
Frying the eggs in hot oil crisps the whites at the edges, which gives contrast with the soft rice.
Cut the nori just before serving so it stays crisp rather than going chewy.
variations: Add a spoonful of gochujang to the soy mixture for a spicy, savoury version.
Top with sautéed mushrooms or sliced avocado for a heartier bowl.
recipe.storage: Best eaten straight away. Keep leftover rice separately in the fridge for up to 1 day and reheat until steaming hot; cook fresh eggs each time.

recipe.title: Malaysian Char Kway Teow
recipe.summary: Wide rice noodles wok-fried with prawns, bean sprouts, egg and dark soy until smoky.
ingredients: 4 spring onions, cut into 3 cm lengths
1 bunch chives, cut into 4 cm lengths

stages.title: Prepare the noodles and sauce
steps: Peel apart the noodles gently with your fingers. If they are stiff from the fridge, cover with a damp paper towel and microwave for 30 seconds, then separate them.
Whisk the dark soy sauce, soy sauce, white sugar and black pepper in a small bowl until the sugar dissolves.
Lightly beat the eggs in a separate bowl.

stages.title: Prepare the aromatics and prawns
steps: Pat the prawns dry with paper towel so they sear rather than steam.
Chop the garlic and cut the spring onions and chives, then keep them in separate piles near the stove.
Measure the bean sprouts and chilli flakes so they are ready to go in quickly.

stages.title: Sear the prawns and scramble the eggs
steps: Heat a wok over high heat until it just begins to smoke. Add 1 tbsp of the vegetable oil, then the prawns, and stir-fry for 1–2 minutes until pink and curled. Tip them onto a plate.
Add 1 tbsp of the oil to the wok, pour in the eggs and let them set for 10 seconds, then break them into pieces. Cook for about 30 seconds until just set, then move them to the plate with the prawns.

stages.title: Stir-fry the noodles
steps: Add the remaining 1 tbsp oil to the wok over high heat. Stir-fry the garlic and chilli flakes for 15 seconds until fragrant.
Add the noodles and the sauce, then toss constantly for 2–3 minutes until the noodles are evenly dark, heated through and slightly charred in spots.
If the noodles stick, lift and toss them rather than stirring so they don't break up.

stages.title: Finish and serve
steps: Return the prawns and eggs to the wok. Add the bean sprouts, spring onions and chives.
Toss over high heat for 1 minute until the sprouts are just wilted but still crisp and the prawns are cooked through with no grey, translucent flesh.
Serve straight away while the noodles are hot.

tips: Cook in a very hot wok and keep the noodles moving, because this gives the smoky char flavour. A crowded or cool wok steams the noodles into a mushy clump.
Pat the prawns dry before searing, since surface water stops them browning and lowers the wok temperature.
Fresh noodles break less when warmed briefly and separated before they hit the wok, as cold, stuck-together strands tear when tossed.
Fry the dish in one batch only if your wok is large; for a smaller pan, make it in two batches so the heat stays high.
variations: Replace the prawns with 250 g firm tofu cut into cubes and pan-fried until golden, and check the soy sauce labels if serving vegetarians.
Add 2 sliced Chinese-style sausages or 100 g sliced fish cake with the garlic for a more traditional version.
recipe.storage: Best eaten straight away. Refrigerate leftovers in an airtight container for up to 1 day and reheat in a hot pan until steaming hot all the way through.

recipe.title: Israeli Sabich Pita
recipe.summary: Soft pita filled with roasted aubergine, boiled eggs, chopped salad and tangy tahini.

stages.title: Roast the eggplant
steps: Heat the oven to 220°C (200°C fan) and line a large tray with baking paper.
Cut the eggplants into 1 cm thick rounds and toss with the olive oil and 1/2 tsp of the salt.
