recipe.summary: Crisp cinnamon-sugar churros with soft centres, dipped into warm dark chocolate sauce.

stages.title: Make the dough
steps: Combine the water, butter and salt in a medium saucepan and heat over medium heat, stirring, until the butter melts and the water comes to a boil.
Tip in the flour all at once and reduce the heat to low. Stir vigorously with a wooden spoon for 1–2 minutes, until the dough forms a smooth ball and pulls away from the sides of the pan.
Transfer the dough to a bowl and cool for 5 minutes, until warm but not hot to the touch.

stages.title: Beat in the eggs and pipe
steps: Beat the eggs and vanilla extract together in a small jug. Add to the dough in 3 additions, beating hard with a wooden spoon or electric beaters after each, until the dough is thick, glossy and smooth.
Spoon the dough into a piping bag fitted with a large star nozzle.
Line a tray with baking paper and pipe 10–12 cm lengths onto it, snipping each with scissors. You should have about 12 churros.

stages.title: Make the chocolate sauce
steps: Place the chocolate in a heatproof bowl.
Heat the cream in a small saucepan over medium heat for 2–3 minutes, until steaming and small bubbles form at the edge. Do not let it boil.
Pour the hot cream over the chocolate and stand for 1 minute, then stir until smooth and glossy. Keep warm.

stages.title: Fry and coat
steps: Mix the caster sugar and ground cinnamon on a shallow plate.
Heat the vegetable oil in a deep, heavy-based saucepan over medium heat to 175°C, or until a small piece of dough sizzles steadily and turns golden in about 1 minute.
Fry 4 churros at a time for 3–4 minutes, turning occasionally, until deep golden and cooked through. Cut one open to check the inside is cooked and not doughy.
Lift out with tongs, drain on paper towel for 30 seconds, then roll in the cinnamon sugar. Repeat with the remaining dough, letting the oil return to 175°C between batches.
Serve the churros hot with the warm chocolate sauce for dipping.

tips: Beating the eggs in a little at a time lets the dough absorb them. It stays thick enough to hold the ridges when piped.
Oil at 175°C cooks the centre before the outside darkens. Cooler oil gives greasy churros, and hotter oil leaves them raw inside.
Fry in small batches so the oil temperature doesn't drop and the churros don't stick together.
The star nozzle makes ridges that crisp up and give the cinnamon sugar more to cling to.
variations: Stir 1 tsp finely grated orange zest into the cream before heating for an orange chocolate sauce.
Add a pinch of chilli powder to the chocolate sauce for a gentle warmth.
recipe.storage: Churros are best eaten within 30 minutes of frying. Refrigerate leftover sauce in a sealed container for up to 3 days and reheat gently in the microwave in short bursts, stirring.

recipe.title: Thai Larb Gai
recipe.summary: Warm minced chicken salad with lime, fish sauce, mint and toasted rice powder.
ingredients: 1 bunch coriander, leaves and tender stems roughly chopped

stages.title: Make the toasted rice powder
steps: Heat a dry frying pan over medium heat and add the 2 tbsp rice.
Toast, shaking the pan often, for 4–5 minutes until deep golden and fragrant.
Tip the rice onto a plate and cool for 3 minutes.
Grind the rice in a mortar or spice grinder to a coarse powder, like fine sand with some texture.

stages.title: Prepare the dressing and herbs
steps: Juice 2 of the limes to get about 80 ml juice and cut the remaining lime into wedges for serving.
Thinly slice the shallots and pick the mint leaves.
Roughly chop the coriander and separate the lettuce leaves, then keep them cold until serving.
Stir the fish sauce and lime juice together in a small bowl.

stages.title: Cook the chicken
steps: Heat a large frying pan over medium-high heat and add the chicken mince with 60 ml water.
Cook for 7–8 minutes, breaking up the mince with a wooden spoon, until cooked through and no longer pink, and most of the liquid has evaporated.
Take the pan off the heat and let the mince cool for 2 minutes.

stages.title: Toss and serve
steps: Pour the fish sauce and lime mixture over the warm chicken and stir through the chilli flakes and shallots.
Fold in the toasted rice powder, mint and coriander.
Taste and add a little more fish sauce or lime if needed.
Spoon the larb into the lettuce leaves and serve with the lime wedges.

tips: Toasting the rice until deep golden gives the nutty flavour and slightly crunchy texture that larb is known for.
Cooking the mince with a little water keeps the small crumbs tender and stops them drying out.
Add the herbs and shallots once the chicken has cooled slightly so they stay fresh and don't wilt.
variations: Use pork mince for larb moo, cooked until no pink remains.
Add 1 tsp sugar and extra chilli flakes for a sweeter, hotter version.
recipe.storage: Refrigerate the chicken mixture in an airtight container for up to 2 days, keeping the lettuce separate. Serve cold or reheat until steaming hot throughout.

recipe.title: Peruvian Aji de Gallina
recipe.summary: Shredded chicken in a creamy yellow chilli and walnut sauce, served with rice and olives.
ingredients: 3 slices white bread, crusts removed, torn

stages.title: Poach the chicken
steps: Put the chicken breast and chicken stock in a medium saucepan and add 400 ml water so the chicken is covered.
Bring to a gentle simmer over medium heat, then reduce to low and poach for 15–18 minutes, until cooked through, no longer pink in the middle and 75°C in the thickest part.
Lift the chicken onto a board and rest for 10 minutes, keeping the broth in the pan.
Shred the chicken with two forks and set aside.

stages.title: Make the walnut sauce base
steps: Put the torn bread in a bowl, pour over the evaporated milk and soak for 5 minutes until soft.
Add the bread and milk, walnuts, parmesan and 250 ml of the reserved warm broth to a blender.
Blend for 1 minute until completely smooth, and set aside.

stages.title: Cook the aji sauce
steps: Heat the olive oil in a large deep frying pan over medium heat and cook the onion with the salt for 5–6 minutes, until soft and translucent.
Add the garlic, aji amarillo paste and turmeric and stir for 2 minutes, until fragrant.
Pour in the blended sauce and stir well, then simmer over low heat for 8–10 minutes, stirring often, until thick and creamy enough to coat a spoon.
Stir in a splash more reserved broth if the sauce becomes too thick.

stages.title: Cook the rice and eggs
steps: Cook the rice according to the packet.
While the rice cooks, put the eggs in a small saucepan of boiling water and boil over medium heat for 10 minutes, until the yolks are firm and cooked through.
Cool the eggs under cold running water, then peel and cut into quarters.

stages.title: Finish and serve
steps: Fold the shredded chicken into the sauce and warm through over low heat for 3–4 minutes, until hot all the way through.
Season with black pepper and extra salt if needed.
Spoon the chicken over the rice and top with the egg quarters and kalamata olives.

tips: Add the aji amarillo paste gradually and taste, because brands vary a lot in heat.
Poaching the chicken gently keeps the breast tender, while a hard boil makes it stringy.
Using the poaching broth to thin the sauce adds chicken flavour that plain water would not.
Blending the soaked bread with the walnuts is what thickens the sauce, so blend until no grit remains.
variations: Replace the walnuts with the same amount of pecans for a slightly sweeter sauce.
Use poached chicken thigh instead of breast for richer, more tender meat, poaching for 20–25 minutes until cooked through.
recipe.storage: Refrigerate the chicken sauce in an airtight container for up to 3 days. Reheat gently in a saucepan over low heat with a splash of water or stock until steaming hot. Keep the rice and eggs separate; freezing is not recommended because the sauce can split.

recipe.title: Indian Baingan Bharta
recipe.summary: Smoky mashed aubergine cooked with onion, tomato, ginger and green chilli.

stages.title: Roast the eggplants
steps: Heat the oven to 230°C (210°C fan) and line a tray with baking paper.
Prick each eggplant 5–6 times with a fork and rub the skins with 1 tbsp of the oil.
Roast for 35–40 minutes, turning once, until the skins are blackened and wrinkled and the flesh is completely soft when pressed.

stages.title: Cool and mash the flesh
steps: Rest the eggplants on the tray for 10 minutes, until cool enough to handle.
Slit them open, scoop out the soft flesh and discard the skins and any pooled bitter liquid.
Chop the flesh roughly with a knife until mashed but still a little chunky.

stages.title: Cook the spiced base
steps: Heat the remaining 2 tbsp oil in a large frying pan over medium heat and add the cumin seeds. Cook for 30 seconds until they sizzle and smell fragrant.
Add the onion and cook, stirring, for 6–7 minutes until soft and golden.
Stir in the garlic, ginger and green chilli and cook for 1 minute until fragrant.
Add the tomatoes, turmeric and salt. Cook for 6–8 minutes, stirring often, until the tomatoes break down into a thick, jammy paste.

stages.title: Combine and finish
steps: Add the mashed eggplant to the pan and stir through the tomato base.
Cook over medium-low heat for 8 minutes, stirring often, until thick and the oil begins to separate at the edges.
Stir through the coriander and taste for salt. Serve hot.

tips: Charring the skins until blackened gives the dish its smoky flavour; pale skins mean a flat-tasting bharta.
Discard the liquid that collects inside the roasted eggplants, as it tastes bitter and makes the dish watery.
Cook the tomatoes until jammy before adding the eggplant so the finished bharta is thick, not soupy.
variations: Hold the eggplants directly over a gas flame, turning with tongs for 10–12 minutes until blackened and collapsed, for a stronger smoky flavour.
Stir in 1/2 cup frozen peas with the eggplant and cook until heated through for a sweeter finish.
recipe.storage: Refrigerate in an airtight container for up to 3 days or freeze for up to 2 months. Reheat in a pan over low heat until steaming hot, adding a splash of water if thick.

recipe.title: American Banana Cream Pie
recipe.summary: Buttery biscuit crust filled with sliced bananas and vanilla custard, crowned with whipped cream.

stages.title: Make the biscuit crust
steps: Crush the digestive biscuits to fine crumbs in a food processor, or in a zip-lock bag with a rolling pin.
Melt the butter in a small saucepan over low heat for 2–3 minutes, then stir it through the crumbs until they look like wet sand.
Press the crumbs firmly over the base and up the sides of a 20 cm pie dish, using the back of a spoon or a flat-bottomed glass.
Chill the crust in the fridge for 30 minutes, until firm.

stages.title: Cook the custard
steps: Heat the milk in a medium saucepan over medium heat for 4–5 minutes, until steaming and small bubbles appear at the edge. Do not let it boil.
Whisk the egg yolks, caster sugar and cornflour in a large heatproof bowl for 1–2 minutes, until pale and smooth.
Pour the hot milk into the yolk mixture in a thin stream, whisking constantly so the eggs don't scramble.
Return the mixture to the saucepan over medium heat and stir constantly with a whisk for 4–5 minutes, until thick and bubbling. Keep stirring for 1 minute more to cook out the cornflour.
Remove from the heat and stir in the vanilla extract.

stages.title: Cool the custard and fill the pie
steps: Pour the custard into a clean bowl, then press cling film directly onto the surface to stop a skin forming. Cool for 10 minutes.
Peel and slice 2 of the bananas into 5 mm rounds and layer them over the chilled crust.
Pour the warm custard over the bananas and smooth the top with a spatula.

stages.title: Chill until set
steps: Press fresh cling film lightly onto the surface of the custard.
Refrigerate for at least 4 hours, until the custard is completely set and holds a clean slice.

stages.title: Top and serve
steps: Whip the thickened cream in a bowl with a whisk or electric beaters for 2–3 minutes, until soft peaks form.
Spread the cream over the set custard, swirling it into peaks.
Slice the remaining banana and arrange it on top just before serving so it doesn't brown.
Cut into 4 wedges with a sharp knife, wiping the blade between cuts.

tips: Pressing cling film onto the custard stops a rubbery skin from forming, which would leave lumps under the cream.
Cooking the custard for a full minute after it bubbles cooks out the starchy taste of the cornflour and ensures it sets firmly.
Pouring the hot milk into the yolks slowly warms them gently, so the eggs thicken the custard instead of scrambling.
Add the fresh banana garnish only at serving; cut banana browns within an hour or two.
variations: Scatter toasted desiccated coconut over the whipped cream for a nutty crunch.
Drizzle a little warm dulce de leche-style caramel over the bananas before adding the custard.
recipe.storage: Refrigerate covered for up to 2 days, though the crust softens over time. Not suitable to freeze, as the custard will weep when thawed.

recipe.title: German Kartoffelsalat
recipe.summary: Warm potato salad dressed with tangy mustard, vinegar and bacon instead of mayonnaise.
ingredients: 1/2 tsp salt, plus extra for the cooking water

stages.title: Cook the potatoes
steps: Scrub the potatoes and leave them whole and unpeeled. Place in a large pot, cover with cold water and add a generous pinch of salt.
Bring to the boil over high heat, then reduce to medium and simmer for 20–25 minutes, until a knife slides into the centre of the largest potato with no resistance.
Drain and leave until cool enough to handle, about 5 minutes. Peel the potatoes while still warm, then cut into 5 mm slices and place in a large bowl.

stages.title: Make the bacon dressing
steps: Heat the olive oil in a frying pan over medium heat. Add the bacon and cook for 5–6 minutes, stirring, until golden and crisp.
Add the onion to the pan and cook in the bacon fat for 3–4 minutes, stirring, until soft and translucent.
Pour in the stock, vinegar, mustard and sugar. Whisk, scraping up any browned bits, and simmer for 2 minutes until slightly reduced.
Stir in the salt and a good grind of black pepper.

stages.title: Dress and rest
steps: Pour the hot dressing over the warm potato slices and fold gently with a large spoon so the slices stay whole.
Leave to sit at room temperature for 15–20 minutes, folding once halfway, until the potatoes have absorbed most of the liquid.
Taste and add salt or a splash more vinegar if needed. Fold through the parsley and serve warm or at room temperature.

tips: Waxy potatoes hold their shape when sliced and tossed, whereas floury varieties break down into mash.
Peeling and slicing the potatoes while warm lets them soak up the dressing; cold potatoes absorb far less flavour.
Starting the potatoes in cold water cooks them evenly, so the outsides don't turn mushy before the centres are tender.
variations: For a vegetarian version, leave out the bacon, cook the onion in 2 tbsp olive oil and check the stock and mustard labels.
Add 2 chopped gherkins and 1 tbsp of their brine to the dressing for a sharper flavour.
recipe.storage: Refrigerate in an airtight container for up to 3 days. Bring to room temperature before serving, or warm gently in a pan. Not suitable for freezing.

recipe.title: Italian Ribollita
recipe.summary: Rustic Tuscan bean-and-vegetable soup thickened with bread, kale and olive oil.
ingredients: 1 x 400 g can cannellini beans, drained and rinsed
200 g kale, stems removed and leaves sliced
200 g stale bread, torn into 2 cm pieces

stages.title: Prepare the vegetables and bread
steps: Finely dice the onion, carrots and celery into pieces about 5 mm wide so they soften evenly.
Crush the garlic and pick the thyme leaves from the sprigs.
Remove the kale stems, then slice the leaves into 2 cm strips.
Tear the stale bread into 2 cm pieces and drain and rinse the cannellini beans.

stages.title: Soften the soffritto
steps: Heat 2 tbsp of the olive oil in a large heavy-based pot over medium heat.
Add the onion, carrots, celery and salt, and cook for 10 minutes, stirring often, until soft and the onion is translucent.
Stir in the garlic and thyme leaves and cook for 1 minute until fragrant.

stages.title: Simmer the soup
steps: Mash half the cannellini beans with a fork until mostly smooth.
Add the diced tomatoes, vegetable stock, mashed beans and the remaining whole beans to the pot, and bring to the boil over high heat.
Reduce the heat to medium-low and simmer for 15 minutes, until the vegetables are very tender.
Stir in the kale and simmer for 8 minutes, until the leaves are dark and tender.

stages.title: Add the bread and rest
steps: Stir the torn bread into the soup, take the pot off the heat and leave for 15 minutes, until the bread has swollen and the soup is thick and stew-like.
Return the pot to low heat and warm for 5 minutes, stirring to break up the bread, until steaming hot.
Season with black pepper and extra salt if needed, then drizzle each serving with some of the remaining 1 tbsp olive oil.

tips: Stale bread holds its shape while it soaks up the broth, whereas fresh bread turns to paste.
Mashing half the beans thickens the soup naturally and gives a creamy base without cream.
Cooking the soffritto slowly for the full 10 minutes draws out the sweetness that carries the soup, since there is no meat.
Ribollita means reboiled and tastes better the next day, because the bread continues to thicken the soup as it sits.
variations: Swap the kale for cavolo nero, which is the traditional Tuscan green, and cook it for an extra 2–3 minutes.
Add a parmesan rind with the stock and remove it before serving for a savoury depth (parmesan is not vegetarian, so check the label if serving vegetarians).
recipe.storage: Refrigerate in an airtight container for up to 3 days. The soup thickens as it sits, so add a splash of water when reheating in a pot over medium heat until steaming hot. Freeze for up to 2 months.

recipe.title: Japanese Chicken Soboro Don
recipe.summary: Sweet-savoury minced chicken and fluffy scrambled egg served in colourful stripes over rice.

stages.title: Cook the rice
steps: Rinse the rice in a sieve under cold water until the water runs mostly clear, then drain.
Cook the rice according to the packet, using short-grain or sushi rice if you can.
Rest the rice, covered and off the heat, for 10 minutes, then fluff with a fork.

stages.title: Prepare the toppings
steps: Grate the ginger and thinly slice the spring onions.
In a small bowl, mix the soy sauce, mirin and white sugar until the sugar dissolves.
Crack the eggs into a separate bowl, add the salt and beat until no streaks of white remain.

stages.title: Cook the chicken soboro
steps: Heat the oil in a large frying pan over medium heat.
Add the chicken mince and ginger, breaking the mince up with a wooden spoon or two spoons as it cooks, for 3–4 minutes until no pink remains.
Pour in the soy mixture and cook over medium heat for 4–5 minutes, stirring constantly, until the liquid has almost evaporated and the mince is fine, glossy and cooked through.
Tip the chicken into a bowl and cover to keep warm.

stages.title: Scramble the eggs
steps: Wipe out the pan and place it over low heat.
Pour in the beaten eggs and stir constantly with a spatula or chopsticks for 3–4 minutes until the eggs form small, soft curds and are cooked through with no liquid egg remaining.
Remove the pan from the heat straight away so the eggs do not turn dry.

stages.title: Assemble the bowls
steps: Divide the rice among four bowls.
Arrange the chicken on one half of each bowl and the egg on the other half.
Scatter the spring onions over the top and serve while warm.

tips: Break the mince up as soon as it hits the pan, before it browns, so it cooks into fine crumbs rather than clumps.
Cooking the eggs over low heat and stirring constantly gives small, tender curds; high heat makes them rubbery.
Simmering the soy mixture until almost dry makes the chicken glossy and seasoned rather than soupy, so it doesn't make the rice wet.
variations: Add blanched green beans or snow peas, sliced thinly, as a third topping for colour and crunch.
Use pork mince instead of chicken and cook until no pink remains.
recipe.storage: Store the rice, chicken and egg in separate airtight containers in the fridge for up to 3 days. Reheat the chicken and rice in the microwave until steaming hot, and the egg until warmed through.

recipe.title: French Madeleines
recipe.summary: Delicate shell-shaped sponge cakes with buttery edges, lemon zest and a soft centre.
ingredients: 110 g butter, plus 1 tbsp extra, softened, for greasing
1 tbsp plain flour, extra, for dusting the tin

stages.title: Melt the butter and mix the dry ingredients
steps: Melt the 110 g butter in a small saucepan over low heat for 2–3 minutes until completely liquid, then pour into a bowl and leave to cool to lukewarm.
Sift the 120 g plain flour and the baking powder into a medium bowl.
Finely grate the zest of the lemon and set aside.

stages.title: Make the batter
steps: Whisk the eggs and caster sugar in a large bowl with electric beaters on high speed for 5–6 minutes, until pale, thick and doubled in volume.
Whisk in the vanilla extract and lemon zest.
Gently fold in the sifted flour mixture in two batches with a spatula until just combined.
Fold in the cooled melted butter until the batter is smooth and glossy, with no streaks of butter.

stages.title: Chill the batter
steps: Cover the bowl with plastic wrap and refrigerate for 45 minutes, until the batter is firm enough to hold its shape when spooned.
Meanwhile, brush the madeleine tin generously with the softened extra butter, dust with the extra 1 tbsp plain flour, then tap out the excess and chill the tin.

stages.title: Bake the madeleines
steps: Heat the oven to 200°C (180°C fan) while the batter finishes chilling.
Spoon the batter into the moulds, filling each about three-quarters full without spreading it out.
Bake on the middle shelf for 9–11 minutes, until risen with a hump, golden at the edges and springy when touched in the centre.

stages.title: Unmould and serve
steps: Rap the tin firmly on the bench and tip the madeleines out onto a wire rack, using a spoon to loosen any that stick.
Cool for 10 minutes, then dust with the icing sugar and serve while still slightly warm.

tips: Chilling the batter makes the cold mixture hit the hot oven and puff quickly, which creates the characteristic hump.
Whisking the eggs and sugar until thick traps air, which gives a light, springy crumb without extra raising agent.
Cooling the melted butter stops it from cooking the eggs or deflating the whisked mixture when folded in.
Greasing and flouring the tin, then chilling it, helps the shell pattern release cleanly.
variations: Swap the lemon zest for orange zest and use half the vanilla for a softer citrus flavour.
Dip the cooled madeleines in melted dark chocolate and let it set on baking paper before serving.
recipe.storage: Best eaten the day they are baked. Store cooled madeleines in an airtight container at room temperature for up to 2 days, or freeze for up to 1 month and thaw at room temperature.

recipe.title: Brazilian Pão de Queijo
recipe.summary: Warm, chewy cheese breads with crisp shells made from tapioca starch and Parmesan.
ingredients: 60 ml vegetable oil, plus extra for greasing and oiling hands

stages.title: Heat the liquid and make the dough base
steps: Heat the oven to 200°C (180°C fan) and line a large baking tray with baking paper.
Put the tapioca starch in a large heatproof bowl.
Combine the milk, the vegetable oil, the salt and 120 ml water in a small saucepan over medium heat. Stir until steaming and just about to boil, about 3–4 minutes.
Pour the hot liquid over the tapioca starch and stir with a wooden spoon until no dry starch remains and you have a sticky, stretchy dough.

stages.title: Cool and add the eggs
steps: Leave the dough to cool for 5 minutes, so the heat does not scramble the eggs.
Beat in the eggs one at a time with the wooden spoon, mixing until each is absorbed and the dough is smooth and glossy before adding the next.

stages.title: Add the cheese and shape
steps: Stir the grated parmesan through the dough until evenly mixed. The dough will be soft and sticky.
Lightly oil your hands with a little extra vegetable oil.
Roll heaped tablespoons of dough into balls about 4 cm wide and place them on the tray 3 cm apart.

stages.title: Bake and serve
steps: Bake for 20–25 minutes, until puffed, golden and lightly crisp on the outside.
Rest on the tray for 5 minutes, as the centres are very hot, then serve warm.

tips: Let the dough cool for 5 minutes before adding the eggs so they blend in smoothly instead of cooking into strands.
Tapioca starch, not flour, creates the chewy, stretchy centre; it will not work with plain flour.
Oiling your hands stops the sticky dough clinging to your palms as you roll.
Finely grated parmesan melts evenly into the dough, giving a savoury flavour without cheese lumps.
variations: Replace half the parmesan with grated mozzarella for a stretchier, milder centre.
Add 1 tbsp finely chopped chives to the dough with the cheese.
recipe.storage: Refrigerate in an airtight container for up to 3 days, or freeze baked balls for up to 2 months. Reheat in a 180°C (160°C fan) oven for 8–10 minutes until hot and crisp.

recipe.title: Italian Polenta with Mushrooms
recipe.summary: Creamy Parmesan polenta topped with golden sautéed mushrooms, garlic and thyme.

stages.title: Prepare the ingredients
steps: Wipe the mushrooms clean with a damp cloth, then slice them thickly, halving any small ones.
Finely chop the garlic and pick the thyme leaves from their stalks.
Finely grate the parmesan and measure the polenta and stock so they are ready beside the stove.

stages.title: Brown the mushrooms
steps: Heat 1 tbsp olive oil in a large frying pan over medium-high heat until it shimmers.
Add half the mushrooms in a single layer and cook for 5–6 minutes, turning occasionally, until deep golden. Tip into a bowl and repeat with the remaining 1 tbsp oil and mushrooms.
Return all the mushrooms to the pan, add the garlic, thyme, a pinch of the salt and black pepper, and cook for 1 minute until fragrant. Cover to keep warm.

stages.title: Cook the polenta
steps: Bring the vegetable stock and the remaining salt to a boil in a medium saucepan over high heat, then reduce to medium-low.
Pour in the polenta in a thin stream, whisking constantly to prevent lumps.
Switch to a wooden spoon and cook for 4–5 minutes, stirring often, until thick, smooth and pulling away from the side of the pan. If it is stiff, loosen with 60 ml hot water.

stages.title: Finish and serve
steps: Take the polenta off the heat and stir in the butter and three-quarters of the parmesan until melted and creamy.
Taste and add more salt and black pepper if needed.
Spoon the polenta into four warm bowls, top with the mushrooms and any pan juices, and finish with the remaining parmesan.

tips: Cooking the mushrooms in two batches keeps the pan hot so they brown instead of steaming in their own liquid.
Pouring the polenta in a thin stream while whisking stops the grains clumping as they hit the hot stock.
Polenta keeps thickening as it sits, so serve it straight away or whisk in a splash of hot water to loosen it.
Parmesan is not vegetarian because it is made with animal rennet. Check the label or use a vegetarian hard cheese if needed.
variations: Stir 2 tbsp mascarpone through the polenta with the parmesan for a richer, softer finish.
Add a handful of baby spinach to the mushrooms with the garlic and cook until just wilted.
recipe.storage: Refrigerate the polenta and mushrooms separately in airtight containers for up to 3 days. Reheat the polenta in a saucepan over low heat with a splash of water or stock, stirring until smooth, and reheat the mushrooms in a frying pan until hot.

recipe.title: Mexican Sopa de Fideo
recipe.summary: Toasted vermicelli noodles simmered in a light tomato and garlic broth with lime.

stages.title: Blend the tomato base
steps: Put the tomatoes, onion, garlic and 250 ml of the chicken stock in a blender.
Blend for 1 minute until completely smooth, then set aside.
Break the vermicelli into 4–5 cm lengths with your hands.

stages.title: Toast the noodles
steps: Heat the oil in a large deep saucepan over medium heat.
Add the vermicelli and cook for 3–5 minutes, stirring constantly, until evenly deep golden brown.
Take care not to let any strands turn dark brown, as they taste bitter.

stages.title: Simmer the sauce
steps: Pour the blended tomato mixture into the pan, standing back as it will spit.
Cook over medium heat for 5 minutes, stirring often, until the sauce darkens and thickens slightly.
Add the salt and a generous grind of black pepper.

stages.title: Cook the noodles in the soup
steps: Pour in the remaining 750 ml chicken stock and stir well, scraping up anything stuck to the base.
Bring to a boil over medium-high heat, then reduce to medium-low.
Simmer for 5–7 minutes, stirring occasionally, until the noodles are tender and the soup has thickened slightly.
Taste and add more salt or pepper if needed.

stages.title: Serve
steps: Ladle the soup into four bowls while hot.
Scatter over the coriander and serve with the lime wedges for squeezing over.

tips: Toasting the vermicelli until golden gives the soup its nutty, savoury flavour, and the coating of oil helps the strands stay separate.
Simmering the blended tomato before adding the rest of the stock cooks off its raw, acidic taste and deepens the colour.
Serve straight away, because the noodles keep absorbing stock and the soup turns thick and stodgy if left standing.
variations: Stir through 2 cups of shredded cooked chicken with the remaining stock for a heartier lunch.
Add 1 tsp chilli flakes with the tomato mixture for a spicier soup.
recipe.storage: Refrigerate in an airtight container for up to 2 days. The noodles will absorb the liquid, so add a splash of water or stock when reheating in a saucepan over medium heat until steaming hot throughout.

recipe.title: French Leek and Potato Soup
recipe.summary: Smooth, buttery leek and potato soup finished with cream and fresh chives.
ingredients: 3 leeks, white and pale-green parts only
500 g potatoes, peeled and cut into 2 cm cubes

stages.title: Prepare the vegetables
steps: Trim the leeks, split them lengthways and rinse well under cold running water, fanning the layers to wash out any grit.
Slice the leeks thinly.
Peel the potatoes and cut them into 2 cm cubes.
Snip the chives finely and set aside for serving.

stages.title: Soften the leeks
steps: Melt the butter in a large heavy-based saucepan over low-medium heat.
Add the leeks and the salt and stir to coat in the butter.
Cover and cook, stirring occasionally, for 10–12 minutes until soft and silky but not browned.

stages.title: Simmer the soup
steps: Add the potatoes and the vegetable stock to the pan and stir.
Increase the heat to medium-high and bring to the boil, then reduce to low-medium and partly cover.
Simmer for 18–20 minutes until the potato breaks apart easily when pressed with a fork.
Remove from the heat and cool for 5 minutes before blending.

stages.title: Blend and finish
steps: Blend the soup with a stick blender until completely smooth, or in batches in a blender with the lid vented.
Return to the pan over low heat and stir in the cream, nutmeg and black pepper.
Warm gently for 2–3 minutes without boiling, then taste and add a little more salt if needed.
Ladle into bowls and scatter with the chives.

tips: Rinse the leeks after slicing if they are very sandy, because grit collects between the layers and ruins the smooth texture.
Cooking the leeks gently with a lid on softens them in their own moisture, which gives a sweet flavour that browning would spoil.
Starchy potatoes such as Sebago or Desiree break down for a naturally creamy soup without needing extra cream.
Add the cream off a boil, since high heat can make it split and look grainy.
variations: For a vichyssoise, cool the blended soup without the hot cream step, stir in the cream once cold and chill for at least 3 hours before serving.
Stir in a handful of baby spinach when blending for a green, slightly earthy soup.
recipe.storage: Refrigerate in an airtight container for up to 3 days. Reheat gently over low heat, stirring, until steaming; don't boil. Freeze without the cream for up to 3 months.

recipe.title: Japanese Oyakodon
recipe.summary: Tender chicken and softly set eggs simmered in a sweet-savoury dashi broth over steaming rice.
ingredients: 450 g chicken thigh, trimmed and cut into 2 cm pieces

stages.title: Cook the rice and prepare the toppings
steps: Cook the rice according to the packet, then keep it covered and warm.
Trim the chicken thighs of excess fat and cut into 2 cm pieces.
Thinly slice the onion and the spring onions, keeping them separate.
Lightly beat the eggs in a jug with a fork, so the whites and yolks are only just combined.

stages.title: Make the simmering sauce
steps: Combine the dashi stock, soy sauce, mirin and sugar in a wide, deep frying pan.
Bring to a simmer over medium heat, stirring until the sugar dissolves, about 2 minutes.
Add the onion and simmer over medium heat for 5–6 minutes, until soft and translucent.

stages.title: Cook the chicken and eggs
steps: Add the chicken to the pan in a single layer and simmer over medium heat for 8–9 minutes, turning once, until cooked through and no longer pink in the middle.
Pour the beaten eggs slowly over the chicken in a circular motion, without stirring.
Cover and cook over medium-low heat for 1–2 minutes, until the whites are just set and the yolks are soft and slightly runny, or cook a little longer if you prefer the egg firm.

stages.title: Assemble the bowls
steps: Divide the hot rice among four deep bowls.
Slide the chicken and egg over each portion with a large spoon, adding some of the pan juices to soak into the rice.
Scatter the spring onions over the top and serve straight away.

tips: Chicken thigh stays tender in the simmering sauce, whereas breast can turn dry and stringy in the same time.
Beat the eggs only lightly so you get ribbons of white and yolk rather than a uniform scramble.
Use a wide pan so the chicken sits in one layer and cooks evenly in the shallow sauce.
Take the pan off the heat while the egg is still slightly wet, because residual heat and the hot rice will finish setting it.
variations: Swap the chicken for thinly sliced pork loin for tanin-style katsudon-like flavour, simmering 4–5 minutes until no longer pink.
Add a handful of sliced mushrooms with the onion for extra savoury depth.
recipe.storage: Best eaten straight away. Refrigerate leftover chicken and egg separately from the rice in sealed containers for up to 2 days, and reheat until steaming hot.

recipe.title: Thai Tom Kha Gai
recipe.summary: Creamy coconut chicken soup infused with galangal, lemongrass, makrut lime and fresh lime juice.
ingredients: 3 lemongrass, bruised and cut into 5 cm lengths
40 g ginger, sliced into thin coins
2 limes, 1 juiced and 1 cut into wedges

stages.title: Prepare the aromatics
steps: Slice the chicken thinly against the grain into bite-sized strips.
Bruise the lemongrass with the back of a knife, then cut it into 5 cm lengths.
Slice the ginger into thin coins and tear the kaffir lime leaves.
Halve or quarter the mushrooms and thinly slice the red chillies.

stages.title: Infuse the broth
steps: Heat the vegetable oil in a large saucepan over medium heat, add the lemongrass, ginger and lime leaves and stir for 1 minute until fragrant.
Pour in the chicken stock and bring to a simmer over medium heat.
Reduce the heat to low and simmer for 10 minutes to infuse the broth.
Stir in the coconut milk and return to a gentle simmer.

stages.title: Cook the chicken and mushrooms
steps: Add the chicken and mushrooms to the broth.
Simmer gently over medium-low heat for 10–12 minutes, stirring occasionally, until the chicken is cooked through with no pink in the centre.
Keep the heat low, as boiling hard can split the coconut milk.

stages.title: Season and serve
steps: Remove the pan from the heat and stir in the fish sauce and the juice of 1 lime.
Taste and add more fish sauce or lime juice if needed.
Ladle into bowls and top with the sliced chilli and coriander leaves.
Serve with the lime wedges, and tell diners the lemongrass, ginger and lime leaves are not for eating.

tips: Bruising the lemongrass breaks its fibres so it releases more fragrance into the broth.
Add the lime juice off the heat, because boiling dulls its fresh flavour and can make it bitter.
Chicken thigh stays tender in the simmering broth, while breast tends to dry out.
Fish sauce differs in saltiness between brands, so add it gradually and taste as you go.
variations: Replace the chicken with 300 g peeled prawns and simmer for 3–4 minutes until pink and cooked through.
Add 1 tbsp of sugar-free chilli paste or extra chilli for a spicier soup.
recipe.storage: Cool quickly, then refrigerate in a sealed container for up to 3 days. Reheat gently on the stovetop until steaming hot throughout. Not suitable for freezing, as the coconut milk may separate.

recipe.title: Turkish Lentil Köfte
recipe.summary: Soft red-lentil and bulgur patties seasoned with tomato paste, cumin, parsley and lemon.
ingredients: 1 lemon, half juiced and half cut into wedges

stages.title: Prepare the ingredients
steps: Rinse the red lentils in a sieve under cold running water until the water runs mostly clear.
Finely chop the onion and the parsley leaves and stems.
Juice half the lemon and cut the other half into wedges.
Separate the lettuce leaves, choosing the small, cup-shaped ones, and set aside.

stages.title: Cook the lentils and bulgur
steps: Put the lentils, 550 ml water and the salt in a medium saucepan and bring to the boil over high heat.
Reduce the heat to medium-low and simmer, stirring occasionally, for 12–15 minutes until the lentils are very soft and have absorbed nearly all the water.
Remove the pan from the heat, stir in the bulgur, cover with a lid and leave for 15 minutes until the bulgur is tender and the mixture is thick.

stages.title: Fry the onion mixture
steps: While the lentils rest, heat the olive oil in a frying pan over medium heat.
Cook the onion, stirring often, for 5 minutes until soft and translucent.
Add the tomato paste, cumin and paprika and cook, stirring, for 1–2 minutes until the paste darkens and smells fragrant.

stages.title: Mix and shape
steps: Scrape the onion mixture into the lentil and bulgur mixture, add the parsley and lemon juice, and stir until evenly combined.
Leave to cool for about 5 minutes, until cool enough to handle, and the mixture holds together when squeezed.
With damp hands, shape tablespoons of the mixture into small ovals, pressing firmly so they hold their shape.
Serve the köfte in the lettuce leaves with the lemon wedges.

tips: Rinsing the lentils removes surface starch, so they cook up clean-tasting and not gluey.
Fine bulgur softens in the residual heat, so keep the lid on and don't add more water or the mixture will be too wet to shape.
Frying the tomato paste until it darkens removes its raw edge and deepens the flavour of the köfte.
Damp hands stop the mixture sticking and let you press the ovals smooth.
variations: Stir 1 tsp chilli flakes into the onion mixture for a hotter köfte.
Add 2 chopped spring onions with the parsley for a fresher, sharper bite.
recipe.storage: Refrigerate in an airtight container for up to 3 days and serve cold or at room temperature. Not recommended for freezing, as the texture turns grainy.

recipe.title: Japanese Chicken Karaage
recipe.summary: Crisp ginger-soy marinated chicken bites with juicy centres and a squeeze of lemon.
ingredients: 650 g chicken thigh, skin on, boneless

stages.title: Cut the chicken
steps: Trim any excess fat from the chicken thigh and cut it into 4 cm chunks.
Pat the chicken pieces dry with paper towel so the coating sticks later.

stages.title: Marinate the chicken
steps: In a bowl, stir together the soy sauce, mirin, ginger and garlic.
Add the chicken and toss until every piece is coated.
Cover and refrigerate for 30 minutes, turning the pieces once halfway.

stages.title: Coat the chicken
steps: Tip the cornflour onto a large plate or tray.
Lift the chicken from the marinade, letting the excess drip off, and discard the leftover marinade.
Press each piece into the cornflour until thickly and evenly coated, then shake off the excess.

stages.title: Fry in batches
steps: Pour the vegetable oil into a large heavy-based pot so it is about 5 cm deep, and heat over medium-high heat to 170°C, or until a pinch of cornflour sizzles steadily.
Fry a third of the chicken for 5–6 minutes, turning occasionally, until deep golden and cooked through with no pink in the centre.
Lift the pieces onto a wire rack set over a tray. Return the oil to 170°C and fry the remaining chicken in two more batches.

stages.title: Season and serve
steps: Sprinkle the hot chicken with the salt.
Serve straight away with the lemon wedges for squeezing over.

tips: Marinating for no longer than 30 minutes keeps the chicken juicy without making it too salty from the soy.
Thigh meat stays tender in the hot oil, whereas breast tends to dry out.
Frying in batches keeps the oil temperature steady, so the coating turns crisp rather than greasy.
Draining on a rack rather than paper towel stops steam softening the underside of the crust.
variations: Add 1 tsp sesame oil to the marinade for a nuttier flavour.
Serve with Japanese-style mayonnaise mixed with a squeeze of lemon juice for dipping.
recipe.storage: Cool completely, then refrigerate in a sealed container for up to 3 days. Reheat on a tray in a 200°C (180°C fan) oven for 8–10 minutes until hot and crisp.

recipe.title: French Pommes Dauphinoise
recipe.summary: Paper-thin potatoes baked slowly in garlic-infused cream beneath a golden, bubbling crust.
ingredients: 1 kg potatoes, waxy such as Desiree or Nicola

stages.title: Prepare the potatoes and dish
steps: Heat the oven to 170°C (150°C fan).
Grease a 20 x 25 cm baking dish with half the butter.
Peel the potatoes and slice them 2–3 mm thick, keeping the starch by not rinsing them.
Pat the slices dry with a clean tea towel if they are wet.

stages.title: Warm the cream mixture
steps: Combine the cream, milk, garlic, thyme, nutmeg, salt and black pepper in a saucepan.
Warm over medium heat for 3–4 minutes, until steaming and just starting to bubble at the edges; do not let it boil.
Remove from the heat and taste the liquid, adding a little more salt if it seems bland.

stages.title: Layer and bake covered
steps: Arrange a third of the potato slices in overlapping layers in the dish.
Pour over a third of the warm cream mixture, then repeat the layers twice more, finishing with the cream.
Press the potatoes down so they are mostly submerged, then cover tightly with foil.
Bake for 50 minutes, until the potatoes are nearly tender when pierced with a knife.

stages.title: Brown the top
steps: Remove the foil and dot the top with the remaining butter.
Bake uncovered for 25 minutes, until the top is deep golden and the knife slides in with no resistance.

stages.title: Rest and serve
steps: Rest the dish for 15 minutes so the sauce thickens and the layers hold together.
Cut into portions and serve hot.

tips: Leave the sliced potatoes unrinsed because their surface starch thickens the cream as it bakes.
Warm the cream before pouring so the potatoes start cooking straight away and the sauce is less likely to split.
Cover the dish for the first stage so the potatoes steam through without the top drying out or browning too early.
A mandoline gives even slices, and even slices cook at the same rate.
variations: Scatter 60 g grated gruyere between the layers and over the top for the final uncovered bake.
Rub the dish with a cut garlic clove instead of crushing garlic into the cream for a milder garlic flavour.
recipe.storage: Refrigerate leftovers in a covered container for up to 2 days. Reheat portions in a 160°C (140°C fan) oven for 15–20 minutes, until hot through.

recipe.title: Italian Semifreddo
recipe.summary: Airy frozen vanilla cream folded with whipped eggs and studded with toasted hazelnuts.
ingredients: 80 g hazelnuts, toasted and roughly chopped

stages.title: Prepare the tin and hazelnuts
steps: Line a 1 litre loaf tin with baking paper, leaving an overhang on the long sides so you can lift the semifreddo out later.
Roughly chop the toasted hazelnuts and set aside.
Half-fill a medium saucepan with water and bring to a gentle simmer over low heat.

stages.title: Cook and whisk the egg mixture
steps: In a large heatproof bowl, whisk the eggs, caster sugar and salt together until combined.
Set the bowl over the pan of simmering water, making sure the base does not touch the water. Whisk constantly for 6–8 minutes, until the mixture is pale, thick and reaches 71°C on a thermometer.
Remove the bowl from the heat and beat with electric beaters on high for 5–6 minutes, until thick, glossy and completely cool to the touch.

stages.title: Whip the cream and fold together
steps: In a separate bowl, whip the thickened cream to soft peaks, so it holds its shape but still looks billowy.
Stir the vanilla extract into the cooled egg mixture.
Gently fold the egg mixture into the whipped cream in two batches, until just combined with no streaks of cream.
Fold in the chopped hazelnuts, keeping back a small handful if you want to scatter them on top.

stages.title: Freeze
steps: Pour the mixture into the lined tin and smooth the top with a spatula.
Fold the baking paper overhang over the top, or cover with plastic wrap, then freeze for at least 6 hours, until firm all the way through.

stages.title: Unmould and serve
steps: Lift the semifreddo out of the tin using the paper overhang and set it on a board.
Let it stand for 5 minutes at room temperature to soften slightly.
Slice with a knife dipped in hot water and wiped dry, and serve straight away.

tips: Heating the eggs to 71°C cooks them safely and makes a stable, thick base that holds the air for a smooth texture.
Cool the egg mixture completely before folding in the cream, or the warmth will deflate the cream and the semifreddo will freeze icy.
Whip the cream only to soft peaks; stiffer cream is hard to fold and can turn grainy.
A knife dipped in hot water gives clean slices without cracking the frozen surface.
variations: Swap the hazelnuts for toasted pistachios and add the finely grated zest of 1 lemon to the egg mixture.
Fold 80 g chopped dark chocolate through with the hazelnuts for a chocolate-hazelnut version.
recipe.storage: Keep wrapped in the freezer for up to 1 week. Do not refreeze once softened or sliced portions have melted.

recipe.title: French Salade Niçoise
recipe.summary: A Provençal salad of tuna, eggs, tomatoes, olives and green beans dressed with sharp Dijon vinaigrette.
ingredients: 2 x 125 g cans tuna in olive oil, drained

stages.title: Cook the eggs
steps: Half-fill a medium saucepan with water and bring to the boil over high heat.
Lower in the eggs and boil over medium-high heat for 9 minutes, until the yolks are firm and cooked through.
Meanwhile, fill a large bowl with cold water and ice. Transfer the eggs to the bowl with a spoon and cool for 5 minutes, then peel and cut into quarters.

stages.title: Blanch the beans
steps: Bring a medium saucepan of salted water to the boil over high heat.
Add the green beans and cook for 3–4 minutes, until bright green and just tender with a slight bite.
Drain, then plunge into a bowl of cold water for 2 minutes to stop the cooking. Drain well and pat dry.

stages.title: Make the dressing
steps: Put the dijon mustard, lemon juice, salt and black pepper in a small bowl.
Whisk in the olive oil, a little at a time, until the dressing is thick and emulsified.

stages.title: Assemble and serve
steps: Spread the lettuce over a large platter.
Arrange the green beans, cherry tomatoes, kalamata olives and tuna in separate groups on the lettuce.
Add the egg quarters, then drizzle with the dressing just before serving.

tips: Cooling the eggs in iced water stops the cooking, which prevents a grey ring around the yolk and makes them easier to peel.
Draining the beans well after blanching stops water diluting the dressing.
Tuna in olive oil is richer and more tender than tuna in brine, so it flakes into soft chunks on the platter.
Dress the salad just before serving so the lettuce stays crisp.
variations: Add 400 g boiled and sliced waxy potatoes, tossed in a spoonful of the dressing while warm.
Swap the canned tuna for 4 seared salmon fillets, cooked over medium-high heat for 3–4 minutes each side until the flesh flakes easily.
recipe.storage: Keep the components separate in the fridge for up to 1 day and dress just before serving. Not suitable for freezing.

recipe.title: Greek Revithia
recipe.summary: Slow-baked chickpeas with lemon, rosemary and olive oil until buttery-soft and fragrant.
ingredients: 2 x 400 g cans chickpeas, drained and rinsed

stages.title: Prepare the ingredients
steps: Heat the oven to 180°C (160°C fan).
Drain and rinse the chickpeas, then leave them to drain in a colander.
Thinly slice the onions and garlic.
Zest the lemon, then juice it and set both aside.

stages.title: Soften the onions
steps: Heat half the olive oil in a large ovenproof casserole over medium heat.
Add the onions and the salt and cook, stirring often, for 10 minutes until soft and golden.
Add the garlic, rosemary sprigs and bay leaf and cook for 1–2 minutes until fragrant.

stages.title: Bake covered
steps: Add the chickpeas, stock, black pepper and the remaining olive oil to the casserole and bring to a simmer over medium heat.
Cover with a lid and bake for 50 minutes, until the chickpeas are very tender and the liquid has thickened slightly.

stages.title: Reduce uncovered
steps: Remove the lid and bake for a further 15 minutes, until the top is lightly browned and the liquid is thick and glossy.
Remove the rosemary sprigs and bay leaf.

stages.title: Finish and serve
steps: Stir in the lemon juice and most of the zest, then taste and add more salt and pepper if needed.
Rest for 5 minutes, then spoon into bowls, scatter with the remaining zest and serve with bread.

tips: Slow-cooking the onions until golden builds sweetness that balances the lemon at the end.
Generous olive oil gives the chickpeas a silky, creamy sauce, so do not cut it back too far.
Adding the lemon juice off the heat keeps its flavour bright, as long cooking dulls it.
Rinsing canned chickpeas removes the tinny liquid and keeps the sauce clean tasting.
variations: Stir in 2 handfuls of baby spinach after baking and let it wilt in the heat for 2 minutes.
Replace the rosemary with 1 tsp dried oregano and add 1 tbsp tomato paste with the garlic.
recipe.storage: Cool, then refrigerate in a sealed container for up to 3 days or freeze for 2 months. Reheat in a saucepan over medium heat until steaming hot, adding a splash of water if thick.

recipe.title: Chinese Egg Drop Soup
recipe.summary: Silky ribbons of egg swirl through a light ginger-scented broth with spring onions and white pepper.

stages.title: Prepare the ingredients
steps: Thinly slice the ginger and spring onions, keeping the spring onions separate.
Crack the eggs into a jug and beat lightly with a fork until the yolks and whites are just combined.
Mix the cornflour with 2 tbsp water in a small bowl until smooth.

stages.title: Infuse the stock
steps: Pour the chicken stock and 250 ml water into a medium saucepan and add the ginger.
Bring to a simmer over medium heat, then reduce to medium-low and simmer gently for 8 minutes.
Lift out the ginger with a slotted spoon and discard it.
Stir in the black pepper and the salt.

stages.title: Thicken and add the egg
steps: Return the stock to a gentle simmer over medium heat. Stir the cornflour mixture again, then pour it in while stirring, and cook for 1 minute until the soup turns slightly glossy and thickens.
Reduce the heat to low. Stir the soup in one slow circular direction to create a gentle swirl.
Pour the beaten eggs in a thin stream into the moving soup, then stop stirring and leave for 30 seconds until the egg ribbons are set and opaque.

stages.title: Finish and serve
steps: Turn off the heat and stir in the sesame oil and most of the spring onions.
Ladle into bowls and scatter over the remaining spring onions.

tips: A thin, slow stream of egg into moving soup makes fine silky ribbons, while pouring it in fast gives clumps.
Keep the soup at a gentle simmer when adding the egg, because a hard boil breaks the egg into small cloudy bits.
The cornflour thickens the broth just enough to suspend the egg, so stir the slurry again right before adding it as it settles quickly.
Add the sesame oil off the heat, as it loses its aroma when cooked.
variations: Add 1 cup of corn kernels with the stock and simmer for 3 minutes for a sweet corn version.
Stir in 100 g of sliced mushrooms with the ginger and simmer until tender for extra body.
recipe.storage: Refrigerate in a sealed container for up to 2 days. Reheat gently in a saucepan over low heat until steaming hot, without boiling.

recipe.title: Italian Zuppa Toscana
recipe.summary: A hearty Tuscan-style soup of sausage, potatoes and kale in a lightly creamy garlic broth.
ingredients: 400 g potatoes, halved lengthways and sliced 5 mm thick
150 g kale, stems removed and leaves roughly torn

stages.title: Prepare the vegetables and sausage
steps: Squeeze the sausage meat out of the casings and discard the casings.
Finely chop the onion and garlic.
Slice the potatoes 5 mm thick, halving them lengthways first if large.
Strip the kale leaves from the stems and tear the leaves into bite-sized pieces.

stages.title: Brown the sausage and soften the onion
steps: Heat the olive oil in a large heavy-based pot over medium-high heat.
Add the sausage meat and cook for 6–8 minutes, breaking it into small chunks with a wooden spoon, until browned and no longer pink.
Reduce the heat to medium, add the onion and cook in the rendered fat for 3–4 minutes until soft.
Stir in the garlic and chilli flakes and cook for 1 minute until fragrant.

stages.title: Simmer the potatoes
steps: Add the potatoes, chicken stock and 250 ml water to the pot and stir, scraping up any browned bits from the base.
Bring to the boil over high heat, then reduce to medium-low.
Simmer, partly covered, for 12–15 minutes until the potato slices are tender when pierced with a knife.

stages.title: Add the kale and cream
steps: Stir in the kale and simmer over medium-low heat for 4–5 minutes until wilted and tender.
Pour in the thickened cream and warm for 2–3 minutes until steaming, without letting it boil.
Season with the salt and black pepper, then taste and add more if needed.
Ladle into bowls and serve hot.

tips: Browning the sausage well builds flavour, and the rendered fat then seasons the onion and the broth.
Slicing the potatoes evenly at 5 mm means they cook at the same rate and a few break down slightly to thicken the soup.
Keep the soup below a boil once the cream goes in, as boiling can make the cream split and look grainy.
Add the kale after the potatoes so it stays tender and green rather than turning dull and soft.
variations: Use hot Italian-style sausages and double the chilli flakes for a spicier soup.
Swap the kale for cavolo nero, cooking it for 6–7 minutes until tender.
recipe.storage: Refrigerate in a sealed container for up to 3 days. Reheat gently in a pot over medium-low heat until steaming hot, adding a splash of water if too thick. Not ideal to freeze as the potato and cream can turn grainy.

recipe.title: Irish Colcannon
recipe.summary: Buttery mashed potatoes folded with tender cabbage and spring onions for a comforting Irish classic.
ingredients: 800 g potatoes, peeled and cut into 4 cm chunks
70 g butter, plus extra for serving
1 tsp salt, plus extra for the cooking water

stages.title: Prepare the vegetables
steps: Peel the potatoes and cut them into 4 cm chunks so they cook evenly.
Remove the tough core from the cabbage and shred the leaves finely.
Thinly slice the spring onions, keeping the white and green parts together.

stages.title: Boil the potatoes
steps: Put the potatoes in a large pot, cover with cold water and add a good pinch of salt.
Bring to the boil over high heat, then reduce to medium and simmer for 15–20 minutes, until a knife slides into a chunk with no resistance.
Drain well in a colander and leave the potatoes to steam dry for 2 minutes.

stages.title: Cook the cabbage and milk
steps: While the potatoes simmer, melt 20 g of the butter in a large frying pan over medium heat.
Add the cabbage and 1/2 tsp of the salt and cook, stirring, for 5–6 minutes, until wilted and tender but still bright green.
Add the spring onions and cook for 1 minute, then remove the pan from the heat.
Warm the milk in a small saucepan over low heat for 1–2 minutes, until steaming but not boiling.

stages.title: Mash and serve
steps: Return the dry potatoes to the pot and mash with the remaining 50 g butter until smooth.
Stir in the warm milk, the pepper and the remaining 1/2 tsp salt until the mash is creamy.
Fold through the cabbage and spring onion mixture until evenly combined.
Spoon into a warm bowl, make a small well in the centre and add a knob of extra butter to melt.

tips: Letting the drained potatoes steam dry for 2 minutes stops the mash turning watery and lets it absorb the butter.
Warm milk keeps the mash hot and fluffy, while cold milk cools it and can make it gluey.
Cooking the cabbage in butter first removes its raw edge and gives a sweeter flavour than boiling it.
Mash by hand rather than in a food processor, which overworks the starch and makes the potato gluey.
variations: Swap the cabbage for shredded kale or cavolo nero, cooked for 1–2 minutes longer until tender.
Fry 3 rashers of chopped bacon until crisp and fold them through at the end for a smoky version.
recipe.storage: Refrigerate in an airtight container for up to 2 days. Reheat in a saucepan over low heat with a splash of milk, stirring, until steaming hot.

recipe.title: Lebanese Batata Harra
recipe.summary: Crisp roasted potatoes tossed with garlic, coriander, chilli and fresh lemon for a lively mezze side.
ingredients: 800 g potatoes, cut into 2 cm cubes
1 bunch coriander, leaves and tender stems roughly chopped

stages.title: Prepare the potatoes and herbs
steps: Peel the potatoes if you like, then cut them into 2 cm cubes so they cook evenly.
Finely chop the garlic and roughly chop the coriander leaves and tender stems.
Halve the lemon and set it aside, ready for juicing at the end.
Put the potatoes in a large pot and cover with cold water by about 3 cm.

stages.title: Parboil the potatoes
steps: Heat the oven to 220°C (200°C fan) and put a large baking tray inside to heat.
Add 1 tsp of the salt to the pot, bring to the boil over high heat, then reduce to medium and simmer for 6–8 minutes, until the edges are soft but the cubes still hold their shape.
Drain well in a colander and leave to steam dry for 3 minutes, shaking the colander once or twice to roughen the edges.

stages.title: Roast until crisp
steps: Toss the dry potatoes with 2 tbsp of the olive oil and the remaining 1/2 tsp salt.
Carefully tip them onto the hot tray in a single layer and roast for 20 minutes.
Turn the potatoes with a spatula and roast for another 12–15 minutes, until deep golden and crisp on the outside and tender in the middle.

stages.title: Fry the garlic and chilli, then toss
steps: While the potatoes finish, warm the remaining 2 tbsp olive oil in a small frying pan over medium heat for 1 minute.
Add the garlic and chilli flakes and cook, stirring, for 30–60 seconds, until fragrant and the garlic is just pale golden. Take off the heat straight away so it doesn't turn bitter.
Tip the hot potatoes into a large bowl, pour over the garlic and chilli oil, add the coriander and squeeze in the juice of the lemon. Toss and serve immediately.

tips: Parboiling and drying the potatoes before roasting gives a fluffy centre and a rough surface that crisps well in the oven.
Preheating the tray means the potatoes start sizzling the moment they land, which helps stop them sticking.
Adding the garlic to the oil at the end, not the oven, keeps its flavour fresh and avoids burnt, bitter bits.
Adding the coriander and lemon off the heat keeps the herbs bright and stops the potatoes going soggy while they wait.
variations: Stir through 1 tsp ground cumin with the garlic and chilli for a warmer, earthier flavour.
Swap the lemon juice for 1 tbsp pomegranate molasses if you have it, for a sweeter tang.
recipe.storage: Best eaten straight away while crisp. Leftovers keep in a sealed container in the fridge for up to 2 days; reheat on a tray in a 200°C (180°C fan) oven for 10 minutes until hot and crisp.

recipe.title: Moroccan Briouats with Almonds
recipe.summary: Crisp triangular pastries filled with fragrant almond paste, cinnamon and orange blossom, dipped in honey.

stages.title: Make the almond filling
steps: Heat the oven to 190°C (170°C fan) and line a large baking tray with baking paper.
Combine the ground almonds, icing sugar and ground cinnamon in a bowl.
Add the orange blossom water and 1 tbsp water, then stir and press until the mixture forms a firm, moist paste that holds together when squeezed.

stages.title: Cut and fill the filo
steps: Stack the filo sheets and cover with a damp tea towel so they don't dry out. Lay 1 sheet on the bench and cut it lengthwise into 3 equal strips, keeping the rest covered.
Brush a strip lightly with melted butter, then place 1 heaped teaspoon of filling on one end, about 2 cm from the edge.
Repeat with the remaining sheets, working one sheet at a time, to make 24 strips.

stages.title: Fold the triangles
steps: Fold the corner of the filled end over the filling to form a triangle, then keep folding the strip over itself, flag-style, along its length until you reach the end.
Brush the loose end with butter and tuck it under to seal. Place seam-side down on the lined tray.
Brush the tops of all the triangles with the remaining melted butter.

stages.title: Bake until golden
steps: Bake the triangles on the middle shelf for 15–18 minutes, until deep golden and crisp all over.
Transfer to a wire rack placed over a tray.

stages.title: Dip in honey
steps: Warm the honey with 1 tbsp water in a small saucepan over low heat for 2 minutes, until runny but not boiling.
Dip each warm triangle briefly in the honey, turning once, and lift out with tongs.
Drain on the rack for 5 minutes, until the honey is tacky and no longer dripping.

tips: Keeping the filo under a damp tea towel stops the thin sheets drying and cracking when folded.
A firm, moist paste holds its shape inside the pastry and won't leak out during baking.
Dipping the pastries while still warm lets the honey cling lightly without making the filo soggy.
variations: Add the finely grated zest of 1 orange to the almond paste for a brighter citrus note.
Sprinkle the honeyed triangles with toasted sesame seeds before the honey sets.
recipe.storage: Store in an airtight container at room temperature for up to 2 days. They soften over time, so re-crisp in a 160°C (140°C fan) oven for 5 minutes.

recipe.title: Italian Pasta e Ceci
recipe.summary: Chickpeas and small pasta simmered in a rosemary-scented tomato broth until thick and comforting.
ingredients: 180 g pasta, ditalini or other small shapes

stages.title: Prepare the base
steps: Drain and rinse the chickpeas well under cold running water, then set aside about 1/2 cup for garnish.
Finely chop the onion and garlic.
Strip the rosemary leaves from the sprig and chop them finely.

stages.title: Soften the aromatics
steps: Heat 2 tbsp of the olive oil in a large saucepan over medium heat.
Cook the onion and the salt, stirring often, for 8–10 minutes until soft and translucent but not browned.
Add the garlic and rosemary and cook, stirring, for 1 minute until fragrant.

stages.title: Simmer the chickpeas
steps: Add the passata, the larger portion of chickpeas and the vegetable stock, then bring to the boil over high heat.
Reduce the heat to medium-low and simmer, partly covered, for 15 minutes until the chickpeas are very tender.
Scoop out about 2 cups of the chickpeas and some liquid, blend with a stick blender or in a jug blender until smooth, then stir back into the pot.

stages.title: Cook the pasta
steps: Return the soup to a steady simmer over medium heat and add the pasta, stirring well.
Cook for 8–10 minutes, or according to the packet, stirring often so the pasta doesn't stick, until the pasta is al dente and the soup is thick; add a splash of hot water if it becomes too thick.
Season with black pepper and extra salt if needed.

stages.title: Rest and serve
steps: Remove from the heat and rest for 2 minutes so the soup thickens slightly.
Ladle into bowls and top with the reserved chickpeas, the remaining 1 tbsp olive oil and the parmesan, if using.

tips: Blending some of the chickpeas makes the broth creamy without any cream, giving the soup its traditional body.
Cooking the onion slowly without browning keeps the flavour sweet and balances the acidity of the passata.
The pasta keeps absorbing liquid as it rests, so serve promptly and loosen with hot water if the soup gets too thick.
Check the label on parmesan if serving vegetarians, as it is made with animal rennet.
variations: Stir in a handful of chopped silverbeet or kale for the last 5 minutes of cooking for added greens.
Add 1/2 tsp chilli flakes with the garlic for a gentle heat.
recipe.storage: Refrigerate in an airtight container for up to 3 days. The pasta will swell, so add a splash of water or stock when reheating over medium heat until steaming hot. Not ideal to freeze once the pasta is added.

recipe.title: Korean Hobak Jeon
recipe.summary: Tender courgette rounds coated in a light egg batter and pan-fried until delicately golden.

stages.title: Salt the zucchini
steps: Cut the zucchini into 5 mm rounds and lay them in a single layer on a tray lined with paper towel.
Sprinkle the rounds evenly with the salt and leave for 10 minutes to draw out moisture.
Pat both sides of each round dry with more paper towel.

stages.title: Set up the coating and dipping sauce
steps: Spread the plain flour in a shallow dish.
Lightly beat the eggs in a second shallow dish until the yolks and whites are combined.
Stir the soy sauce and rice vinegar together in a small bowl to make the dipping sauce.

stages.title: Coat and pan-fry
steps: Heat 2 teaspoons of the vegetable oil in a large non-stick frypan over medium heat.
Dip each zucchini round in the flour, shake off the excess, then coat in the egg.
Fry a batch in a single layer for 2–3 minutes per side, until golden and the egg is set.
Transfer to a paper towel-lined plate, then wipe the pan and add 2 teaspoons more oil before each of the remaining batches, cooking all rounds the same way.

stages.title: Serve
steps: Arrange the warm jeon on a plate.
Serve with the soy and rice vinegar dipping sauce.

tips: Salting and drying the zucchini removes water, so the egg coating sticks and the rounds fry golden instead of steaming.
Shake off excess flour before dipping, or the coating turns pasty and peels away in the pan.
Keep the heat at medium; higher heat browns the egg before the zucchini softens.
variations: Add 1 finely sliced red chilli and a pinch of sesame seeds to the dipping sauce for heat and nuttiness.
Use rounds of eggplant cut 8 mm thick, frying 3–4 minutes per side until tender.
recipe.storage: Refrigerate in an airtight container for up to 2 days. Reheat in a frypan over medium heat for 1–2 minutes per side until hot through; the coating will be softer than when fresh.

recipe.title: Vietnamese Che Ba Mau
recipe.summary: Colourful layers of sweet beans, pandan jelly and coconut milk served over crushed ice.
ingredients: 150 g pandan jelly, cut into 1 cm strips

stages.title: Sweeten the red beans
steps: Combine the red beans, 3 tbsp of the sugar and 100 ml water in a small saucepan.
Simmer over medium-low heat for 8–10 minutes, stirring occasionally, until the liquid is syrupy and the beans are glossy.
Tip into a bowl and leave to cool to room temperature.

stages.title: Sweeten the mung beans
steps: Combine the mung beans, 3 tbsp of the sugar and 100 ml water in a second small saucepan.
Simmer over medium-low heat for 8–10 minutes, stirring gently so the beans stay whole, until the liquid has thickened and coated them.
Tip into a bowl and leave to cool to room temperature.

stages.title: Make the coconut sauce
steps: Whisk the cornflour with 2 tbsp water in a small saucepan until smooth, then add the coconut milk, the remaining sugar and the salt.
Heat over medium heat for 3–4 minutes, stirring constantly, until the sauce thickens slightly and coats the back of a spoon. Do not let it boil hard.
Pour into a jug and cool for 5 minutes.

stages.title: Chill the components
steps: Cover the red beans, mung beans and coconut sauce separately.
Refrigerate for at least 20 minutes, until cold.
Keep the pandan jelly strips in the fridge until assembling.

stages.title: Assemble and serve
steps: Divide the mung beans among 4 tall glasses, then add a layer of red beans.
Top with the pandan jelly strips.
Pack in the crushed ice, pressing it down lightly.
Pour the cold coconut sauce over the ice and serve straight away with long spoons, stirring the layers together as you eat.

tips: Cooking each bean separately keeps the colours distinct and lets you control how sweet each layer is.
Cornflour gives the coconut sauce body so it clings to the ice instead of sinking and diluting.
Chilling every component first slows the ice melting, so the dessert stays thick rather than watery.
Simmer the mung beans gently, because hard bubbling breaks them up and clouds the layer.
variations: Swap the pandan jelly for grass jelly or cubes of mango.
Top with roasted crushed peanuts for crunch.
recipe.storage: Keep the beans, jelly and coconut sauce in separate airtight containers in the fridge for up to 3 days. Assemble with fresh ice just before serving.

recipe.title: French Gougeres
recipe.summary: Airy choux pastry puffs with nutty Gruyère and a delicate crisp shell.

stages.title: Prepare the trays and cheese
steps: Heat the oven to 200°C (180°C fan) and line two large baking trays with baking paper.
Finely grate 120 g gruyere, then set aside 2 tbsp of it for sprinkling on top.
Sift the flour onto a sheet of baking paper so it can be tipped into the pan in one go.

stages.title: Cook the choux paste
steps: Combine the water, milk, butter and salt in a medium saucepan over medium heat, stirring until the butter melts, then bring to a rolling boil.
Remove the pan from the heat and tip in the flour all at once. Beat hard with a wooden spoon until the mixture is smooth and comes away from the sides of the pan.
Return the pan to low heat and stir for 1–2 minutes, until a thin film forms on the base of the pan.
Transfer the paste to a bowl and cool for 5 minutes, until warm but not hot.

stages.title: Beat in the eggs and cheese
steps: Lightly whisk the eggs in a jug. Beat about one-third into the paste until fully combined and glossy.
Add the remaining egg in 2 more batches, beating well each time, until the paste is smooth and falls slowly from the spoon in a thick ribbon. You may not need all the egg.
Stir in the grated gruyere (except the reserved 2 tbsp), the nutmeg and a few grinds of black pepper.

stages.title: Pipe and bake
steps: Spoon the mixture into a piping bag with a 1 cm plain nozzle, or use two spoons. Pipe or spoon walnut-sized mounds onto the trays, 4 cm apart.
Dab down any peaks with a wet finger, then sprinkle the reserved cheese over the tops.
Bake for 10 minutes without opening the oven door. Reduce the temperature to 180°C (160°C fan) and bake for another 15–20 minutes, until puffed, deep golden and crisp.
Pierce the side of each gougere with a skewer to release steam, then return to the switched-off oven for 5 minutes to dry out. Serve warm.

tips: Beat the eggs in gradually: too much egg makes a loose paste that spreads and won't puff, so stop when it drops slowly from the spoon.
Cooking the paste briefly on the heat dries it out, which gives a crisper shell and a better rise.
Keep the oven door shut for the first 10 minutes, as the steam that lifts the puffs collapses if the oven cools.
Finely grated cheese melts evenly into the paste without blocking the piping nozzle.
variations: Replace the nutmeg with 1 tsp dijon mustard beaten in with the cheese for a sharper flavour.
Use cheddar cheese instead of gruyere and add 1 tbsp chopped chives.
recipe.storage: Store cooled gougeres in an airtight container for up to 2 days, or freeze for up to 1 month. Reheat at 180°C (160°C fan) for 5–8 minutes until crisp and hot through.

recipe.title: Brazilian Pao de Queijo
recipe.summary: Chewy, golden cheese rolls made with tapioca starch and Parmesan, crisp outside and stretchy within.

stages.title: Heat the oven and prepare the tin
steps: Heat the oven to 200°C (180°C fan).
Brush a 12-hole mini muffin tin with 1 tsp of the vegetable oil, keeping the remaining oil for the dough.
Tip the tapioca starch into a large heatproof bowl.

stages.title: Scald the starch
steps: Combine the milk, the remaining vegetable oil and the salt in a small saucepan.
Heat over medium heat for 3–4 minutes, until steaming and small bubbles form around the edge. Do not let it boil hard.
Pour the hot liquid over the tapioca starch and stir with a wooden spoon until no dry patches remain and the mixture looks shaggy and slightly translucent.

stages.title: Cool and finish the dough
steps: Leave the mixture to cool for about 10 minutes, until warm to the touch rather than hot, so it won't cook the egg.
Add the egg and beat vigorously with the spoon or your hands for 2–3 minutes, until the egg is absorbed and the dough is smooth and very sticky.
Add the parmesan and mix until evenly combined and stretchy.
Wet your hands and roll the dough into 12 balls about the size of a golf ball, then place one in each muffin hole.

stages.title: Bake and rest
steps: Bake on the middle shelf for 20–22 minutes, until puffed, deep golden and set. They should feel light, with a crisp shell and a soft, chewy centre.
Rest in the tin for 3 minutes, then lift out and serve warm.

tips: Letting the scalded mixture cool before adding the egg stops the egg scrambling and keeps the dough smooth.
Finely grated parmesan melts into the dough evenly; coarse shreds leave pockets that leak and brown too fast.
Wet hands stop the sticky dough clinging to your fingers when you roll the balls.
Serve warm, as the centres go dense once cold; a quick re-bake brings back the crisp shell.
variations: Replace half the parmesan with grated mozzarella for a stretchier, milder centre.
Add 1 tsp finely chopped chives or a pinch of chilli flakes to the dough with the cheese.
recipe.storage: Refrigerate in an airtight container for up to 3 days. Reheat on a tray in a 180°C (160°C fan) oven for 6–8 minutes, until hot and crisp outside. Raw shaped balls can be frozen and baked from frozen for 5–8 minutes longer.

recipe.title: Italian Sbrisolona
recipe.summary: Crumbly almond shortbread from Mantua with a sandy texture and buttery toasted edges.
ingredients: 150 g almonds, finely chopped, or ground almonds
170 g cold butter, cut into 1 cm cubes, plus extra for greasing

stages.title: Prepare the tin and oven
steps: Heat the oven to 170°C (150°C fan).
Grease a 24 cm round springform tin with a little extra butter and line the base with baking paper.

stages.title: Make the crumb mixture
steps: Combine the plain flour, polenta, almonds, caster sugar, lemon zest and salt in a large bowl.
Add the cold butter and rub it in with your fingertips until the mixture forms coarse, uneven crumbs with some pea-sized lumps.
Add the egg yolks and toss through with a fork until the mixture clumps in places but stays crumbly. Do not knead it smooth.

stages.title: Fill the tin
steps: Scatter the crumbs loosely into the prepared tin.
Press very lightly with your palm so the surface is just even, keeping the texture rough.

stages.title: Bake
steps: Bake in the centre of the oven for 35–40 minutes, until deep golden on top and the edges are lightly browned.
Check that the centre looks dry and set, with no pale, raw patches.

stages.title: Cool and serve
steps: Cool the cake in the tin for 30 minutes so it firms up and can be handled.
Remove the side of the tin and break the sbrisolona into rustic pieces with your hands or the back of a knife.

tips: Cold butter rubbed in unevenly gives the crumbly, short texture the cake is known for. Warm butter makes it dense and greasy.
Leave the mixture lumpy and press only lightly, because overworking it forms a smooth dough and loses the crunchy crumb.
Polenta adds the characteristic grit and crunch. Use fine or regular polenta, not instant, for the best bite.
Cooling in the tin lets the butter set, so the cake breaks into pieces rather than collapsing into loose crumbs.
variations: Replace 50 g of the almonds with roughly chopped hazelnuts for a toastier flavour.
Add 1 tsp vanilla extract with the egg yolks for a softer, rounder flavour.
recipe.storage: Store in an airtight container at room temperature for up to 5 days. Keep it dry, as it softens in the fridge.

recipe.title: Spanish Crema Catalana
recipe.summary: Silky citrus-and-cinnamon custard topped with a brittle layer of caramelised sugar.
ingredients: 1 lemon, peel only, removed in wide strips
1 orange, peel only, removed in wide strips

stages.title: Infuse the milk
steps: Remove the peel from the lemon and orange in wide strips with a vegetable peeler, avoiding the bitter white pith.
Combine the milk, cinnamon stick, lemon peel and orange peel in a medium saucepan.
Heat over medium heat for 3–4 minutes until steaming and small bubbles form at the edge, then remove from the heat.
Cover and leave to steep for 10 minutes, then strain into a jug and discard the cinnamon and peel.

stages.title: Make the custard base
steps: Place the egg yolks, 60 g of the caster sugar and the cornflour in a medium heatproof bowl.
Whisk for 1–2 minutes until pale and smooth, with no lumps of cornflour.
Slowly pour in the warm infused milk while whisking constantly so the yolks do not scramble.

stages.title: Cook the custard
steps: Pour the mixture back into the clean saucepan and place over low heat.
Stir constantly with a whisk or wooden spoon, scraping the base and corners, for 6–8 minutes until it thickens and coats the back of a spoon.
Let it bubble gently for 1 minute to cook out the cornflour, then remove from the heat.
Divide the custard among four 150 ml ramekins or shallow dishes.

stages.title: Chill until set
steps: Cool the ramekins on the bench for 20 minutes.
Cover the surface of each custard with plastic wrap to prevent a skin forming.
Refrigerate for at least 3 hours until completely cold and firm.

stages.title: Caramelise and serve
steps: Remove the plastic wrap and blot any moisture from the surface with a paper towel.
Sprinkle the remaining 30 g caster sugar evenly over the custards in a thin layer.
