Heat the sugar with a kitchen torch for 1–2 minutes per custard until melted and deep golden brown.
Rest for 2 minutes until the caramel hardens, then serve straight away.

tips: Stirring constantly over low heat stops the yolks scrambling and keeps the custard smooth.
Peel without white pith, as pith makes the infusion bitter.
Drying the surface before adding sugar helps it melt into an even, crisp layer instead of dissolving into a wet patch.
Caramelise just before serving; the crust softens as it sits on the custard.
variations: Add a strip of lime peel or a split vanilla bean to the milk for a different aroma.
Use a very hot grill instead of a torch, placing the ramekins in a tray of ice to keep the custard cold.
recipe.storage: Keep the uncaramelised custards covered in the fridge for up to 3 days. Caramelise just before serving; do not freeze.

recipe.title: Peruvian Causa Limena
recipe.summary: Chilled lime-and-chilli mashed potato layers filled with creamy tuna and avocado.
ingredients: 800 g yellow potatoes, peeled and cut into 3 cm chunks
2 x 185 g cans canned tuna, drained

stages.title: Cook the potatoes
steps: Put the potatoes in a large pot, cover with cold water, add 1/2 tsp of the salt and bring to the boil over high heat.
Reduce to medium heat and simmer for 15–18 minutes, until a knife slides into a chunk with no resistance.
Drain well and let the potatoes steam dry in the colander for 3 minutes.

stages.title: Make the potato layer
steps: Mash the warm potatoes until completely smooth, or push them through a potato ricer.
Squeeze the juice of 2 limes and stir it into the potato with the aji amarillo paste, olive oil and the remaining 1/2 tsp salt.
Taste and add more salt if needed, then knead briefly until the mixture is smooth and holds together like a soft dough.

stages.title: Make the tuna filling
steps: Combine the tuna, mayonnaise, spring onions, the juice of the remaining lime and black pepper in a bowl.
Flake the tuna with a fork and mix until creamy.

stages.title: Layer the causa
steps: Line a 20 cm square dish or four 9 cm ring moulds with baking paper or plastic wrap, leaving some overhang.
Press half the potato mixture into the base in an even layer, smoothing the top with a wet spoon.
Spread the tuna filling over the potato, then arrange the avocado slices on top.
Press the remaining potato mixture over the avocado and smooth the surface.

stages.title: Chill and serve
steps: Cover and refrigerate for at least 45 minutes, until the causa is firm and cold.
Lift out using the overhang or slide off the moulds, cut into 4 portions with a sharp knife wiped clean between cuts, and serve cold.

tips: Mash the potatoes while hot, as cooled potato turns gluey and will not give a smooth layer.
Yellow, waxy-fleshed potatoes such as Nicola or Gold give the right buttery colour and texture; floury varieties can turn crumbly.
Wetting your spoon or hands stops the potato sticking when you smooth the layers.
Squeeze out the tuna well so the filling does not make the layers wet and slippery.
variations: Replace the tuna with shredded cooked chicken mixed with mayonnaise and a little extra lime juice.
Add a layer of finely diced tomato or sliced hard-boiled egg between the tuna and avocado.
recipe.storage: Cover and refrigerate for up to 2 days. Serve cold; do not freeze, as the potato turns grainy and the avocado browns.

recipe.title: Japanese Chawanmushi
recipe.summary: Delicate savoury egg custard steamed with dashi, mushrooms and prawns until barely set.
ingredients: 450 ml dashi stock, cooled to room temperature
4 shiitake mushrooms, stems removed and caps thinly sliced
100 g cooked prawns, peeled and roughly chopped

stages.title: Prepare the custard base
steps: Crack the eggs into a jug and whisk gently with a fork, lifting the fork rather than beating, so no foam forms.
Stir in the cooled dashi stock, the soy sauce and the mirin until combined.
Pour the mixture through a fine sieve into a clean jug to remove any stringy egg white and bubbles.

stages.title: Cook the mushrooms and fill the cups
steps: Heat the vegetable oil in a small frying pan over medium heat.
Cook the sliced shiitake mushrooms, stirring often, for 2–3 minutes until softened and lightly golden, then cool for 2 minutes.
Divide the mushrooms and chopped prawns among four heatproof cups or ramekins of about 200 ml capacity.
Pour the strained custard evenly over the fillings, skimming off any surface bubbles with a spoon.

stages.title: Steam the custards
steps: Cover each cup tightly with foil to stop condensation dripping onto the custard.
Bring about 2 cm of water to a boil in a large lidded pan or wok, then set a steaming rack inside and reduce the heat to low so the water barely simmers.

Stand the cups on the rack, cover with the lid slightly ajar, and steam for 15–20 minutes until the custard is just set with a slight wobble and the juices run clear when a skewer is inserted in the centre.

stages.title: Rest and serve
steps: Lift the cups out carefully and rest them for 3 minutes, uncovered.
Scatter the sliced spring onion over the top and serve warm with a spoon.

tips: Straining the egg mixture gives a silky, smooth custard because it removes strings of egg white and trapped air.
Cool the dashi before mixing, as hot stock will partly cook the eggs and leave the custard lumpy.
Keep the water at a bare simmer; a hard boil makes tiny holes and a rubbery texture in the custard.
Leaving the lid slightly ajar lets some steam escape, which keeps the temperature gentle and the surface smooth.
variations: Replace the prawns with 100 g shredded cooked chicken thigh and add a few blanched edamame to each cup.
Top each cooked custard with a spoonful of thickened dashi, made by simmering 100 ml dashi with 1 tsp soy sauce and 1 tsp cornflour mixed with a little water until glossy.
recipe.storage: Cool, cover and refrigerate for up to 2 days. Reheat gently, covered, in a steamer for 5–8 minutes until hot through. Don't freeze.

recipe.title: French Socca
recipe.summary: Thin chickpea-flour flatbread baked until blistered, with crisp edges and a peppery olive-oil finish.

stages.title: Make the batter
steps: Sift the chickpea flour and the salt into a large bowl.
Gradually pour in 300 ml water, whisking until completely smooth with no lumps.
Whisk in 1 tbsp of the olive oil.

stages.title: Rest the batter
steps: Cover the bowl and leave the batter at room temperature for 30 minutes so the flour hydrates.
Skim off any foam from the surface with a spoon before cooking.

stages.title: Heat the pan
steps: While the batter rests, place a 28 cm cast-iron frying pan on the middle oven rack and heat the oven to 250°C (230°C fan), or its highest setting, for at least 5 minutes until the pan is very hot.
Switch the oven grill on to high as well if your oven has one.

stages.title: Cook the socca
steps: Wearing oven mitts, carefully remove the hot pan and add 1 tbsp of the olive oil, swirling to coat the base.
Pour in the batter straight away so it forms a thin layer about 3 mm thick.
Return the pan to the oven and cook for 6–8 minutes, until the edges are crisp and the top is blistered, firm and golden in patches.

stages.title: Finish and serve
steps: Brush the top with the remaining 1 tbsp olive oil and sprinkle over the black pepper.
Loosen the socca with a spatula, slide it onto a board and cut into wedges.
Serve while hot and crisp at the edges.

tips: Resting the batter lets the chickpea flour absorb the water fully, giving a creamy centre instead of a gritty one.
A very hot pan sets the batter on contact, which is what creates the crisp, blistered edges.
Pour a thin layer; thick batter stays gummy in the middle before the top colours.
variations: Stir 1 tbsp chopped rosemary or thyme into the batter for a more traditional Niçoise flavour.
Top the cooked socca with crumbled feta and a handful of rocket just before serving.
recipe.storage: Refrigerate in an airtight container for up to 2 days. Reheat in a 200°C (180°C fan) oven for 5–8 minutes until hot and crisp. Not suitable for freezing.

recipe.title: Greek Skordalia
recipe.summary: A punchy garlic-and-potato dip whipped with olive oil and lemon until creamy and smooth.
ingredients: 500 g potatoes, peeled and cut into 3 cm chunks

stages.title: Prepare the potatoes
steps: Peel the potatoes and cut them into even 3 cm chunks so they cook at the same rate.
Put the potatoes in a medium saucepan and cover with cold water by about 3 cm.
Add 1/2 tsp of the salt to the water.

stages.title: Make the garlic paste
steps: Put the garlic and the remaining 1/2 tsp salt in a mortar.
Pound with the pestle until it forms a smooth, sticky paste with no visible pieces, or crush it with the flat of a knife on a board.
Juice the lemon and set the juice aside.

stages.title: Boil the potatoes
steps: Bring the potatoes to the boil over high heat, then reduce to medium heat and simmer for 15–20 minutes, until a knife slides in with no resistance and the edges begin to crumble.
Drain well in a colander.
Return the potatoes to the dry hot pan off the heat for 2 minutes so the steam escapes and they dry out.

stages.title: Mash and beat in the flavours
steps: Mash the warm potatoes with a masher or potato ricer until completely smooth.
Stir in the garlic paste until evenly combined.
Beat in the olive oil a tablespoon at a time, waiting until each addition is absorbed, until the mixture is thick, creamy and glossy.
Stir in the lemon juice, then taste and add a little more salt or lemon if needed. Stop mixing as soon as it is smooth, as overworking turns it gluey.

stages.title: Serve
steps: Spoon the skordalia into a shallow bowl and drizzle with a little extra olive oil if you like.
Serve warm or at room temperature with fried or roasted vegetables, or grilled fish.

tips: Dry the drained potatoes in the hot pan, because leftover water makes the skordalia loose and stops it absorbing the oil.
Mash the potatoes while still hot, as cold potato turns gluey and hard to smooth out.
Add the oil slowly so it emulsifies into the potato, giving a creamy rather than greasy texture.
Pounding the garlic with salt breaks it down fully, which avoids harsh raw chunks in the finished dip.
variations: Replace half the potato with 100 g of soaked, squeezed day-old bread for a more traditional, lighter skordalia.
Stir in 50 g of finely ground walnuts or almonds with the oil for a nutty, richer version.
recipe.storage: Refrigerate in an airtight container for up to 2 days. Bring to room temperature and stir in a splash of olive oil or water to loosen before serving. Not suitable for freezing.

recipe.title: Portuguese Bifana
recipe.summary: Thin pork steaks simmered in garlicky white-wine sauce and tucked into crusty bread rolls.
ingredients: 500 g pork loin, trimmed and sliced 5 mm thick

stages.title: Slice and pound the pork
steps: Cut the pork loin across the grain into slices about 5 mm thick, giving 8 or so slices.
Place the slices between sheets of baking paper and pound lightly with a rolling pin to an even 3 mm thickness.
Crush the garlic cloves with the flat of a knife and a pinch of the salt until pasty.

stages.title: Marinate
steps: In a non-metallic bowl, combine the garlic paste, the remaining salt, black pepper, paprika, bay leaves, white wine and 1 tbsp of the olive oil.
Add the pork and turn to coat every slice.
Cover and refrigerate for 30 minutes, turning once halfway.

stages.title: Sear and simmer
steps: Lift the pork from the marinade, keeping the marinade and bay leaves, and pat the slices dry with paper towel.
Heat the remaining 1 tbsp olive oil in a large frying pan over high heat.
Sear the pork in 2 batches for 1 minute per side until browned, then set aside.
Pour the marinade and bay leaves into the pan and simmer over medium heat for 3–4 minutes until reduced by half.
Return the pork and any juices to the pan and simmer for 2 minutes until cooked through with no pink remaining.

stages.title: Assemble
steps: Warm the bread rolls in a 160°C (140°C fan) oven for 3–4 minutes until the crust is crisp and the centre is soft.
Remove the bay leaves from the pan sauce.
Fill each roll with the pork and spoon over some sauce so it soaks into the bread.

tips: Pounding the pork thin means it cooks in minutes and stays tender instead of turning tough.
Patting the marinated pork dry before searing lets it brown rather than steam in the wine.
Dipping the cut sides of the rolls in the pan sauce is traditional and keeps the bread from tasting dry.
variations: Add a pinch of chilli flakes to the marinade for a gentle heat.
Serve with a smear of Dijon mustard in the roll, as is common in Portuguese cafes.
recipe.storage: Refrigerate the pork and sauce separately in an airtight container for up to 2 days. Reheat in a pan over medium heat until steaming hot, and fill fresh rolls just before serving.

recipe.title: Italian Frittata di Zucchine
recipe.summary: A tender courgette-and-Parmesan omelette with golden edges and fresh basil.

stages.title: Prepare the vegetables and eggs
steps: Slice the zucchini into thin rounds about 3 mm thick and thinly slice the onion.
Crack the eggs into a large bowl and whisk with a fork until the yolks and whites are combined.
Stir in the parmesan, the salt, the pepper and half the torn basil leaves.

stages.title: Cook the onion and zucchini
steps: Heat the oil in a 24 cm non-stick ovenproof frying pan over medium heat.
Add the onion and cook, stirring occasionally, for 4 minutes until soft and translucent.
Add the zucchini and cook, stirring often, for 8 minutes until golden at the edges and the moisture has evaporated from the pan.

stages.title: Set the frittata
steps: Heat the grill to high with the rack positioned about 15 cm from the element.
Spread the vegetables evenly over the base of the pan and reduce the heat to medium-low.
Pour in the egg mixture and cook for 5 minutes, without stirring, until the edges are set and the centre is still slightly wet.
Place the pan under the grill for 2–3 minutes until the top is golden and the centre is set and no longer wobbles.

stages.title: Rest and serve
steps: Rest the frittata in the pan for 3 minutes so it firms up for slicing.
Scatter the remaining basil over the top and cut into 4 wedges.

tips: Cooking the zucchini until the moisture has evaporated stops the frittata turning watery and helps it hold its shape when sliced.
Use a pan with an ovenproof handle, as a plastic handle will melt under the grill.
Cooking the base over low heat prevents the underside from browning too fast before the top sets.
variations: Add 100 g crumbled feta over the zucchini before pouring in the eggs for a saltier, tangier frittata.
Swap the basil for 2 tbsp chopped mint and add a pinch of chilli flakes with the onion.
recipe.storage: Cool completely, then refrigerate in an airtight container for up to 2 days. Eat cold or reheat gently in a 160°C (140°C fan) oven for 10 minutes until warmed through.

recipe.title: German Rote Grutze
recipe.summary: Glossy summer berries gently thickened into a ruby fruit pudding, served with cold vanilla cream.

stages.title: Prepare the fruit and slurry
steps: Set aside a handful (about 100 g) of the berries in the fridge to fold in at the end; leave them to thaw.
Finely grate the zest from the lemons to give 1 tsp.
Whisk the cornflour with 3 tbsp cold water in a small bowl until smooth.

stages.title: Simmer the berries
steps: Combine the cherry juice, caster sugar and lemon zest in a medium saucepan over medium heat and stir until the sugar dissolves, about 2 minutes.
Add the remaining berries and bring to a gentle simmer over medium heat.
Simmer for 5 minutes, stirring occasionally, until the berries are soft and have released their juices.

stages.title: Thicken
steps: Reduce the heat to medium-low and stir the cornflour mixture again, as it settles quickly.
Pour it into the simmering fruit while stirring constantly.
Cook for 1–2 minutes, stirring, until the mixture turns glossy and coats the back of a spoon.
Remove from the heat and gently fold in the reserved berries.

stages.title: Cool and chill
steps: Spoon the grutze into four serving glasses or bowls.
Cool at room temperature for 30 minutes.
Cover and chill for at least 2 hours, until cold and softly set.

stages.title: Serve
steps: Pour the thickened cream into a jug.
Serve the grutze cold, with the cream poured over or alongside.

tips: Reserving some berries and folding them in off the heat keeps a few pieces whole, so the dessert has texture as well as a smooth jelly.
Whisk the cornflour into cold water first so it doesn't form lumps when it meets the hot juice.
Boil the cornflour for a full minute or two, otherwise the grutze tastes starchy and can set loosely.
variations: Replace the cherry juice with red grape or blackcurrant juice, and reduce the sugar slightly if the juice is sweetened.
Serve with vanilla custard or cold milk instead of the cream, as is common in northern Germany.
recipe.storage: Cover and refrigerate for up to 3 days. Serve cold; the cream is best poured on just before serving. Not suitable to freeze, as it turns watery when thawed.

recipe.title: Moroccan Baghrir
recipe.summary: Soft semolina pancakes dotted with tiny holes that soak up warm honey and melted butter.

stages.title: Make the batter
steps: Add the semolina, plain flour, instant yeast, baking powder and salt to a blender.
Pour in 450 ml warm water and blend for 2 minutes until completely smooth and the consistency of thin pouring cream.
Pour the batter into a large jug, scraping down the blender.

stages.title: Rest the batter
steps: Cover the jug with a clean tea towel and leave in a warm spot for 30 minutes.
The batter is ready when the surface is foamy and has risen slightly with bubbles on top.
Stir gently once; do not beat out the bubbles.

stages.title: Cook the baghrir
steps: Heat a non-stick frying pan over medium heat for 2 minutes. Lightly wipe the pan with the vegetable oil on a paper towel, using only a thin film.
Pour in about 80 ml (1/3 cup) batter and swirl gently to make a round about 12 cm wide.
Cook on one side only for 2–3 minutes, until the surface is covered in small holes and no longer wet or shiny. Do not flip.
Slide the pancake onto a clean tea towel, holes facing up, and repeat with the remaining batter, wiping the pan with oil between batches only if it starts to stick. You should get about 12 pancakes.

stages.title: Make the honey butter and serve
steps: Melt the butter with the honey in a small saucepan over low heat for 2 minutes, stirring until combined and runny.
Stack the cooled pancakes in layers without pressing down, spotted side up.
Drizzle the warm honey butter over the pancakes and serve straight away.

tips: Blending for a full 2 minutes aerates the batter, which helps create the characteristic holes on the surface.
Cook on one side only; flipping closes the holes that soak up the honey butter and makes the pancake dense.
Keep the pan at medium heat: too hot and the base browns before the top sets, too cool and the bubbles fail to form.
Cool the pancakes in a single layer before stacking so the spotted tops stay dry and don't turn gluey.
variations: Swap the honey butter for a drizzle of olive oil and a spoonful of ground cinnamon-sweetened yoghurt.
Serve with warm honey and sliced almonds scattered over for crunch.
recipe.storage: Cool completely, layer with baking paper and refrigerate in an airtight container for up to 2 days or freeze for up to 1 month. Reheat in a toaster or covered in a 160°C (140°C fan) oven for 5 minutes until warmed through.

recipe.title: Chinese Sesame Balls
recipe.summary: Crisp golden glutinous-rice balls coated in sesame seeds with a sweet red-bean centre.

stages.title: Make the dough
steps: Stir the sugar into 150 ml warm water in a jug until the sugar dissolves completely.
Put the glutinous rice flour in a large bowl and pour in the sugar water a little at a time, mixing with your hand.
Knead for 2–3 minutes until the dough is smooth, soft and no longer sticks to your hands. If it cracks, knead in 1 tsp more water; if it sticks, knead in a little more flour.
Cover the bowl with a damp tea towel so the dough does not dry out.

stages.title: Fill and shape the balls
steps: Divide the red bean paste into 16 portions of about 10 g and roll each into a small ball.
Divide the dough into 16 equal pieces of about 25 g and roll each into a ball.
Flatten one dough ball into a disc about 6 cm wide, place a ball of red bean paste in the centre and fold the dough up around it.
Pinch the edges together to seal with no gaps, then roll between your palms until smooth and round.
Lightly moisten each ball with wet fingers, then roll it in the sesame seeds until evenly coated and press gently so the seeds stick.

stages.title: Fry the sesame balls
steps: Pour the oil into a deep heavy-based saucepan or wok and heat over medium-low heat to 150–160°C. A sesame seed dropped in should sizzle gently, not brown at once.
Fry 5–6 balls at a time, so the oil does not cool, for 6–8 minutes, turning gently with a slotted spoon, until the balls puff, float and are evenly golden brown.
Use the back of the spoon to press each ball very gently against the side of the pan as it fries to help it expand evenly.
Lift out with the slotted spoon and drain on a wire rack or paper towel. Return the oil to 150–160°C between batches.

stages.title: Cool and serve
steps: Rest the sesame balls for 5 minutes, as the red bean filling will be very hot inside.
Serve warm while the shells are crisp and the centres are soft and chewy.

tips: Glutinous rice flour gives the chewy texture, and regular rice flour will not work as a substitute.
Sealing the dough without gaps keeps the filling from bursting out, which would spatter hot oil.
Frying at a gentle 150–160°C lets the balls cook through and expand before the sesame seeds darken. Hotter oil browns the outside while the dough stays dense.
Roll the balls in the seeds while they are still slightly damp so the seeds stick and don't fall off in the oil.
variations: Swap the red bean paste for black sesame paste, or for a filling of 2 tbsp peanut butter mixed with 1 tbsp icing sugar.
Roll the dough balls in desiccated coconut instead of sesame seeds for a milder coating.
recipe.storage: Best eaten the day they are fried. Keep leftovers in an airtight container in the fridge for up to 2 days and reheat in a 160°C (140°C fan) oven for 8–10 minutes until hot through; they will be less crisp.

recipe.title: Greek Fasolakia Lathera
recipe.summary: Green beans slowly braised with tomatoes, potatoes and olive oil until meltingly tender.
ingredients: 500 g green beans, trimmed and halved
300 g potatoes, peeled and cut into 3 cm chunks
400 g tomatoes, coarsely grated, skins discarded

stages.title: Prepare the vegetables
steps: Trim the stalk ends from the green beans and cut them in half.
Peel the potatoes and cut them into 3 cm chunks.
Cut the tomatoes in half and grate the cut sides on a box grater into a bowl, discarding the skins.
Thinly slice the onion and garlic, and finely chop the parsley.

stages.title: Build the sauce base
steps: Heat the olive oil in a large heavy-based pot over medium heat.
Add the onion and cook, stirring often, for 6–8 minutes until soft and translucent but not browned.
Add the garlic and tomato paste and stir for 1 minute until fragrant.
Pour in the grated tomato, then add the oregano, salt and black pepper, and simmer for 3–4 minutes until the sauce thickens slightly.

stages.title: Braise the beans and potatoes
steps: Add the potatoes and green beans to the pot and stir to coat in the sauce.
Pour in 200 ml water and bring to a simmer over medium heat.
Reduce the heat to low, cover and cook for 30–35 minutes, stirring gently every 10 minutes, until the beans are very soft and a knife slides easily into the potatoes.

stages.title: Reduce and finish
steps: Remove the lid and cook over medium heat for 3–5 minutes until the sauce is thick and glossy and clings to the vegetables.
Stir through the parsley, taste and add more salt if needed, then serve warm or at room temperature.

tips: Grating the tomatoes gives a smooth sauce without tough skins, so the dish stays silky after a long braise.
Greek beans are cooked until very soft rather than crisp; the long, gentle braise lets them absorb the oil and tomato.
The generous olive oil is what makes this dish 'lathera' (oily) and gives the sauce its body, so don't cut it back too far.
Cutting the potatoes into chunks of similar size means they finish cooking at the same time as the beans.
variations: Serve with crumbled feta and crusty bread to mop up the sauce.
Add 1/2 tsp chilli flakes with the oregano for a gentle heat.
recipe.storage: Refrigerate in an airtight container for up to 3 days. Reheat gently in a pan over low heat until hot, adding a splash of water if the sauce has thickened. It is also good served cold.

recipe.title: Vietnamese Banh Xeo
recipe.summary: Crisp turmeric rice crêpes filled with prawns, pork and bean sprouts, wrapped in fresh herbs.
ingredients: 150 g pork loin, thinly sliced into strips

stages.title: Make the batter
steps: Whisk the rice flour, turmeric and 1/2 tsp salt in a large bowl.
Whisk in the coconut milk and 250 ml water until smooth, then stir in the spring onions.
Rest the batter for 20 minutes so the flour hydrates; it should be the consistency of thin pouring cream, so whisk in a little more water if thick.

stages.title: Make the dipping sauce
steps: Juice 2 of the limes (about 80 ml) and cut the remaining lime into wedges.
Stir the lime juice, fish sauce, sugar, chilli and 60 ml water until the sugar dissolves, then set aside.

stages.title: Cook the pork and prawns
steps: Heat 1 tbsp of the oil in a large non-stick frying pan over medium-high heat.
Cook the pork and garlic for 3–4 minutes, stirring, until browned and cooked through with no pink remaining.
Add the prawns and cook for 2–3 minutes until pink and opaque, then season with a pinch of salt and black pepper.
Transfer to a plate and wipe the pan clean.

stages.title: Cook the pancakes
steps: Heat 1 tsp of the remaining oil in the same pan over medium-high heat until shimmering.
Stir the batter, then pour in about 125 ml, swirling to coat the base thinly; it should sizzle immediately.
Scatter a quarter of the pork and prawns and a small handful of bean sprouts over one half, then cover and cook for 2 minutes.
Uncover, drizzle 1 tsp oil around the edge, and cook over medium heat for 3–4 minutes until the underside is deep golden and the edges are crisp.
Fold the pancake in half, slide onto a plate, and repeat to make 4 pancakes, keeping them warm in a 100°C (80°C fan) oven.

stages.title: Serve
steps: Arrange the lettuce, mint, coriander and lime wedges on a platter.
Serve the pancakes hot, torn into pieces, wrapped in lettuce with the herbs and dipped in the sauce.

tips: Resting the batter lets the rice flour absorb the liquid, giving a crisper, more tender pancake that doesn't tear.
Get the pan properly hot before pouring; the sizzle sets the base quickly and creates the lacy crisp edge.
Slice the pork thinly so it cooks through in minutes and doesn't turn tough.
variations: Replace the pork and prawns with sliced mushrooms and cubed firm tofu, and use soy sauce instead of fish sauce in the dip for a vegetarian version.
Add thin slices of cooked chicken thigh instead of pork.
recipe.storage: Store cooked pancakes and fillings separately in the fridge for up to 2 days. Reheat pancakes in a hot dry pan for 1–2 minutes per side until crisp and heated through; the batter keeps 2 days in the fridge.

recipe.title: American Devilled Eggs
recipe.summary: Creamy mustard-and-mayo yolk filling piped into tender egg whites with a dusting of paprika.

stages.title: Boil the eggs
steps: Lower the eggs gently into a saucepan of boiling water over medium-high heat, then reduce to medium so the water simmers steadily.
Cook for 10 minutes, until the whites are firm and the yolks are cooked through and pale yellow.
Meanwhile, fill a large bowl with cold water and plenty of ice.

stages.title: Cool and peel
steps: Lift the eggs into the ice water with a slotted spoon and leave for 15 minutes, until completely cold.
Tap each egg all over on the bench, then peel under cold running water so the shell slips off without tearing the whites.
Pat the eggs dry with paper towel.

stages.title: Make the filling
steps: Cut each egg in half lengthways and pop the yolks into a bowl, keeping the whites intact.
Mash the yolks with a fork until fine and crumbly.
Add the mayonnaise, Dijon mustard, white vinegar, salt and black pepper and stir until smooth and creamy.
Taste and add a little more salt if needed.

stages.title: Fill and chill
steps: Spoon the filling into the egg whites, or pipe it using a piping bag with a star nozzle for a neater finish.
Refrigerate the eggs, uncovered or loosely covered, for 10 minutes to firm up.
Dust with the paprika, scatter over the chives and serve.

tips: Cooling the eggs in ice water stops the cooking, which prevents a grey-green ring around the yolks and makes the shells easier to peel.
Eggs that are a week or two old peel more cleanly than very fresh ones, so you lose less white.
Mash the yolks to a fine crumb before adding the wet ingredients, because lumps will not smooth out once the mayonnaise goes in.
Wiping the bench and trimming a thin slice off the base of each white stops the eggs sliding around on the platter.
variations: Stir 2 tbsp finely chopped crispy bacon into the filling for a smoky, salty version.
Replace the paprika topping with a pinch of cayenne pepper and a few pickled jalapeno slices for heat.
recipe.storage: Keep in an airtight container in the fridge for up to 2 days. Serve cold and do not reheat.

recipe.title: Indian Bhindi Masala
recipe.summary: Tender okra stir-fried with onions, tomatoes and aromatic spices until lightly crisp and savoury.

stages.title: Prepare the okra and aromatics
steps: Wash the okra, then dry each pod thoroughly with a clean tea towel so it doesn't turn slimy when cooked.
Trim the tops and tails, then slice the okra into 2 cm pieces.
Finely chop the onion and garlic, and chop the tomatoes.

stages.title: Brown the okra
steps: Heat 2 tbsp of the oil in a large frying pan over medium-high heat.

Add the okra in a single layer, working in two batches if the pan is crowded, and cook, stirring occasionally, for 8–10 minutes until the edges are browned and the pieces are tender when pierced with a knife.
Transfer the okra to a plate and wipe out the pan.

stages.title: Make the masala
steps: Heat the remaining 1 tbsp oil in the same pan over medium heat.
Add the onion and cook, stirring often, for 6–7 minutes until soft and golden.
Stir in the garlic, ground cumin, ground coriander, turmeric and chilli powder and cook for 1 minute until fragrant.
Add the tomatoes and salt, then cook, stirring and pressing the tomatoes down, for 8–10 minutes until broken down into a thick paste and the oil begins to separate at the edges.

stages.title: Combine and finish
steps: Return the okra to the pan and fold it gently through the masala.
Cook over medium-low heat for 3–4 minutes until the okra is coated and heated through.
Sprinkle over the garam masala and half the chopped coriander, then toss once.
Serve scattered with the remaining coriander.

tips: Drying the okra fully before cutting limits the sticky mucilage that makes it slimy.
Browning the okra separately over high heat sears the cut surfaces, which keeps the pieces from turning mushy in the masala.
Cooking the tomatoes until the oil separates removes their raw sharpness and gives a concentrated masala.
Adding the garam masala at the end keeps its aroma, which fades with long cooking.
variations: Add 1 tsp amchur or a squeeze of lemon juice at the end for a tangy dry-style bhindi.
Stir in 1 diced potato, cooked in the pan with the onion, to make it more filling.
recipe.storage: Refrigerate in an airtight container for up to 2 days. Reheat in a frying pan over medium heat until steaming hot throughout.

recipe.title: Italian Carciofi alla Romana
recipe.summary: Tender artichokes braised in olive oil, garlic, mint and lemon in the Roman style.

stages.title: Trim the artichokes
steps: Halve 1 lemon and squeeze the juice of the second lemon into a large bowl of cold water (about 1 litre); keep the squeezed halves in the bowl.
Snap off the tough outer leaves of each artichoke until you reach pale yellow-green leaves, then cut off the top third of the remaining leaves.
Peel the stems and trim the base, then rub all cut surfaces with the cut lemon half.
Spread the leaves open slightly with your thumbs, scoop out the fuzzy choke with a teaspoon, and drop each artichoke into the lemon water.

stages.title: Season the artichokes
steps: Mix the garlic, parsley, mint, salt and a few grinds of black pepper with 1 tbsp of the olive oil in a small bowl.
Drain the artichokes and shake out the excess water.
Spoon the herb mixture into the centres and press some between the outer leaves.

stages.title: Braise the artichokes
steps: Choose a saucepan just wide enough to hold the artichokes snugly, and stand them stem-up in it.
Pour in the 200 ml water and the remaining 2 tbsp olive oil.
Bring to a simmer over medium heat, then cover and reduce to low heat.
Cook for 30–35 minutes, until the stems and bases slip off a knife tip easily and an outer leaf pulls away with no resistance.
If the liquid evaporates before the artichokes are tender, add 50 ml water.

stages.title: Rest and serve
steps: Remove the lid and simmer over medium heat for 3–5 minutes, until the liquid reduces to a glossy sauce.
Rest the artichokes in the pan juices for 5 minutes, then serve warm with the juices spooned over and a squeeze of the lemon.

tips: Rubbing cut surfaces with lemon straight away stops the flesh oxidising and turning brown and bitter.
Standing the artichokes stem-up in a snug pan keeps them upright so they steam in the oil and water and the herbs stay in the centres.
Peeling the stems lets you eat them; the inner stem is as tender and sweet as the heart.
variations: Add 1 tsp chilli flakes to the herb mixture for a gentle heat.
Replace the mint with 1 tbsp chopped fresh thyme for a more earthy flavour.
recipe.storage: Refrigerate in an airtight container with the cooking juices for up to 2 days. Serve at room temperature or reheat gently in a covered pan over low heat until warmed through.

recipe.title: Tunisian Lablabi
recipe.summary: Warm chickpeas in a cumin-garlic broth poured over torn bread, finished with lemon and harissa.
ingredients: 4 thick slices crusty bread, torn into bite-sized pieces

stages.title: Prepare the chickpeas and bread
steps: Drain the chickpeas into a colander and rinse under cold water, then set aside.
Crush the garlic and juice the lemon.
Tear the bread into bite-sized pieces and divide among 4 deep bowls.

stages.title: Build the flavour base
steps: Heat the olive oil in a large saucepan over medium heat.
Add the garlic, ground cumin and cumin seeds and stir for 30–60 seconds until fragrant but not browned.
Stir in 1 tbsp of the harissa and cook for 30 seconds.

stages.title: Simmer the broth
steps: Add the chickpeas, vegetable stock and salt, and bring to a boil over high heat.
Reduce the heat to medium-low and simmer for 20 minutes, until the chickpeas are very tender.
Crush about a quarter of the chickpeas against the side of the pan with a wooden spoon to thicken the broth.
Stir in the lemon juice and simmer for 2 minutes. Taste and add more salt if needed.

stages.title: Assemble and serve
steps: Ladle the hot chickpeas and broth over the bread so it soaks up the liquid.
Top each bowl with a little of the remaining harissa, and serve straight away.

tips: Rinsing canned chickpeas removes the starchy canning liquid, which can make the broth taste flat.
Crushing some of the chickpeas thickens the broth without flour or cream, giving the traditional soupy but hearty texture.
Use stale or day-old bread if you can, because it soaks up the broth without turning to mush.
Add harissa at the table as well as in the pot, as brands vary a lot in heat.
variations: Top each bowl with a soft-boiled or poached egg, cooked until the white is set and the yolk is runny, or cooked through if you prefer.
Add a drained can of tuna and a spoonful of capers on top of each bowl for a more traditional street-style version.
recipe.storage: Store the broth without the bread in a sealed container in the fridge for up to 3 days, or freeze for up to 3 months. Reheat in a saucepan over medium heat until steaming hot, then pour over fresh bread.

recipe.title: French Tarte Flambée
recipe.summary: A paper-thin Alsatian flatbread topped with crème fraîche, onions and smoky bacon.
ingredients: 150 g bacon, cut into thin strips

stages.title: Make the dough
steps: Combine the flour and salt in a large bowl and make a well in the centre.
Pour in 125 ml water and the olive oil, then mix with a spoon until a rough dough forms.
Knead on a lightly floured bench for 3–4 minutes until smooth and elastic.
Divide the dough into 2 equal pieces, shape into balls and cover with a clean tea towel.

stages.title: Prepare the toppings
steps: Stir the nutmeg and a generous grind of black pepper into the crème fraîche.
Slice the onion as thinly as you can and separate the slices into rings.
Cut the bacon into thin strips about 1 cm wide.

stages.title: Rest the dough and heat the oven
steps: Heat the oven to 250°C (230°C fan) and put 2 large baking trays on separate shelves to heat up.
Leave the dough covered to rest for 20 minutes so it rolls out thinly without springing back.

stages.title: Shape and top the tartes
steps: Roll each dough ball on a sheet of baking paper into a very thin oval or rectangle, about 2–3 mm thick.
Spread half the crème fraîche mixture over each base, leaving a 1 cm border.
Scatter the onion and bacon evenly over both bases.

stages.title: Bake
steps: Carefully slide each tarte on its baking paper onto a hot tray.
Bake for 10–12 minutes, until the edges are crisp and browned, the bacon is cooked and browned at the tips, and the onion is softened and lightly charred.
Swap the trays between shelves after 6 minutes if one side is browning faster.

stages.title: Rest and serve
steps: Rest the tartes on a board for 2 minutes so the base firms up.
Cut each into pieces with a sharp knife or pizza wheel and serve hot.

tips: Roll the dough very thin, because a thick base turns bready instead of crisp like a traditional tarte flambée.
Preheating the trays gives the base an immediate blast of heat from underneath, which crisps the underside before the topping releases moisture.
Slice the onion paper-thin so it softens and chars in the short bake instead of staying raw and sharp.
Leave a border when spreading the crème fraîche so it doesn't run off the edge and burn on the tray.
variations: Add 100 g grated gruyere over the crème fraîche for a richer, gratinée-style tarte.
For a sweet version, omit the bacon and onion, top with thinly sliced apples and a sprinkle of caster sugar and cinnamon, and bake until the apple edges are golden.
recipe.storage: Best eaten straight away while crisp. Refrigerate leftovers in an airtight container for up to 2 days and reheat on a tray in a 200°C (180°C fan) oven for 5–6 minutes until hot through and crisp.

recipe.title: French Ile Flottante
recipe.summary: Cloudlike poached meringues floating on chilled vanilla custard with ribbons of amber caramel.

stages.title: Separate the eggs and warm the milk
steps: Separate the 4 eggs, putting the yolks in a medium heatproof bowl and the whites in a large, clean, dry bowl.
Pour the milk into a medium saucepan and add the vanilla extract.
Heat the milk over medium heat for 3–4 minutes until steaming and small bubbles form at the edge, then remove from the heat.

stages.title: Make the custard
steps: Whisk the yolks with 50 g of the caster sugar for 1–2 minutes until pale and thick.
Slowly pour the warm milk into the yolks, whisking constantly, then return the mixture to the saucepan.

Stir with a wooden spoon over low heat for 6–8 minutes until the custard thickens enough to coat the back of the spoon and a finger drawn through it leaves a clear line. Do not let it boil or it will scramble.
Strain the custard through a fine sieve into a jug or shallow serving dish.

stages.title: Chill the custard
steps: Press baking paper onto the surface of the custard to stop a skin forming.
Refrigerate for at least 2 hours until completely cold.

stages.title: Poach the meringues
steps: Whisk the egg whites with the pinch of salt using electric beaters on medium speed for 1–2 minutes until foamy.
Add 30 g of the caster sugar a spoonful at a time, then beat on high for 2–3 minutes until stiff, glossy peaks form.
Bring the 1 litre water to a bare simmer in a wide frying pan over medium-low heat, with only tiny bubbles breaking the surface.
Using two spoons, shape the meringue into 4 large ovals and slip them into the water. Poach for 1 minute on each side until puffed and firm to the touch.
Lift out with a slotted spoon and drain on paper towel.

stages.title: Make the caramel and serve
steps: Put the remaining 40 g caster sugar in a small, clean saucepan over medium heat. Do not stir; swirl the pan occasionally for 4–5 minutes until the sugar melts into a golden amber caramel.
Remove from the heat as soon as it is amber, as it darkens quickly and turns bitter.
Pour the cold custard into 4 shallow bowls and float a meringue on each.
Drizzle the caramel over the meringues and serve straight away.

tips: Stirring the custard over low heat and straining it protects the yolks from curdling and catches any small lumps.
Poaching below a simmer keeps the meringues tender; fast bubbling makes them rubbery and they collapse.
A clean, dry bowl with no trace of yolk lets the whites whip to stiff peaks.
Add the caramel just before serving, as it softens and melts into the meringue if left to stand.
variations: Use a split vanilla pod instead of extract: scrape the seeds into the milk, add the pod, and remove it before making the custard.
Scatter toasted flaked almonds over the top for crunch.
recipe.storage: Keep the custard and meringues separate, covered in the fridge, for up to 2 days. Add the meringues and fresh caramel just before serving. Do not freeze.

recipe.title: Lebanese Shish Barak
recipe.summary: Tiny lamb-filled dumplings gently simmered in warm garlicky yoghurt sauce with dried mint.

stages.title: Make and rest the dough
steps: Combine the flour and 1/4 tsp of the salt in a large bowl, then add 130 ml water and mix to a shaggy dough.
Knead on a bench for 5 minutes until smooth and elastic.
Cover with a damp tea towel and rest for 25 minutes.

stages.title: Cook the lamb filling
steps: Heat 1 tbsp of the olive oil in a frying pan over medium heat and cook the onion for 4 minutes until soft.
Add the lamb mince, cinnamon, the remaining 1/4 tsp salt and a pinch of black pepper, breaking up the mince with a spoon.
Cook for 6–8 minutes over medium-high heat until browned, cooked through with no pink remaining, and dry.
Tip onto a plate and cool for 10 minutes.

stages.title: Shape the dumplings
steps: Roll the dough out on a floured bench until 2 mm thick and cut into 6 cm circles.
Place 1 tsp of the filling in the centre of each circle, fold over into a half moon and press the edges firmly to seal.
Bring the two corners together, pinch to join and set on a floured tray.

stages.title: Bake the dumplings
steps: Heat the oven to 200°C (180°C fan) and line a baking tray with baking paper.
Toss the dumplings with the remaining 1 tbsp olive oil on the tray in a single layer.
Bake for 15–18 minutes, turning once, until golden and crisp.

stages.title: Cook the yoghurt sauce
steps: Whisk the yoghurt, egg and cornflour in a large saucepan until smooth, then add 250 ml cold water if the mixture feels very thick.
Heat over medium heat, stirring constantly in one direction, until it comes to a gentle simmer, about 10 minutes.
Reduce to low and simmer gently for 10 minutes, stirring often, until slightly thickened and the egg is cooked through.
Add the baked dumplings and simmer for 5 minutes over low heat until the pastry is tender.

stages.title: Fry the garlic and mint
steps: Melt the butter in a small frying pan over medium heat.
Fry the garlic for 1 minute until fragrant and just golden, then stir in the dried mint for 10 seconds.
Spoon the garlic and mint over the dumplings in the sauce and serve hot.

tips: Stirring the yoghurt in one direction and bringing it up slowly keeps the egg and cornflour stabilising it, so it does not split.
Dry the lamb filling well, because excess moisture makes the dumplings soggy and hard to seal.
Rolling the dough very thin gives tender dumplings; thick dough stays chewy after simmering.
Greek yoghurt is thick enough to give a creamy sauce without long reduction.
variations: Swap the lamb for beef mince and add 1/2 tsp ground allspice to the filling.
Serve over cooked rice to stretch the dish further.
recipe.storage: Refrigerate in an airtight container for up to 2 days. Reheat gently in a saucepan over low heat with a splash of water, stirring, and do not boil.

recipe.title: Finnish Lohikeitto
recipe.summary: Tender salmon, potatoes and leeks in a delicate creamy dill broth with a fresh lemon finish.
ingredients: 500 g salmon fillet, skin removed, pin-boned
500 g potatoes, peeled and cut into 2 cm cubes
2 leeks, white and pale green parts only, halved and sliced

stages.title: Prepare the vegetables and salmon
steps: Cut the salmon into 3 cm cubes and refrigerate until needed.
Peel the potatoes and cut them into 2 cm cubes, then dice the carrot into 1 cm pieces.
Halve the leeks lengthways, slice them and rinse well in a colander to remove grit, then drain.
Pick the dill fronds from the stalks and chop them roughly.

stages.title: Soften the leeks and carrot
steps: Melt the butter in a large heavy-based pot over medium heat.
Add the leeks and carrot and the salt, and cook, stirring often, for 6–7 minutes until the leeks are soft and glossy but not browned.

stages.title: Simmer the potatoes
steps: Add the potatoes and pour in the chicken stock and 200 ml water.
Bring to the boil over high heat, then reduce to medium-low and simmer for 12–15 minutes, until a knife slides easily into a potato cube.

stages.title: Poach the salmon
steps: Reduce the heat to low so the soup barely bubbles.
Add the salmon cubes and the cream and cook for 4–5 minutes, until the salmon is opaque and flakes easily.
Do not let the soup boil once the cream is in, or it may split.

stages.title: Finish and serve
steps: Remove the pot from the heat and stir in the chopped dill, lemon juice and black pepper.
Taste and add a little more salt or lemon juice if needed, then ladle into warm bowls.

tips: Waxy potatoes hold their shape in the soup, while floury ones break down and make it cloudy and thick.
Add the salmon last and keep the heat low, as it cooks in a few minutes and turns dry and chalky if boiled.
Add the lemon juice off the heat so the cream does not curdle and the dill stays fresh.
Rinse the sliced leeks well, because grit collects between the layers and ruins the soup.
variations: Replace half the salmon with firm white fish fillets, cut into the same size cubes, for a milder soup.
Add 1 tsp ground allspice berries or a few whole allspice berries with the stock for a more traditional Finnish flavour.
recipe.storage: Cool quickly and refrigerate in a sealed container for up to 2 days. Reheat gently over low heat without boiling. Not suitable for freezing because the cream and potatoes change texture.

recipe.title: Japanese Zaru Soba
recipe.summary: Chilled buckwheat noodles served with a savoury soy-dashi dipping sauce, spring onions and wasabi.
ingredients: 1 sheet nori, cut into thin strips

stages.title: Make the dipping sauce
steps: Combine the dashi stock, soy sauce and mirin in a small saucepan.
Bring to a simmer over medium heat and cook for 2 minutes to cook off the alcohol in the mirin.
Pour the sauce into a heatproof bowl and let it cool for 10 minutes.

stages.title: Chill the sauce and prepare the garnishes
steps: Cover the sauce and refrigerate for at least 30 minutes, until completely cold.
While the sauce chills, thinly slice the spring onions and cut the nori into thin strips with scissors.
Fill a large bowl with cold water and plenty of ice, ready for the noodles.

stages.title: Cook and rinse the noodles
steps: Bring a large pot of water to a rolling boil over high heat. Add the soba noodles and stir straight away so the strands do not stick together.
Cook according to the packet, usually 4–6 minutes, until tender but still with a slight bite.
Drain in a colander and rinse under cold running water, rubbing the noodles gently with your hands, until the water runs clear and the noodles are cold.
Plunge the noodles into the iced water for 30 seconds, then drain very well.

stages.title: Serve
steps: Divide the noodles among 4 plates or bamboo trays and scatter the nori strips on top.
Pour the chilled sauce into 4 small bowls and place the spring onions and wasabi alongside.
To eat, stir wasabi and spring onions into the sauce, then dip a few noodles at a time.

tips: Rinsing the noodles under cold water and rubbing them removes surface starch, which stops them turning gluey and clumping.
The ice bath chills the noodles quickly and firms them, giving the chewy texture zaru soba is known for.
Chill the sauce fully, as warm sauce softens the noodles and dulls the wasabi.
Soba brands vary in cooking time, so taste a strand a minute before the packet time is up.
variations: Serve the sauce with a little grated ginger and a pinch of toasted sesame seeds alongside the spring onions.
Use the same sauce with chilled udon noodles instead of soba. Check the label if you need a wheat-free soba, as many contain wheat flour.
recipe.storage: Eat the noodles straight away. Keep leftover dipping sauce in a covered container in the fridge for up to 3 days.

recipe.title: Indian Aloo Paratha
recipe.summary: Golden wholewheat flatbreads stuffed with spiced mashed potatoes, crisp outside and soft within.
ingredients: 300 g wholewheat atta flour, plus 1/4 cup extra for rolling
450 g potatoes, peeled and cut into 3 cm chunks

stages.title: Make and rest the dough
steps: Combine the atta flour and 1/4 tsp of the salt in a large bowl.
Gradually add 180 ml water, mixing with your hand until a soft, shaggy dough forms.
Knead on a bench for 3–4 minutes until smooth and supple, then cover with a damp tea towel.
Rest the dough for 20 minutes, which relaxes the gluten so the parathas roll without tearing.

stages.title: Cook and season the potato filling
steps: Put the potatoes in a saucepan, cover with cold water and add a pinch of salt, then bring to the boil over high heat.
Reduce to medium heat and simmer for 12–15 minutes until a knife slides in easily.
Drain well and leave in the colander for 5 minutes so the steam escapes.
Mash the potatoes until completely smooth, then stir in the chilli, cumin seeds, garam masala, coriander and the remaining 1/4 tsp salt.
Cool the filling for 5 minutes, then roll it into 6 equal balls.

stages.title: Stuff and roll the parathas
steps: Divide the dough into 6 equal portions and roll each into a ball.
Flatten one dough ball into a 9 cm round, using a little of the extra flour for dusting.
Place a potato ball in the centre, pull the edges up around it and pinch together to seal fully.
Flatten the sealed ball gently, then roll with light pressure into an 18 cm round, dusting with flour as needed.
Repeat with the remaining dough and filling, stacking the rolled parathas with baking paper or flour between them.

stages.title: Cook the parathas
steps: Heat a large non-stick frying pan or flat skillet over medium-high heat for 2 minutes until hot.
Cook one paratha for 1 minute, until small bubbles appear and the underside has pale spots, then flip.
Brush the top with some of the melted butter and cook for 1 minute, then flip and brush the other side.
Cook for a further 30–60 seconds each side, pressing gently with a spatula, until both sides are golden brown with darker spots.
Keep the cooked parathas wrapped in a clean tea towel while you cook the rest, then serve hot.

tips: Mash the potatoes until there are no lumps and let them cool; a wet or lumpy filling splits the dough when rolling.
Seal the dough completely around the filling, because any gap lets the potato leak out and burn in the pan.
Dust with only as much flour as needed, since excess flour scorches in the pan and tastes bitter.
Cook over medium-high heat so the parathas brown and cook through quickly; a low heat dries them out and makes them tough.
variations: Add 1/2 tsp ground turmeric and 1/2 tsp chilli flakes to the filling for a more fiery, golden paratha.
Mix 60 g crumbled paneer into the mashed potato for a richer, creamier filling.
recipe.storage: Cool completely, then refrigerate in an airtight container for up to 2 days or freeze with baking paper between layers for up to 1 month. Reheat in a dry frying pan over medium heat for 1–2 minutes each side until hot through.

recipe.title: French Clafoutis aux Cerises
recipe.summary: Sweet cherries baked in a delicate vanilla custard with lightly golden edges and a soft centre.

stages.title: Prepare the dish
steps: Heat the oven to 180°C (160°C fan).
Grease a 24 cm baking dish thoroughly with the softened butter.
Pat the pitted cherries dry with paper towel so they don't thin the batter.
Scatter the cherries in a single layer over the base of the dish.

stages.title: Make the batter
steps: Whisk the eggs and caster sugar in a large bowl for 1–2 minutes until pale and slightly frothy.
Add the plain flour a little at a time, whisking until no lumps remain.
Whisk in the milk and vanilla extract until you have a smooth, thin batter.

stages.title: Bake the clafoutis
steps: Pour the batter slowly over the cherries so they stay spread out.
Bake on the middle shelf for 35–40 minutes, until puffed, golden on top and set in the centre.
Test by inserting a knife into the centre; it should come out clean, with no raw batter.

stages.title: Rest and serve
steps: Rest the clafoutis in the dish for 15 minutes; it will sink slightly and the custard will firm up.
Dust with the icing sugar just before serving.
Serve warm or at room temperature, straight from the dish.

tips: Pat the cherries dry so excess juice doesn't make the custard watery or leave pale, soggy patches.
Whisking the flour in gradually gives a lump-free batter and a tender, custardy texture rather than a rubbery one.
Resting after baking lets the custard set so it slices cleanly instead of collapsing.
variations: Swap the cherries for halved plums or apricots, adding 1 tbsp extra caster sugar if the fruit is tart.
Leave the cherry pits in for a traditional, slightly almondy flavour, and warn your guests before serving.
recipe.storage: Cover and refrigerate for up to 2 days. Bring to room temperature or warm gently in a 150°C (130°C fan) oven for 10 minutes before serving. Not suitable for freezing.

recipe.title: Peruvian Arroz Chaufa
recipe.summary: Peruvian-Chinese fried rice with chicken, eggs, spring onions and a deeply savoury soy glaze.
ingredients: 300 g chicken thigh, cut into 1 cm pieces
4 spring onions, whites and greens separated, thinly sliced

stages.title: Prepare the ingredients
steps: Break up any clumps in the cold rice with your fingers so the grains separate.
Toss the chicken with the salt and black pepper in a bowl.
Separate the white and green parts of the spring onions and keep them in two piles.
Mix the soy sauce and sesame oil in a small jar or cup, ready to pour.

stages.title: Scramble the eggs
steps: Heat 1 tbsp of the vegetable oil in a wok over high heat until shimmering.
Pour in the beaten eggs and stir for 30–40 seconds until just set and no longer runny.
Tip the eggs onto a plate and break into small pieces, then wipe out the wok.

stages.title: Cook the chicken
steps: Heat the remaining 1 tbsp vegetable oil in the wok over high heat.
Add the chicken in a single layer and leave for 1 minute to brown, then stir-fry for 4–5 minutes until golden and cooked through with no pink in the centre.
Add the garlic and spring onion whites and stir for 30 seconds until fragrant.

stages.title: Fry the rice and finish
steps: Add the rice to the wok and toss over high heat for 3–4 minutes, pressing it against the wok, until steaming hot throughout and lightly toasted in places.
Pour the soy sauce and sesame oil mixture around the edge of the wok and toss for 1 minute until the rice is evenly coloured.
Return the eggs to the wok and toss for 30 seconds to combine.
Stir through the spring onion greens and serve straight away.

tips: Cold rice from the fridge is drier, so the grains fry and toast instead of turning mushy and clumping together.
Cutting the chicken into 1 cm pieces means it cooks through in the few minutes before the rice goes in.
Pouring the soy sauce around the hot edge of the wok makes it sizzle and caramelise slightly, adding a smoky flavour.
Frying in a single layer and keeping the heat high gives the browning that characterises chaufa; cook in two batches if your wok is small.
variations: Use 300 g peeled prawns instead of chicken and cook for 2–3 minutes until pink and opaque.
Add 1 tbsp finely grated ginger with the garlic for a sharper, more Chinese-Peruvian flavour.
recipe.storage: Cool quickly and refrigerate in a covered container for up to 2 days. Reheat in a hot pan or microwave until steaming hot throughout. Do not reheat more than once.

recipe.title: Ethiopian Atakilt Wat
recipe.summary: Tender cabbage, potatoes and carrots simmered with turmeric, ginger and gentle Ethiopian spices.
ingredients: 500 g cabbage, cut into wide strips
400 g potatoes, peeled and cut into 2 cm cubes

stages.title: Prepare the vegetables
steps: Cut the cabbage into wide strips, discarding the tough core.
Peel the potatoes and cut them into 2 cm cubes; cut the carrots into thick half-moons.
Finely dice the onion, finely chop the garlic and grate the ginger.

stages.title: Soften the onion and spices
steps: Heat the vegetable oil in a large, deep frying pan or wide pot over medium heat.
Add the onion and the salt and cook, stirring often, for 8 minutes until soft and translucent but not browned.
Add the garlic, ginger and turmeric and stir for 30 seconds until fragrant, taking care not to scorch the spices.

stages.title: Cook the potatoes and carrots
steps: Add the potatoes and carrots to the pan and stir to coat in the spiced onion.
Pour in 150 ml water, bring to a gentle simmer over medium heat and cover with a lid.
Cook for 12 minutes, stirring once halfway, until the vegetables are just starting to soften at the edges.

stages.title: Add the cabbage and finish
steps: Add the cabbage on top, season with the black pepper and stir through; it will fill the pan at first and collapse as it cooks.
Cover and cook over medium-low heat for 12–15 minutes, stirring now and then, until the potato is tender when pierced with a knife and the cabbage is soft.
Remove the lid and cook for 2–3 minutes over medium heat until any excess liquid has evaporated.
Taste, add more salt if needed and serve warm.

tips: Cooking the onion slowly without browning gives the sweet, mild base that this turmeric-yellow dish depends on.
Cutting the potatoes and carrots smaller than the cabbage lets them cook through in the same time and keeps their shape.
Cooking the turmeric for only 30 seconds avoids a bitter, scorched flavour.
variations: Add 1 sliced capsicum with the cabbage for extra sweetness and colour.
Stir in 1/2 tsp ground cumin with the turmeric for a warmer, earthier flavour.
recipe.storage: Refrigerate in an airtight container for up to 2 days. Reheat gently in a pan over low heat with a splash of water until hot; the potato will be softer after reheating.

recipe.title: Syrian Fatteh
recipe.summary: Crisp pita layered with warm chickpeas, garlicky yoghurt, toasted pine nuts and lemon.
ingredients: 2 pita bread, torn into 3 cm pieces
2 x 400 g cans chickpeas, drained and rinsed

stages.title: Toast the pita
steps: Heat the oven to 190°C (170°C fan).
Spread the torn pita on a baking tray and toss with the olive oil.
Bake for 8–10 minutes, turning once, until golden and crisp, then set aside.

stages.title: Make the garlic yoghurt
steps: Combine the yoghurt, garlic, 2 tbsp of the lemon juice and half the salt in a bowl.
Stir until smooth, taste, and add a little more lemon juice if you want it sharper.

stages.title: Warm the chickpeas
steps: Put the chickpeas in a saucepan with 125 ml water, the cumin and the remaining salt.
Heat over medium heat for 5–6 minutes, stirring occasionally, until hot and the liquid has mostly reduced.
Keep warm over the lowest heat.

stages.title: Brown the pine nuts
steps: Melt the butter in a small frying pan over medium-low heat.
Add the pine nuts and cook, stirring constantly, for 2–3 minutes until golden brown.
Remove from the heat straight away, as they scorch quickly.

stages.title: Assemble and serve
steps: Divide the toasted pita between 4 shallow bowls.
Spoon the warm chickpeas and a little of their liquid over the pita.
Top with the garlic yoghurt, then spoon the hot pine nut butter over the top.
Scatter with the parsley and serve immediately.

tips: Toasting the pita until fully crisp stops it turning to mush under the chickpeas and yoghurt.
Keep the pine nuts over medium-low heat and stir constantly, because the butter's milk solids and the nuts burn quickly and turn bitter.
Spooning some of the chickpea liquid over the pita softens the edges slightly while the centres stay crunchy.
Use full-fat yoghurt at room temperature so it stays creamy and doesn't cool the warm chickpeas too much.
variations: Stir 1 tbsp tahini into the yoghurt for a nuttier, richer sauce.
Replace the pine nuts with slivered almonds, browned the same way, if you prefer.
recipe.storage: Assembled fatteh goes soggy, so serve it straight away. Store leftover chickpeas and garlic yoghurt separately in the fridge for up to 2 days, and the pita in an airtight container. Reheat the chickpeas until piping hot.

recipe.title: Japanese Ochazuke
recipe.summary: Steamed rice bathed in hot green tea with salmon flakes, nori and sesame.
ingredients: 1 sheet nori, cut into thin strips

stages.title: Cook the salmon
steps: Pat the salmon fillets dry and season both sides with the salt.
Heat the oil in a non-stick frying pan over medium heat.
Cook the salmon skin-side down for 4–5 minutes, until the skin is crisp, then turn and cook 2–3 minutes more, until the flesh flakes easily.
Lift the salmon onto a plate, remove the skin and any bones, then flake the flesh into large pieces.

stages.title: Prepare the toppings and rice
steps: Thinly slice the spring onions and cut the nori into thin strips with scissors.
Toast the sesame seeds in a dry small frying pan over medium heat for 1–2 minutes, shaking often, until lightly golden.
Warm the cooked rice in the microwave in a covered bowl for 2–3 minutes, until steaming hot, then divide among four bowls.

stages.title: Make the tea broth and serve
steps: Heat 500 ml of brewed green tea in a small saucepan over medium heat for 2–3 minutes, until steaming but not boiling.
Stir the soy sauce into the tea.
Top the rice with the flaked salmon, spring onions, nori and sesame seeds.
Pour the hot tea around the rice, dividing it evenly among the bowls, and serve straight away.

tips: Heat the tea until steaming but not boiling, because boiling water makes green tea bitter and dulls its flavour.
Crisping the salmon skin and flaking the fish into large pieces keeps it from dissolving in the hot tea.
Pour the tea around the rice rather than over it so the nori stays crisp for the first few bites.
variations: Swap the salmon for 4 tbsp of shredded cooked chicken breast or a drained can of tuna.
Add 1 tsp of wasabi, stirred into the tea, for a sharper, hotter broth.

recipe.title: Filipino Arroz Caldo
recipe.summary: Comforting ginger chicken rice porridge with garlic, spring onions and a squeeze of calamansi or lime.
ingredients: 400 g chicken thigh, cut into 2 cm pieces
30 g ginger, cut into fine matchsticks

stages.title: Prepare the ingredients
steps: Rinse the rice in a sieve under cold running water for 1 minute, then drain well.
Cut the chicken thigh into 2 cm pieces, discarding any large pieces of fat.
Finely dice the onion, mince the garlic and cut the ginger into fine matchsticks.
Thinly slice the spring onions and cut the limes into wedges for serving.

stages.title: Soften the aromatics and brown the chicken
steps: Heat the oil in a large heavy-based pot over medium heat.
Cook the onion for 4 minutes, stirring often, until soft and translucent.
Add the ginger and garlic and cook for 1 minute until fragrant.
Add the chicken and cook for 4–5 minutes, stirring, until the outside is opaque.

stages.title: Simmer the rice into porridge
steps: Add the rice and stir for 1 minute to coat the grains in the pan juices.
Pour in the chicken stock and 500 ml water, then bring to the boil over high heat.
Reduce the heat to low and simmer, partly covered, for 40 minutes, stirring every 5 minutes to stop the rice sticking.
The porridge is ready when the grains have broken down and thickened, and the chicken is cooked through with no pink inside.

stages.title: Season and serve
steps: Stir in the fish sauce and black pepper.
If the porridge is thicker than you like, stir in up to 125 ml hot water and heat over low heat for 2 minutes.
Ladle into bowls and top with the spring onions, serving the lime wedges alongside.

tips: Rinsing the rice removes surface starch so the grains break down evenly rather than turning gluey at the bottom of the pot.
Chicken thigh stays tender through a long simmer, where breast would turn dry and stringy.
Stir regularly in the last 15 minutes, as the thickening porridge catches easily on the base of the pot.
Add the fish sauce at the end so its flavour stays fresh and you can judge the saltiness after the stock has reduced.
variations: Top with fried garlic and a halved boiled egg for a more traditional street-food style bowl.
Replace half the water with extra stock and add a pinch of saffron threads with the rice for the golden colour used in some versions.
recipe.storage: Refrigerate in a covered container for up to 2 days. The porridge thickens as it cools, so reheat with a splash of water or stock until piping hot.

recipe.title: Italian Polenta con Funghi
recipe.summary: Creamy Parmesan polenta topped with buttery mushrooms, garlic and thyme.

stages.title: Prepare the ingredients
steps: Slice the mushrooms thickly, leaving small ones whole.
Finely chop the garlic and pick the thyme leaves from the sprigs.
Finely grate the parmesan.

stages.title: Brown the mushrooms
steps: Heat the olive oil and half the butter in a large frying pan over medium-high heat.
Add the mushrooms in a single layer, working in two batches if the pan is crowded, and cook for 6–8 minutes without stirring too often, until deep golden and any liquid has evaporated.
Add the garlic and thyme leaves and cook, stirring, for 1 minute until fragrant.
Season with half the salt and a generous grind of black pepper, then cover to keep warm off the heat.

stages.title: Cook the polenta
steps: Pour the vegetable stock and the remaining salt into a medium saucepan and bring to the boil over high heat.
Reduce the heat to medium-low and slowly pour in the polenta in a thin stream, whisking constantly to prevent lumps.
Cook, stirring with a wooden spoon, for 3–5 minutes or according to the packet, until thick and pulling away from the side of the pan.
Remove from the heat and stir in the remaining butter and the parmesan until melted and smooth.

stages.title: Serve
steps: Spoon the hot polenta into four warmed bowls.
Top with the mushrooms and any pan juices, and finish with extra black pepper.

tips: Mushrooms release a lot of water, so a wide pan and high heat let it evaporate and the mushrooms brown instead of steaming.
Pour the polenta in a slow stream while whisking so the grains separate and hydrate evenly, avoiding lumps.
Polenta thickens quickly as it stands, so stir in a splash of hot stock or water if it firms up before serving.
Mixed mushrooms such as Swiss brown, oyster and shiitake give more varied flavour and texture than one type.
variations: Stir 100 g gorgonzola or other blue cheese through the polenta with the parmesan for a stronger, tangier finish.
Finish the mushrooms with 2 tbsp white wine, simmered for 1 minute until almost evaporated, for extra depth.
recipe.storage: Refrigerate the polenta and mushrooms separately in covered containers for up to 2 days. Reheat the polenta in a saucepan over low heat with a splash of water or stock, stirring until smooth and hot, and reheat the mushrooms until steaming.

recipe.title: Persian Mast o Khiar
recipe.summary: Cool thick yoghurt with diced cucumber, mint, walnuts and a hint of dried rose.

stages.title: Toast the walnuts
steps: Heat a small dry frying pan over medium heat.
Add the walnuts and toast for 3 minutes, stirring often, until fragrant and lightly golden.
Tip onto a plate and cool for 3 minutes, then roughly chop.

stages.title: Prepare the cucumber and sultanas
steps: Finely dice the cucumbers, then toss with the salt in a sieve set over a bowl.
Leave to drain for 5 minutes, then press gently and pat dry with paper towel so the yoghurt stays thick.
Roughly chop the sultanas so they spread evenly through the dip.

stages.title: Mix the yoghurt
steps: Spoon the greek yoghurt into a serving bowl and stir until smooth.
Rub the dried mint between your palms as you add it, then stir in the garlic.
Fold through the drained cucumber, the sultanas and two-thirds of the walnuts.

stages.title: Chill and serve
steps: Cover and refrigerate for 25 minutes so the mint softens and the flavours blend.
Taste and add a pinch more salt if needed.
Scatter the remaining walnuts and the rose petals over the top just before serving.

tips: Salting and draining the cucumber removes water that would otherwise thin the yoghurt as it sits.
Rubbing dried mint between your palms warms it and releases its aroma.
Toast the walnuts to bring out their flavour and keep them crisp against the creamy yoghurt.
variations: Swap the sultanas for finely chopped dried apricots for a tarter sweetness.
Thin with 1/4 cup cold water and chill to serve as a cold soup over ice, in the style of a summer Persian soup.
recipe.storage: Refrigerate covered for up to 2 days. Stir before serving, as a little liquid may separate. Not suitable to freeze.

recipe.title: Indian Upma
recipe.summary: Fluffy savoury semolina cooked with mustard seeds, curry leaves, vegetables and lemon.

stages.title: Prepare the vegetables
steps: Finely dice the onion and carrot into pieces about 5 mm.
Juice the lemon and measure out the frozen peas.
Measure the semolina and the water so everything is within reach of the stove.

stages.title: Toast the semolina
steps: Heat a large, deep frying pan over low-medium heat and add the semolina without any oil.
Stir constantly for 4–5 minutes until it smells nutty and looks slightly darker, but has not browned.
Tip the semolina into a bowl and wipe out the pan.

stages.title: Cook the flavour base
steps: Heat the vegetable oil in the same pan over medium heat.
Add the mustard seeds and cook for 30–60 seconds until they pop, then add the curry leaves and stir for 10 seconds (they will spit).
Add the onion, carrot and salt and cook, stirring, for 4–5 minutes until the onion is soft and translucent.

stages.title: Cook the upma
steps: Pour in the 500 ml water, add the peas and bring to a boil over medium-high heat.
Reduce the heat to low and pour in the toasted semolina in a slow stream, stirring constantly so no lumps form.
Cover and cook for 2–3 minutes until the water is absorbed and the semolina is soft and fluffy.
Stir in the lemon juice, fluff with a fork and serve hot.

tips: Toasting the semolina dry keeps the grains separate and fluffy instead of pasty.
Add the semolina in a slow stream while stirring, as pouring it in at once forms lumps that will not break down.
Dice the carrot very finely so it softens in the short cooking time.
variations: Add 1 tbsp roasted cashews with the mustard seeds for crunch.
Stir in 1 finely chopped red chilli with the onion for a spicier upma.
recipe.storage: Refrigerate in a covered container for up to 2 days. Reheat with a splash of water in a pan or microwave until piping hot.

recipe.title: Mexican Calabacitas
recipe.summary: Tender courgette and sweetcorn sautéed with tomatoes, onion and mild green chilli.
ingredients: 1 red chilli, finely chopped (seeded for less heat)

stages.title: Prepare the vegetables
steps: Cut the zucchini into 1.5 cm dice so the pieces cook at the same rate.
Dice the tomatoes and finely chop the onion and chilli.
If using frozen corn, tip it into a sieve and rinse under warm water to thaw, then drain well.

stages.title: Soften the onion and chilli
steps: Heat the olive oil in a large frying pan over medium heat.
Add the onion and cook, stirring often, for 4–5 minutes until soft and translucent.
Add the chilli and cook, stirring, for 1 minute until fragrant.

stages.title: Cook the zucchini and corn
steps: Increase the heat to medium-high, add the zucchini and the salt, and cook, stirring every minute, for 5–6 minutes until golden at the edges and just tender.
Add the corn and tomatoes and cook, stirring, for 3–4 minutes until the tomatoes have softened and released their juices but the zucchini still holds its shape.

stages.title: Finish and serve
steps: Taste and add a pinch more salt if needed.
Transfer to a serving dish and scatter over the feta and coriander.
Serve straight away while the zucchini is still tender.

tips: Dicing the zucchini evenly and cooking it over medium-high heat browns the edges and stops it steaming into mush.
Salt goes in with the zucchini so it draws out some moisture, which concentrates the flavour and helps the pieces colour.
Add the tomatoes late because long cooking breaks them down and makes the dish watery.
Feta is saltier than traditional queso fresco, so taste before adding extra salt at the end.
variations: Add 1 diced capsicum with the zucchini for extra sweetness and colour.
Stir through 2 tbsp sour cream at the end for a creamier version.
recipe.storage: Refrigerate in a covered container for up to 2 days. Reheat gently in a frying pan over medium heat for 2–3 minutes until hot; the zucchini will be softer than when fresh.

recipe.title: Vietnamese Ca Kho To
recipe.summary: Tender fish steaks braised in caramelised fish sauce with black pepper and spring onion.
ingredients: 600 g white fish fillets, firm-fleshed, cut into 4 cm thick pieces

stages.title: Prepare the fish and aromatics
steps: Cut the fish into 4 cm thick pieces and pat dry with paper towel.
Finely chop the garlic and shallots.
Thinly slice the spring onions and the red chilli, and keep them separate for serving.

stages.title: Make the caramel
steps: Heat the oil in a small heavy-based saucepan or clay pot over medium heat, then add the sugar.
Cook without stirring, swirling the pan occasionally, for 4–5 minutes until the sugar melts to a deep amber colour.
Add the garlic and shallots and stir for 1 minute until fragrant.
Stand back and carefully pour in the water, as it will spit. Stir for 1–2 minutes until the caramel dissolves, then stir in the fish sauce.

stages.title: Simmer the fish
steps: Bring the sauce to a gentle simmer over medium-low heat.
Nestle the fish pieces into the sauce in a single layer and cook, uncovered, for 6 minutes.
Turn the fish carefully and cook for 5–6 minutes more, spooning sauce over, until the fish flakes easily and is cooked through.
Meanwhile, cook the rice according to the packet.

stages.title: Reduce and serve
steps: Lift the fish onto a plate and cover loosely to keep warm.
Increase the heat to medium-high and boil the sauce for 3–4 minutes until syrupy and glossy.
Return the fish to the pan and spoon the sauce over for 1 minute to coat.
Sprinkle with the pepper, spring onions and chilli, and serve with the rice.

tips: Stop caramelising at deep amber, not dark brown; burnt sugar turns the sauce bitter.
Firm fish holds together during simmering, whereas delicate fillets can break up in the pan.
Use a small pan so the fish sits in the sauce; a wide pan makes the sauce reduce too quickly and leaves the fish dry.
Pouring the water into the hot caramel makes it spit, so add it slowly with the pan held away from you.
variations: Swap the fish for 600 g chicken thigh pieces and simmer for 20–25 minutes until cooked through with no pink inside.
Add 1 tbsp finely grated ginger with the garlic for a sharper, warmer flavour.
recipe.storage: Refrigerate in a covered container for up to 2 days. Reheat gently in a pan with a splash of water until piping hot.

recipe.title: Italian Bresaola Rucola e Grana
recipe.summary: Paper-thin cured beef layered with peppery rocket, Parmesan shavings and lemon.

stages.title: Prepare the rocket and cheese
steps: Wash the rocket, then dry it thoroughly in a salad spinner or between clean tea towels so the dressing clings.
Shave the parmesan into thin curls with a vegetable peeler and keep them in the fridge until serving.
Put four plates in the fridge to chill.

stages.title: Make the dressing
steps: Zest the lemon finely, then juice it to get about 3 tbsp juice.
Whisk 2 tbsp lemon juice with the olive oil, black pepper and salt in a small bowl until combined.
Taste the dressing on a piece of rocket and add a little more lemon juice if you want it sharper.

stages.title: Arrange the bresaola
steps: Take the chilled plates from the fridge.
Lay the bresaola slices loosely across the plates in a single layer, slightly overlapping, using 40 g per plate.
Leave the slices to sit for 5 minutes at room temperature so the flavour softens and the slices separate easily.

stages.title: Dress and serve
steps: Toss the rocket in a large bowl with half the dressing until lightly coated.
Pile the rocket over the bresaola on each plate.
Scatter the parmesan curls and lemon zest on top.
Drizzle with the remaining dressing and serve straight away, before the rocket wilts.

tips: Dry rocket keeps the dressing from watering down and lets it cling to the leaves.
Chilled plates keep the thin bresaola cool and stop it going greasy as it sits.
Dress the rocket only at the last minute, because lemon juice wilts the leaves within minutes.
Shaving the cheese with a peeler gives wide, thin curls that melt on the tongue rather than crumbling.
variations: Add 2 tbsp toasted pine nuts over the top for crunch.
Replace the parmesan with shaved pecorino for a sharper, saltier flavour.

recipe.title: Italian Semolina Gnocchi alla Romana
recipe.summary: Golden baked semolina rounds enriched with butter and Parmesan, crisp on top and tender inside.

stages.title: Prepare the tray and cheese
steps: Cut the butter into two portions: 30 g to stir into the semolina and 40 g for greasing and topping.
Use a little of the 40 g butter to grease a 20 x 30 cm tray, then line the base with baking paper.
