Finely grate the parmesan and divide it into two equal portions of 45 g.
Lightly whisk the egg yolks in a small bowl.

stages.title: Cook the semolina
steps: Heat the milk and salt in a large saucepan over medium heat for 4–5 minutes until steaming but not boiling.
Reduce the heat to low and whisk in the semolina in a slow, steady stream to avoid lumps.
Switch to a wooden spoon and stir for 8–10 minutes until the mixture is very thick and pulls away from the sides of the pan.
Remove from the heat and beat in the 30 g butter, the egg yolks and 45 g of the parmesan until smooth and glossy.

stages.title: Spread and set
steps: Scrape the mixture onto the prepared tray and spread it to an even 1.5 cm thickness, smoothing the top with a wet spatula.
Cool for 15 minutes at room temperature, then refrigerate for 30 minutes until completely firm to the touch.

stages.title: Cut the rounds
steps: Heat the oven to 200°C (180°C fan).
Cut the set semolina into rounds with a 5 cm cutter, dipping it in water between cuts.
Grease a 20 x 30 cm baking dish with a little of the remaining butter.
Overlap the rounds in the dish, including the trimmings pressed into any gaps.

stages.title: Bake until golden
steps: Dot the remaining butter over the rounds and scatter over the remaining 45 g parmesan.
Bake for 20–25 minutes until the tops are golden and the edges are crisp and bubbling.
Rest in the dish for 5 minutes before serving so the rounds hold their shape.

tips: Whisk the semolina in slowly while the milk is hot but not boiling, because dumping it in at once makes lumps that won't beat out.
Chill the mixture until fully firm so the rounds cut cleanly and don't slump or melt into one another when baked.
Dip the cutter in water between cuts so the sticky semolina releases without tearing.
Pressing the trimmings into the gaps means nothing is wasted and the top bakes into an even golden crust.
variations: Add a pinch of ground nutmeg with the egg yolks for a classic warm, nutty note.
Lay a few sage leaves between the rounds before baking, and scatter over extra browned butter to serve.
recipe.storage: Refrigerate in a covered container for up to 2 days. Reheat at 180°C (160°C fan) for 15 minutes until piping hot and crisp on top.

recipe.title: Greek Melitzanosalata
recipe.summary: Smoky aubergine dip with lemon, garlic, parsley and fruity olive oil.

stages.title: Roast the eggplants
steps: Heat the oven to 220°C (200°C fan) and line a baking tray with baking paper.
Prick each eggplant 6–8 times all over with a fork.
Roast the eggplants on the tray for 40–45 minutes, turning once halfway, until the skins are wrinkled and charred and the flesh is completely soft when pressed.

stages.title: Drain the flesh
steps: Leave the eggplants to cool for 10 minutes, until you can handle them.
Split them open and scoop the flesh into a fine sieve, discarding the skins.
Let the flesh drain for 15 minutes, pressing gently with a spoon once or twice to release the bitter liquid.

stages.title: Mix the salad
steps: Chop the drained flesh roughly on a board, keeping some texture.
Place it in a bowl with the garlic, lemon juice, salt and black pepper.
Stir in the olive oil a little at a time until the mixture is creamy but still chunky.
Fold through the parsley.

stages.title: Rest and serve
steps: Cover and rest the melitzanosalata at room temperature for 15 minutes so the garlic and lemon mellow into the eggplant.
Taste and add more salt or lemon juice if needed.
Warm the pita in the oven for 2–3 minutes if you like, then serve with the dip.

tips: Pricking the skins lets steam escape so the eggplants don't burst in the oven.
Roasting until the skin is charred gives a smoky flavour; underbaked eggplant tastes bitter and stays stringy.
Draining the flesh stops the dip turning watery and diluting the lemon and garlic.
Adding the oil gradually helps it blend into the flesh for a creamier texture.
variations: Add 1 tbsp red wine vinegar in place of half the lemon juice for a sharper, more traditional taste.
Char the eggplants directly over a gas flame or barbecue, turning often for 15–20 minutes, for a stronger smoky flavour.
recipe.storage: Refrigerate in a covered container for up to 2 days. Bring to room temperature and stir before serving. Not suitable for freezing.

recipe.title: Korean Gyeran Jjim
recipe.summary: Cloudlike steamed eggs with spring onions, gently cooked until soft and trembling.

stages.title: Make the egg mixture
steps: Let the vegetable stock cool to room temperature if it is warm, as hot stock will scramble the eggs.
Crack the eggs into a bowl and whisk gently with a fork until the whites and yolks are combined, without creating foam.
Stir in the cooled stock, fish sauce and salt until evenly mixed.
Pour the mixture through a fine sieve into a heatproof 1 litre bowl, then skim off any surface bubbles with a spoon.
Thinly slice the spring onions and set them aside.

stages.title: Set up the steamer
steps: Place a steaming rack or upturned heatproof saucer in a large wide pot and add water to reach 3 cm below the rack.
Bring the water to a gentle simmer over medium heat, then reduce to medium-low so it simmers barely.
Cover the bowl of egg mixture loosely with foil, leaving a small gap for steam to escape.

stages.title: Steam the custard
steps: Carefully lower the covered bowl onto the rack, put the lid on the pot and steam over medium-low heat for 12–15 minutes.
Check at 12 minutes by gently shaking the bowl: the custard is ready when the surface is set and the centre has only a slight wobble, with no liquid egg when pressed lightly with a spoon.
If the centre is still liquid, re-cover and steam for 2–3 minutes more, then check again.

stages.title: Rest and serve
steps: Turn off the heat and lift the bowl out with oven mitts, taking care with the hot steam.
Rest the custard for 2 minutes so it finishes setting.
Scatter the spring onions over the top, drizzle with the sesame oil and serve hot in the bowl.

tips: Straining the egg mixture removes the stringy egg white, which gives a smooth, even custard.
Keep the water at a barely-there simmer, because a hard boil makes the custard curdle and develop holes.
Loose foil stops condensation dripping onto the surface and leaving pockmarks.
Whisk gently without foaming the eggs, as bubbles turn into a spongy texture when steamed.
variations: Stir 1 tbsp finely grated carrot into the egg mixture for extra sweetness and colour.
Add 1 tsp kimchi juice or a pinch of chilli flakes to the egg mixture for a gentle kick.
recipe.storage: Best eaten straight away. Leftovers keep covered in the fridge for up to 2 days; reheat gently in the microwave on medium for 30–60 seconds, until just warm.

recipe.title: Spanish Espinacas con Garbanzos
recipe.summary: Chickpeas and spinach simmered with smoky paprika, cumin and a garlic-bread thickener.
ingredients: 2 x 400 g cans chickpeas, drained and rinsed
2 slices bread, stale or day-old, torn into pieces

stages.title: Prepare the ingredients
steps: Drain and rinse the chickpeas, then leave them in the colander to drain well.
Tear the bread into rough 2 cm pieces and thinly slice the garlic.
Wash the baby spinach if needed and dry it well.
Cut the lemon into wedges.

stages.title: Fry the bread and garlic
steps: Heat 2 tbsp of the olive oil in a large, deep frying pan over medium heat.
Fry the bread, stirring often, for 2–3 minutes until golden all over.
Add the garlic and cook for 30 seconds until fragrant and pale golden, taking care it doesn't burn.
Tip the bread and garlic into a small blender, leaving the oil in the pan.

stages.title: Make the picada paste
steps: Add the paprika, ground cumin, red wine vinegar and 100 ml of the stock to the blender.
Blend for 1 minute until a thick, mostly smooth paste forms, scraping down the sides once.

stages.title: Simmer the chickpeas
steps: Return the pan to medium heat with the remaining 1 tbsp olive oil and add the chickpeas. Stir for 1 minute to coat.
Pour in the remaining 150 ml stock and simmer for 8 minutes until the liquid has reduced by about half.
Stir in the bread paste and the salt, and cook for 3 minutes until the sauce is thick and clings to the chickpeas.

stages.title: Wilt the spinach and serve
steps: Add the spinach a handful at a time over medium heat, stirring each batch in until it wilts before adding the next, about 3–4 minutes in total.
Simmer for 2 minutes more until the sauce is thick and no watery liquid pools.
Season with black pepper and extra salt if needed, and serve hot with the lemon wedges.

tips: Stale bread soaks up the oil and thickens the sauce; fresh bread turns gluey, so dry it in a low oven if needed.
Fry the garlic only until pale golden, as browned garlic turns bitter and will dominate the paste.
Add the spinach in batches so the pan stays hot and the leaves wilt rather than stew and release excess water.
The red wine vinegar brightens the earthy chickpeas and cuts through the richness of the fried bread.
variations: Add 100 g diced chorizo, fried in the pan before the chickpeas, for a smoky meaty version.
Stir through a handful of toasted pine nuts and sultanas at the end for a Sevillan-style finish.
recipe.storage: Refrigerate in a covered container for up to 3 days. Reheat gently in a pan over low heat with a splash of water or stock until piping hot. Does not freeze well because of the spinach.

recipe.title: Egyptian Basbousa
recipe.summary: Tender semolina cake soaked in fragrant lemon syrup and topped with toasted almonds.
ingredients: 100 g butter, melted, plus extra for greasing
1 lemon, half juiced (about 2 tbsp) and the other half cut into 2 strips of peel

stages.title: Make the batter
steps: Heat the oven to 180°C (160°C fan) and grease a 20 cm square cake tin with a little extra butter, then line the base with baking paper.
In a large bowl, stir together the semolina, caster sugar and baking powder.
Add the yoghurt and the melted butter and stir until just combined into a thick, spoonable batter.
Rest the batter in the bowl for 5 minutes so the semolina absorbs some liquid.

stages.title: Shape and score
steps: Spoon the batter into the tin and smooth the top with a wet spatula.
Cut the batter into 12 diamonds or squares with a knife, cutting almost to the base.
Press one almond into the centre of each piece.

stages.title: Bake the cake
steps: Bake on the middle rack for 30–35 minutes, until deep golden on top and a skewer inserted in the centre comes out clean.
While the cake bakes, put the white sugar, water and lemon peel strips in a small saucepan over medium heat and stir until the sugar dissolves.
Bring to a boil, then reduce to medium-low and simmer for 8 minutes until slightly syrupy.
Remove from the heat, stir in the lemon juice and discard the peel strips.

stages.title: Soak and rest
steps: Pour the warm syrup slowly and evenly over the cake as soon as it comes out of the oven, while the cake is still hot.
Re-cut along the score lines if they have closed up.
Leave the cake in the tin for at least 1 hour, until it has absorbed the syrup and cooled, before lifting out the pieces.

tips: Pouring warm syrup over a hot cake lets the semolina soak it up evenly, so the pieces stay moist rather than soggy on the bottom.
Scoring before baking gives clean pieces, because the syrupy cake is too tender to cut neatly afterwards.
Resting the batter for 5 minutes softens the semolina grains, which gives a tender crumb instead of a gritty one.
variations: Replace the lemon juice in the syrup with 1 tsp orange blossom water if you have it, added once the syrup is off the heat.
Stir 3 tbsp desiccated coconut into the dry ingredients for a coconut basbousa.
recipe.storage: Keep covered at room temperature for 1 day or in the fridge for up to 3 days. Bring to room temperature before serving.

recipe.title: Turkish Mercimek Kofte
recipe.summary: Soft red lentil and bulgur patties seasoned with pepper paste, cumin and fresh herbs.

stages.title: Cook the lentils
steps: Rinse the red lentils in a sieve under cold water until the water runs mostly clear.
Place the lentils in a medium saucepan with 600 ml water and the salt, and bring to the boil over high heat.
Reduce the heat to medium-low and simmer, stirring often, for 12–15 minutes until the lentils have collapsed and the mixture is thick and mushy.
Take the pan off the heat.

stages.title: Hydrate the bulgur
steps: Stir the fine bulgur into the hot lentils until evenly combined.
Cover the pan with a lid and leave off the heat for 15 minutes, until the bulgur has swollen and absorbed the moisture and the mixture is a thick, firm paste.

stages.title: Make the onion base
steps: Heat the olive oil in a frying pan over medium heat.
Cook the diced onion, stirring often, for 6–7 minutes until soft and golden.
Stir in the tomato paste and ground cumin and cook for 1 minute until the paste darkens slightly and smells fragrant.

stages.title: Combine the mixture
steps: Scrape the onion mixture into the lentil and bulgur mixture and stir well.
Add the spring onions, parsley and lemon juice and mix, using damp hands, until the mixture is evenly coloured and holds together when squeezed.
Leave to cool for 5 minutes until comfortable to handle.

stages.title: Shape and serve
steps: With damp hands, take a heaped tablespoon of mixture, squeeze it in your fist and press into a small oval about 6 cm long, leaving finger marks.
Repeat with the remaining mixture to make about 20 kofte.
Arrange the kofte on a platter with the lettuce leaves and serve warm or at room temperature, wrapped in the leaves with a squeeze of extra lemon if you like.

tips: Rinsing the lentils removes surface starch and foam, so the cooked mixture is cleaner in flavour and less gluey.
Fine bulgur softens in the lentils' residual heat without cooking, so you get a firm, shapeable paste rather than a wet one.
Shape the kofte with damp hands because the warm mixture sticks to dry ones.
Frying the tomato paste briefly removes its raw edge and deepens the colour and flavour.
variations: Add 1 tsp chilli flakes with the cumin for a spicier kofte.
Stir 1 tbsp pomegranate molasses through the mixture with the lemon juice for a sweet-sour finish, if you have it.
recipe.storage: Refrigerate in a covered container for up to 3 days and serve cold or at room temperature. Freeze shaped kofte for up to 1 month and thaw in the fridge overnight.

recipe.title: Korean Sigeumchi Namul
recipe.summary: Tender spinach dressed with sesame oil, garlic and toasted sesame for a simple banchan.
ingredients: 2 bunches English spinach (about 300 g), roots trimmed

stages.title: Wash and set up
steps: Wash the spinach in a large bowl of cold water, lifting it out and changing the water until no grit remains at the bottom.
Trim the roots, keeping the stems attached so the leaves hold together.
Bring a large pot with 2 litres water to a rolling boil over high heat and stir in the salt.
Half-fill a large bowl with cold water and ice for cooling the spinach.

stages.title: Blanch and cool
steps: Add the spinach to the boiling water and push it under with tongs. Cook for 30–45 seconds, until the stems are just tender and the leaves are bright green.
Lift the spinach straight into the iced water and leave for 1 minute until cold, which keeps the colour bright.
Gather the spinach into a bundle and squeeze firmly with both hands until no more water drips out.
Cut the bundle crosswise into 5 cm lengths and shake the pieces loose into a bowl.

stages.title: Season and serve
steps: Add the garlic, sesame oil and soy sauce to the spinach.
Toss with your hands for about 30 seconds, gently pulling the strands apart so the seasoning coats every piece.
Taste and add a pinch more salt only if needed, as the soy is already salty.
Pile into a serving bowl and scatter over the sesame seeds and spring onion.

tips: Squeezing out the water is the key step: wet spinach dilutes the dressing and makes the dish bland and soggy.
Blanching for under a minute keeps the spinach tender with a little bite; longer turns it limp and dull.
Grate the garlic finely so it blends into the dressing, as raw chunks taste harsh in such a simple dish.
variations: Add 1 tsp gochujang to the dressing for a mild chilli kick.
Replace the soy sauce with 1 tsp fish sauce for a more savoury, traditional-style seasoning (not vegetarian).
recipe.storage: Refrigerate in a covered container for up to 2 days. Serve cold or at room temperature; it is best eaten the day it is made as it releases water on standing.

recipe.title: Chinese Liangban Huanggua
recipe.summary: Smashed cucumber in a punchy black-vinegar dressing with garlic, chilli and sesame.

stages.title: Smash the cucumbers
steps: Trim the ends from the cucumbers and lay them on a board.
Smash each one firmly with the flat side of a cleaver or a rolling pin until it splits and cracks along its length.
Tear or cut the cucumber into bite-sized chunks, about 3 cm.

stages.title: Salt and drain
steps: Toss the cucumber chunks with the salt in a bowl.
Leave them to stand for 10 minutes so they release water.
Tip the cucumbers into a colander and drain well, shaking off the liquid, then pat dry with paper towel.

stages.title: Make the dressing
steps: In a large bowl, whisk the garlic, black vinegar, soy sauce, chilli oil, sesame oil and sugar.
Keep whisking for about 1 minute until the sugar has dissolved and no grains remain.

stages.title: Toss and serve
steps: Add the drained cucumbers to the dressing and toss until every piece is coated.
Serve straight away for the crispest texture, or chill for up to 15 minutes if you want it cold.

tips: Smashing rather than slicing creates rough, craggy edges that grip the dressing much better than clean cuts.
Salting draws out water that would otherwise dilute the dressing and make the salad soggy.
Black vinegar gives a malty, mellow tang; if you can't find it, use 1 tbsp rice vinegar plus 1 tsp balsamic vinegar.
Dress the cucumbers just before serving, as the vinegar and salt keep drawing out liquid.
variations: Add 1 tbsp roasted peanuts, roughly chopped, and a handful of chopped coriander for crunch and freshness.
Replace the chilli oil with 1 tsp sesame seeds and a pinch of chilli flakes for a drier, toasty version.
recipe.storage: Refrigerate covered for up to 2 days; the cucumbers will soften and release liquid, so drain before serving.

recipe.title: Persian Adas Polo
recipe.summary: Fragrant rice layered with lentils, caramelised onions, raisins and warm cinnamon.
ingredients: 40 g butter, cut into small pieces
1 tbsp salt, plus 1/2 tsp for the lentils and extra for the rice water

stages.title: Soak the rice and slice the onions
steps: Rinse the rice in a sieve under cold running water until the water runs almost clear.
Put the rice in a bowl with 1 tbsp salt and cover with 1 litre cold water, then leave to soak for 20 minutes.
While the rice soaks, peel and thinly slice the onions and measure out the sultanas, cinnamon and butter.

stages.title: Cook the lentils
steps: Put the lentils in a saucepan with 750 ml water and bring to the boil over high heat.
Reduce the heat to medium-low and simmer for 15–20 minutes, until tender but still holding their shape.
Drain the lentils, stir in 1/2 tsp salt and the black pepper, and set aside.

stages.title: Caramelise the onions
steps: Heat the oil in a large frying pan over medium heat.
Add the sliced onions and cook, stirring often, for 15–18 minutes, until deep golden brown.
Stir in the sultanas and cinnamon and cook for 2 minutes, until the sultanas plump up.
Stir half the onion mixture through the lentils and keep the rest for the top.

stages.title: Parboil the rice
steps: Bring 2 litres water and a generous pinch of salt to the boil in a large non-stick pot over high heat.
Drain the soaked rice, add it to the boiling water and cook for 5–6 minutes, until the grains are soft outside but still firm in the centre.
Drain the rice in a sieve and rinse briefly with warm water.

stages.title: Layer the pot
steps: Wipe out the pot and return it to the stove over medium heat with half the butter, letting it melt.
Spoon in a third of the rice, then half the lentil mixture, repeating with another third of rice, the remaining lentils and the last of the rice, mounding it into a pyramid.
Poke 4–5 holes through the mound with the handle of a wooden spoon to let the steam escape.
Dot the remaining butter over the top.

stages.title: Steam and serve
steps: Wrap the pot lid in a clean tea towel and cover the pot tightly.
Cook over medium-high heat for 5 minutes until steam builds, then reduce to the lowest heat and steam for 25 minutes, until the rice is fluffy and tender and a golden crust has formed on the base.
Spoon the rice onto a platter, scatter the reserved onion mixture over the top, and break up the crust to serve alongside.

tips: Soaking the rice in salted water lets the grains cook evenly and lengthen without breaking.
Stop the lentils while they still hold their shape, as they keep softening during steaming and turn mushy if overcooked.
A tea towel under the lid absorbs condensation so the rice steams fluffy rather than soggy.
A non-stick pot helps the crust (tahdig) release in one piece; keep the heat low so it browns without burning.
variations: Add 1/2 tsp ground turmeric and a pinch of saffron threads steeped in 2 tbsp hot water, drizzled over the top before steaming.
Stir 2 tbsp chopped dates through the onions in place of the sultanas for a deeper sweetness.
recipe.storage: Cool quickly, then refrigerate in a covered container for up to 2 days. Reheat with a splash of water in a covered pan or microwave until steaming hot throughout.

recipe.title: French Tarte Fine aux Pommes
recipe.summary: Thin apple slices baked on crisp buttery puff pastry with a glossy apricot glaze.
ingredients: 1 sheet puff pastry, thawed (about 25 cm square)

stages.title: Prepare the pastry base
steps: Heat the oven to 200°C (180°C fan) and line a large baking tray with baking paper.
Lay the puff pastry sheet on the tray.
Use a small sharp knife to score a border about 1.5 cm in from the edge, cutting only halfway through the pastry.
Prick the pastry inside the border all over with a fork so the centre doesn't puff up too much.

stages.title: Slice and arrange the apples
steps: Juice the lemon into a large bowl.
Halve and core the apples, leaving the skin on, then slice them very thinly (2–3 mm) and toss them in the lemon juice so they don't brown.
Arrange the apple slices in slightly overlapping rows inside the scored border, covering the pastry completely.
Brush the apples with the melted butter and sprinkle evenly with the caster sugar.

stages.title: Bake the tart
steps: Bake the tart on the middle shelf for 30 minutes, until the pastry border is puffed and deep golden and the apple edges are browned.
If the apples are browning faster than the pastry, cover the tart loosely with foil for the last 5–10 minutes.
Check that the pastry underneath is golden and crisp by lifting an edge with a spatula.

stages.title: Glaze the tart
steps: While the tart bakes, or just before it comes out, put the apricot jam and 1 tsp water in a small saucepan over low heat.
Stir for 1–2 minutes until the jam is runny, then brush it over the hot apples and the pastry border.

stages.title: Cool and serve
steps: Leave the tart on the tray for 10 minutes so the pastry firms up.
Slide it onto a board and cut into 4 pieces with a sharp knife, using a gentle sawing motion.

tips: Slice the apples very thinly so they soften and caramelise in the time the pastry takes to bake.
Scoring only halfway through the pastry lets the border rise while the centre stays flat.
Brushing the apricot glaze on while the tart is hot helps it spread thinly and set to a shine.
Use a firm apple such as granny smith or pink lady, as it holds its shape rather than turning to mush.
variations: Swap the apples for firm, ripe pears and add a pinch of ground cinnamon to the sugar.
Spread 2 tbsp of the apricot jam over the pastry before adding the apples for a fruitier base.
recipe.storage: Best eaten the day it is made. Keep leftovers loosely covered in the fridge for up to 2 days and reheat in a 180°C (160°C fan) oven for 8–10 minutes to re-crisp the pastry.

recipe.title: Italian Gnocchi with Brown Butter and Sage
recipe.summary: Pillowy potato gnocchi tossed in nutty browned butter with crisp sage leaves and Parmesan.
ingredients: 1 tbsp salt, for the cooking water

stages.title: Prepare the ingredients
steps: Finely grate the parmesan into a bowl.
Zest the lemon with a fine grater, then cut the lemon into wedges for serving.
Pick the 16 sage leaves and pat them dry with paper towel so they crisp rather than spit.
Cut the butter into 4 or 5 pieces so it melts evenly.

stages.title: Brown the butter and crisp the sage
steps: Bring 3 litres water to the boil in a large pot over high heat and stir in the salt.
Melt the butter in a large frying pan over medium heat, swirling occasionally, until it foams.
Add the sage leaves and cook for 1–2 minutes, until the leaves are crisp and the butter smells nutty and turns golden brown.
Remove the pan from the heat and lift the sage out onto paper towel, leaving the butter in the pan.

stages.title: Cook the gnocchi
steps: Add the gnocchi to the boiling water and cook for 2–3 minutes, until they float to the surface.
Scoop out 100 ml of the cooking water, then lift the gnocchi out with a slotted spoon.

stages.title: Toss and serve
steps: Return the pan of brown butter to medium heat and add the gnocchi with the reserved cooking water.
Toss gently for 1–2 minutes, until the gnocchi are lightly golden and coated in a glossy sauce.
Take the pan off the heat and stir through the lemon zest, half the parmesan and a good grind of black pepper.
Divide among 4 bowls, scatter over the crisp sage and the remaining parmesan, and serve with the lemon wedges.

tips: Pat the sage dry before frying, as water makes the butter spit and the leaves go limp instead of crisp.
Watch the butter closely once it foams. It goes from golden to burnt in under a minute, so pull the pan off the heat as soon as it smells nutty.
The starchy cooking water helps the butter and gnocchi come together into a smooth, glossy sauce rather than a greasy one.
Lifting the gnocchi out with a slotted spoon avoids draining the pot and keeps them from sticking together.
variations: Add 100 g toasted walnuts, roughly chopped, for crunch and a nutty flavour.
Stir through 2 handfuls of baby spinach with the gnocchi and cook for 1 minute until wilted.
recipe.storage: Refrigerate in an airtight container for up to 2 days. Reheat in a frying pan over medium heat with a splash of water for 3–4 minutes until piping hot. The sage will soften.

recipe.title: Indonesian Gado Gado
recipe.summary: Blanched vegetables, tofu and eggs with a rich peanut dressing and crunchy toppings.
ingredients: 600 g potatoes, peeled and cut into 2 cm chunks
200 g green beans, trimmed and halved
200 g firm tofu, cut into 2 cm cubes

stages.title: Cook the potatoes and eggs
steps: Put the potatoes in a large pot, cover with cold water, add the salt and bring to the boil over high heat.
Reduce to medium heat and simmer for 10–12 minutes, until a knife slides in easily, then lift out with a slotted spoon and drain.
Lower the eggs into the same boiling water and cook over medium heat for 8–9 minutes, until the whites are set and the yolks are just firm.
Cool the eggs in cold water for 5 minutes, then peel and cut into quarters.

stages.title: Blanch the vegetables
steps: Bring a pot of water to the boil over high heat and cook the green beans for 3 minutes, until bright green and just tender.
Lift out the beans and add the cabbage to the water for 1 minute, until just wilted.
Add the bean sprouts for 20 seconds, then drain everything and rinse under cold water to stop the cooking.
Slice the cucumber while the vegetables drain.

stages.title: Fry the tofu
steps: Pat the tofu dry with paper towel so it browns rather than steams.
Heat the vegetable oil in a large frying pan over medium-high heat.
Fry the tofu for 6–8 minutes, turning occasionally, until golden on all sides, then drain on paper towel.

stages.title: Make the peanut sauce
steps: Heat a small saucepan over low heat and cook the garlic and chilli for 1 minute, until fragrant.
Stir in the peanut butter, kecap manis, soy sauce and 150 ml water, whisking for 2–3 minutes until smooth and warmed through.
Take off the heat and stir in the lime juice, adding a splash more water if the sauce is too thick to pour.

stages.title: Assemble
steps: Arrange the potatoes, green beans, cabbage, bean sprouts, cucumber, tofu and eggs on a large platter or four plates.
Spoon the warm peanut sauce over the top and serve straight away.

tips: Start the potatoes in cold water so the chunks cook evenly through to the middle without falling apart on the outside.
Rinsing the blanched vegetables under cold water keeps them crisp and bright green.
Patting the tofu dry before frying removes surface moisture, giving a golden crust.
Thin the sauce with water rather than oil, as it thickens as it cools.
variations: Swap the tofu for tempeh, fried the same way until golden.
Add a handful of crushed peanuts or fried shallots over the top for crunch.
recipe.storage: Store the sauce and the components separately in airtight containers in the fridge for up to 2 days. Serve the vegetables cold or at room temperature, and warm the sauce gently with a splash of water.

recipe.title: Indian Besan Chilla
recipe.summary: Golden chickpea-flour pancakes speckled with onion, coriander, chilli and cumin.

stages.title: Make the batter
steps: Sift the chickpea flour into a large bowl and add the salt and ground cumin.
Pour in 260 ml water gradually, whisking until the batter is smooth and free of lumps.
The batter should be thick but pourable, like pancake batter.

stages.title: Add the vegetables
steps: Finely chop the onion, green chilli and coriander if not already done.
Fold the onion, chilli and coriander into the batter.

stages.title: Rest the batter
steps: Cover the bowl and leave the batter at room temperature for 15 minutes so the flour hydrates and the chillas hold together.
Stir the batter again. If it has thickened too much to spread, loosen it with 1–2 tbsp extra water.

stages.title: Cook the chillas
steps: Heat a large non-stick frying pan over medium heat and brush with a little of the vegetable oil.
Pour in about 1/2 cup batter and spread it quickly into a thin round about 18 cm wide with the back of the ladle.
Cook for about 3 minutes, until the surface looks set, bubbles appear and the edges lift away from the pan.
Drizzle a little more oil around the edge, flip and cook for 1–2 minutes, until golden with brown spots and cooked through with no wet batter left.

stages.title: Repeat and serve
steps: Repeat with the remaining batter and oil over medium heat to make 6 chillas, using the same visual cues each time.
Keep the cooked chillas warm under a clean tea towel while you cook the rest.
Serve hot with the chutney.

tips: Resting the batter lets the chickpea flour absorb the water, which gives a tender chilla that is less likely to taste raw or tear.
Keep the heat at medium: a hotter pan browns the outside before the batter in the centre has set.
Spread the batter thinly and quickly as soon as it hits the pan, because it sets fast and thick chillas turn doughy inside.
variations: Add 1/2 cup grated zucchini, squeezed dry, to the batter for extra moisture and a softer texture.
Scatter crumbled paneer over each chilla just after spreading the batter for a more filling breakfast.
recipe.storage: Cool completely and refrigerate in an airtight container for up to 2 days. Reheat in a dry frying pan over medium heat for 1–2 minutes each side until hot through.

recipe.title: South African Bobotie
recipe.summary: Curried minced beef baked beneath a golden savoury egg custard with raisins and warming spices.

stages.title: Soak the bread and prepare the base
steps: Heat the oven to 180°C (160°C fan) and lightly grease a 20 x 25 cm baking dish.
Tear the bread into a bowl and pour over 125 ml of the milk. Leave to soak for 10 minutes.
Finely chop the onion and garlic while the bread soaks.
Squeeze the bread lightly with your hands, returning the squeezed liquid to the bowl. Set the bread and the liquid aside separately.

stages.title: Cook the spiced mince
steps: Heat the olive oil in a large frying pan over medium heat. Cook the onion for 4–5 minutes, stirring, until soft and translucent.
Add the garlic and curry powder and stir for 1 minute until fragrant.
Add the beef mince, breaking up the lumps with a wooden spoon. Cook over medium-high heat for 6–8 minutes, until browned all over and no pink remains.
Remove from the heat and stir in the squeezed bread, vinegar, sultanas, chutney, salt and pepper, mashing the bread into the mince until evenly combined.

stages.title: Assemble the bobotie
steps: Spoon the mince mixture into the baking dish and press down firmly with the back of a spoon to make an even, compact layer.
Whisk the eggs with the remaining 125 ml milk and the reserved liquid from the bread until smooth.
Pour the egg mixture evenly over the mince, then press the bay leaves gently onto the surface.

stages.title: Bake until set
steps: Bake for 30–35 minutes, until the custard topping is golden and set and no longer wobbles when the dish is gently shaken.
Rest for 5 minutes, then remove the bay leaves and cut into squares to serve.

tips: Pressing the mince down firmly gives a compact base, so the custard sits on top as a distinct layer instead of seeping through.
Mashing the soaked bread into the mince keeps the meat moist and gives the bobotie its soft, tender texture.
Resting the dish for 5 minutes lets the custard finish setting so the squares hold their shape when cut.
Using fatty beef mince gives a richer, juicier result than very lean mince.
variations: Swap the sultanas for chopped dried apricots for a tangier, fruitier flavour.
Scatter 2 tbsp flaked almonds over the custard before baking for a crunchy topping.
recipe.storage: Refrigerate in an airtight container for up to 3 days, or freeze for up to 2 months. Reheat until steaming hot throughout.

recipe.title: Scottish Cullen Skink
recipe.summary: Creamy smoked haddock chowder with tender potatoes, leek and parsley.
ingredients: 500 g potatoes, peeled and cut into 1.5 cm cubes
1 leek, white and pale green part only, halved lengthways and thinly sliced
1/4 tsp salt, plus extra to taste

stages.title: Prepare the vegetables
steps: Peel the potatoes and cut them into 1.5 cm cubes so they cook evenly.
Trim the leek, halve it lengthways, rinse out any grit and slice it thinly.
Finely chop the onion.
Finely chop the parsley and set it aside for serving.

stages.title: Poach the haddock
steps: Place the haddock skin-side down in a large saucepan and add the milk, 300 ml water and the bay leaf.
Heat over medium heat for 3–4 minutes until the liquid just begins to simmer, then reduce to low and poach for 5–6 minutes, until the fish flakes easily when pressed with a fork.
Lift the fish onto a plate with a slotted spoon and strain the liquid into a jug, discarding the bay leaf.
Peel the skin from the fish and discard it, then flake the flesh into large pieces, removing any bones. Cover and set aside.

stages.title: Soften the leek and onion
steps: Wipe out the saucepan and melt the butter over medium heat.
Add the leek and onion and cook, stirring often, for 6–8 minutes, until soft and translucent but not browned.

stages.title: Simmer the soup
steps: Add the potatoes to the pan and stir to coat in the butter for 1 minute.
Pour in the strained poaching liquid and bring to a simmer over medium heat, about 2 minutes.
Reduce the heat to medium-low and simmer, partly covered, for 10–12 minutes, until the potatoes are tender when pierced with a knife.
Crush about a quarter of the potatoes against the side of the pan with a potato masher, so the soup thickens but stays chunky.

stages.title: Finish and serve
steps: Stir in the cream and the flaked haddock and warm over low heat for 3–4 minutes, until steaming hot. Do not let it boil.
Season with the pepper and the salt, then taste and add more salt only if needed, as the haddock is salty.
Stir through the parsley and ladle into warm bowls.

tips: Undyed smoked haddock gives the best flavour; the poaching liquid carries the smoke through the whole soup, so don't discard it.
Keep the soup below a boil once the cream and fish go in, as boiling can split the cream and make the fish tough.
Mashing some of the potato thickens the soup without flour, which keeps the traditional creamy but chunky texture.
Taste before salting, because smoked fish and its poaching liquid are already salty.
variations: Stir in 1 cup of corn kernels with the potatoes for a sweeter, chunkier soup.
Swap half the potato for peeled, cubed sweet potato for a slightly sweeter soup.
recipe.storage: Refrigerate in an airtight container for up to 2 days. Reheat gently over low heat until steaming hot, without boiling. Not recommended to freeze, as the potato and cream can turn grainy.

recipe.title: British Ploughman's Lunch
recipe.summary: A rustic plate of mature cheddar, crusty bread, pickles, apple and crisp vegetables.
ingredients: 4 tbsp fruit chutney or sweet pickle

stages.title: Bring the cheese to room temperature
steps: Take the cheddar out of the fridge and leave it on the bench, still wrapped, for 10 minutes so the flavour and texture soften.
Meanwhile, spoon the chutney into a small bowl and put the butter in a second small bowl to soften.

stages.title: Prepare the vegetables
steps: Wash the cucumber and radishes, then trim the radish tops and roots, leaving a little green stem if you like.
Cut the cucumber into thick batons about 7 cm long.
Cut the radishes in half lengthways.
Drain the pickled onions and set them aside on a small plate.

stages.title: Slice the cheese and apples
steps: Unwrap the cheddar and cut it into 4 thick wedges or chunky slices.
Squeeze the juice of the lemon into a bowl with 250 ml water.
Core the apples and cut each into 8 wedges, then toss the wedges in the lemon water for 30 seconds and drain well so they stay pale and crisp.

stages.title: Warm the bread
steps: Heat the oven to 180°C (160°C fan).
Place the bread slices directly on the oven rack and warm for 5 minutes, until the crust is crisp and the inside is warm.
Spread the softened butter over the warm bread.

stages.title: Assemble the platter
steps: Divide the cheese, apple wedges, cucumber, radishes and pickled onions among 4 plates or one large board.
Add a spoonful of chutney to each serving and serve straight away with the buttered warm bread.

tips: Use a mature or vintage cheddar, because its sharp, savoury flavour stands up to the sweet chutney and tangy pickled onions.
Letting the cheese sit out for 10 minutes means it tastes fuller and slices more cleanly than straight from the fridge.
A short soak in lemon water slows browning on the apples, so they stay crisp and pale on the board.
Warming the bread briefly makes the crust crisp and helps the butter spread without tearing the slices.
variations: Add 4 hard-boiled eggs, boiled for 9–10 minutes until the yolks are firm, then peeled and halved, for a heartier plate.
Swap the cheddar for a crumbly cheese such as Cheshire or a wedge of blue cheese.
recipe.storage: Best eaten straight away. Wrap leftover cheese and keep the cut vegetables in airtight containers in the fridge for up to 2 days; bring the cheese to room temperature before serving again.

recipe.title: Nepalese Chicken Momo
recipe.summary: Steamed dumplings packed with ginger-scented chicken, spring onion and coriander.

stages.title: Make and rest the dough
steps: Combine the flour and 1/4 tsp of the salt in a large bowl.
Add 180 ml water gradually, mixing until a shaggy dough forms.
Knead on a lightly floured bench for 8 minutes until smooth and firm.
Cover the dough with a damp tea towel and rest for 30 minutes.

stages.title: Mix the filling
steps: Place the chicken mince in a bowl with the spring onions, ginger, garlic, onion and coriander.
Add the soy sauce, cumin, black pepper, the remaining 1/4 tsp salt and the oil.
Mix with your hands for 2 minutes until the filling looks sticky and well combined.

stages.title: Roll and fill the momo
steps: Divide the dough into 24 equal pieces and cover them with the damp tea towel.
Roll each piece on a lightly floured bench into a thin 9 cm circle, keeping the edges thinner than the centre.
Place 1 tablespoon of filling in the middle of a circle.
Pleat the edge around the filling, pinching to seal fully and twisting the top closed.
Repeat with the remaining dough and filling.

stages.title: Steam the momo
steps: Line a bamboo steamer with baking paper punched with holes, or lightly oil it, and bring water in a wok or pot to a boil over high heat.
Arrange a batch of momo in the steamer with 2 cm between them, then place the steamer over the boiling water and reduce to medium-high heat.
Steam each batch for 12–15 minutes, until the dough is translucent and the chicken is cooked through with no pink remaining.
Serve straight away while hot.

tips: Roll the edges of each circle thinner than the centre so the pleated top isn't doughy and the base can hold the filling without tearing.
Keep unused dough pieces under a damp tea towel because dry dough cracks and won't seal.
Finely chopped onion in the filling releases moisture as it steams, which keeps the lean chicken mince juicy.
Oil or line the steamer so the momo don't stick to it and tear their bases.
variations: Serve with a tomato chilli achar made from blended tomatoes, chilli, garlic and coriander.
Pan-fry the steamed momo in a little oil over medium heat for 3 minutes until the bases are golden.
recipe.storage: Refrigerate in an airtight container for up to 3 days or freeze uncooked on a tray, then bag, for up to 2 months. Re-steam for 8–10 minutes (15 minutes from frozen) until steaming hot throughout.

recipe.title: Persian Fesenjan
recipe.summary: Tender chicken braised in a dark, tangy walnut and pomegranate sauce with gentle cinnamon warmth.
ingredients: 700 g chicken thigh, skinless and boneless, cut into large chunks
1 tbsp white sugar, optional, to balance the sourness

stages.title: Toast and grind the walnuts
steps: Heat a dry frying pan over medium heat and toast the walnuts for 4–5 minutes, stirring often, until fragrant and a shade darker.
Tip the walnuts onto a plate and cool for 5 minutes.
Pulse the cooled walnuts in a food processor until finely ground and sandy, stopping before they turn to paste.

stages.title: Prepare the chicken and onion
steps: Finely dice the onion.
Cut the chicken into large chunks.
Season the chicken with the salt and black pepper.

stages.title: Brown the chicken and soften the onion
steps: Heat the olive oil in a large heavy-based pot over medium-high heat.
Brown the chicken in two batches for 3–4 minutes per batch, turning once, until golden on the outside. Transfer to a plate.
Reduce the heat to medium, add the onion to the same pot and cook for 6–7 minutes, stirring, until soft and lightly golden.

stages.title: Simmer the walnut sauce
steps: Stir the ground walnuts and cinnamon into the onion and cook for 1 minute over medium heat until fragrant.
Pour in the chicken stock and stir, scraping up any browned bits from the base of the pot.
Return the chicken and any juices to the pot and bring to a gentle simmer.
Cover with the lid slightly ajar and cook over low heat for 30 minutes, stirring every 10 minutes, until the chicken is tender and cooked through with no pink remaining.

stages.title: Add the molasses and thicken
steps: Stir in the pomegranate molasses and the sugar, if using.
Simmer uncovered over low heat for 15 minutes, stirring occasionally, until the sauce is thick, glossy and dark, with the oil from the walnuts rising to the surface.
Cook the rice according to the packet while the sauce reduces.
Taste and add a little more sugar if too sour, or a pinch of salt if flat, then serve over the rice.

tips: Toasting the walnuts first deepens their flavour and reduces any bitterness in the finished sauce.
Grind the walnuts only until sandy; over-processing releases oil and makes the sauce greasy before it has simmered.
Pomegranate molasses varies in sourness and sweetness between brands, so add the sugar only after tasting at the end.
Stir regularly during the long simmer because the ground walnuts settle and catch on the base of the pot.
variations: Use duck legs instead of chicken, browning them skin-side down first and simmering for about 1 hour 15 minutes until the meat is very tender.
Replace the chicken with 400 g pumpkin chunks and use vegetable stock for a vegetarian version, simmering for 25 minutes until the pumpkin is tender.
recipe.storage: Refrigerate in an airtight container for up to 3 days, or freeze for up to 2 months. Reheat gently on the stove until steaming hot throughout, adding a splash of water if the sauce has thickened.

recipe.title: Swedish Cinnamon Buns
recipe.summary: Soft cardamom-scented buns spiralled with buttery cinnamon sugar and finished with pearl sugar.

stages.title: Make the dough
steps: Warm the milk and 50 g of the butter in a small saucepan over low heat for 2–3 minutes, until the butter melts and the milk is lukewarm, not hot. Remove from the heat.
In a large bowl, combine the flour, 50 g of the caster sugar, the dried yeast, ground cardamom and salt.
Pour in the milk mixture and stir to form a shaggy dough.
Knead on a lightly floured bench for 8–10 minutes, until smooth, elastic and slightly tacky.

stages.title: First rise
steps: Place the dough in a clean large bowl and cover with a tea towel.
Leave in a warm spot for 1 hour, until doubled in size.

stages.title: Fill and shape
steps: Mix 50 g of the soft butter, the remaining 40 g caster sugar and the ground cinnamon into a smooth paste.
Roll the dough on a floured bench into a 30 x 40 cm rectangle.
Spread the cinnamon paste evenly over the dough, leaving a 1 cm border along one long edge.
Roll up tightly from the opposite long edge, finishing at the clean border, then slice into 12 even rounds.
Place the buns cut side up on two baking trays lined with baking paper, spaced apart.

stages.title: Second rise
steps: Cover the trays loosely with tea towels and leave in a warm spot for 30 minutes, until puffy and springy when pressed gently.
In the last 15 minutes, heat the oven to 220°C (200°C fan).

stages.title: Bake and finish
steps: Beat the egg and brush it over the buns.
Bake for 10–12 minutes, swapping the trays halfway, until deep golden and the buns sound hollow when tapped underneath.
Melt the remaining 30 g butter and brush it over the hot buns, then sprinkle with the white sugar.
Cool on the trays for 10 minutes before serving.

tips: Heat the milk only until lukewarm, because hot milk kills the yeast and the dough won't rise.
Keep the dough slightly tacky, as extra flour makes the buns dry and dense.
Roll the log tightly so the buns hold their spiral and don't unwind in the oven.
Brushing the hot buns with butter and sprinkling with sugar keeps the crust soft and lightly sweet.
variations: Add an extra 1/2 tsp ground cardamom to the cinnamon filling for a stronger Swedish flavour.
Skip the sugar topping and drizzle the cooled buns with a glaze of 1/2 cup icing sugar mixed with 1 tbsp milk.
recipe.storage: Store in an airtight container at room temperature for 2 days, or freeze for up to 1 month. Reheat in a 160°C (140°C fan) oven for 5–8 minutes, until warmed through.

recipe.title: Colombian Arepas con Queso
recipe.summary: Golden corn cakes with crisp edges and a soft, cheesy centre.

stages.title: Make the dough
steps: Whisk the cornmeal and salt together in a large bowl.
Pour in 300 ml warm water and 15 g of the butter, then mix with your hands until no dry patches remain.
Knead for 2 minutes until the dough is soft, smooth and doesn't stick to your hands. Add a little more cornmeal if it is sticky, or a splash of water if it cracks.

stages.title: Rest and add the cheese
steps: Cover the bowl with a clean tea towel and rest the dough for 5 minutes so the cornmeal absorbs the water.
Add the grated mozzarella and knead for 2 minutes until the cheese is evenly distributed through the dough.

stages.title: Shape the arepas
steps: Divide the dough into 8 equal portions and roll each into a ball.
Flatten each ball between your palms into a disc about 1.5 cm thick and 8 cm wide.
Pinch and smooth any cracks around the edges so the discs don't split while cooking.

stages.title: Cook the arepas
steps: Heat a large non-stick frying pan over medium heat and melt half the remaining butter (about 7 g).
Cook 4 arepas for 7 minutes on the first side, until a golden crust forms and they release easily from the pan.
Flip and cook for another 6 minutes, until golden on both sides, the cheese has melted and they sound hollow when tapped.

Transfer to a plate and wipe out the pan with paper towel. Return it to medium heat, melt the last of the butter and cook the remaining 4 arepas the same way, 7 minutes on the first side and 6 minutes on the second, until golden and hollow-sounding. Serve hot.

tips: Use precooked masarepa, not ordinary cornmeal or polenta, which will not form a dough.
Resting the dough lets the cornmeal hydrate fully, which stops the edges cracking when you shape the discs.
Medium heat cooks the arepas through and melts the cheese; high heat browns the outside before the centre is hot.
Coarsely grated mozzarella gives pockets of melted, stretchy cheese rather than a uniform dough.
variations: Split the hot arepas and fill with scrambled eggs.
Use half mozzarella and half grated feta for a saltier, tangier filling, and reduce the salt to 1/2 tsp.
recipe.storage: Best eaten fresh. Refrigerate leftovers in an airtight container for up to 2 days and reheat in a frying pan over medium-low heat for 3–4 minutes per side until hot through.

recipe.title: Japanese Miso-Glazed Aubergine
recipe.summary: Tender roasted aubergine lacquered with sweet-salty miso glaze and finished with toasted sesame.

stages.title: Score the eggplants
steps: Heat the oven to 210°C (190°C fan) and line a large baking tray with baking paper.
Halve the eggplants lengthways, keeping the stalks on if you like.
Score the cut flesh in a diamond pattern about 1 cm deep, taking care not to cut through the skin.
Place the eggplants cut-side up on the tray, brush with the vegetable oil and sprinkle with the salt.

stages.title: Roast the eggplants
steps: Roast on the middle shelf for 25 minutes, until the flesh is very soft and lightly browned.
While they roast, whisk the miso paste, mirin, sugar and soy sauce in a small bowl until smooth and the sugar has dissolved.
Cook the rice according to the packet while the eggplants roast, then keep covered to stay warm.
Toast the sesame seeds in a dry frying pan over medium heat for 2–3 minutes, shaking the pan, until golden, then tip onto a plate.

stages.title: Glaze and grill
steps: Switch the oven to grill on high and move the rack to the upper third.
Spread the miso mixture in a thin layer over the hot eggplant flesh.
Grill for 3–4 minutes, watching closely, until the glaze is bubbling and spotted dark brown at the edges.
Take out the tray and rest the eggplants for 2 minutes.

stages.title: Serve
steps: Divide the rice among 4 bowls or plates.
Place the eggplants on top of or alongside the rice.
Scatter over the spring onions and toasted sesame seeds, and serve hot.

tips: Scoring the flesh lets the heat reach the centre and gives the glaze small crevices to sink into, so the eggplant cooks evenly and tastes seasoned throughout.
Add the glaze only for the final grilling, because the sugar and miso scorch and turn bitter if they sit in a hot oven for long.
Roast until the flesh is completely soft and collapsing; undercooked eggplant is spongy and slightly bitter.
Spread the glaze thinly, as a thick layer burns on top before it can heat through.
variations: Use red miso in place of white for a deeper, saltier glaze, and reduce the soy sauce to 2 tsp.
Add 1 tsp grated ginger to the glaze for a sharper, fresher edge.
recipe.storage: Refrigerate the eggplant and rice separately in airtight containers for up to 3 days. Reheat the eggplant in a 180°C (160°C fan) oven for 10 minutes until hot through. Not suitable for freezing, as the flesh turns watery.

recipe.title: Greek Lemon Chicken and Potatoes
recipe.summary: Roasted chicken and potatoes soaked in lemon, oregano and garlic, with crisp edges and savoury pan juices.
ingredients: 900 g chicken thighs, bone-in and skin-on
800 g potatoes, peeled and cut into thick wedges

stages.title: Prepare the chicken and potatoes
steps: Heat the oven to 200°C (180°C fan).
Place the potato wedges in a large roasting dish in a single layer.
Place the chicken thighs among the potatoes, skin side up.
Season the chicken and potatoes with the salt and black pepper.

stages.title: Make the lemon dressing
steps: Juice both lemons into a jug to get about 80 ml juice.
Add the olive oil, garlic, oregano, paprika and chicken stock, then whisk to combine.
Pour the dressing evenly over the chicken and potatoes, turning the potatoes to coat them.

stages.title: Roast
steps: Roast for 25 minutes.
Turn the potatoes and spoon the pan juices over the chicken.
Roast for another 20 minutes, until the potatoes are tender when pierced with a knife and the chicken skin is golden.

stages.title: Brown and rest
steps: Increase the oven to 220°C (200°C fan) and roast for 10 minutes, until the potato edges are golden and the juices have reduced.
Check the thickest chicken thigh is cooked through, with no pink meat and clear juices.
Rest the dish for 5 minutes, then spoon the pan juices over to serve.

tips: Use a wide dish so the potatoes roast in a single layer. Crowding them makes them steam and turn soft rather than golden.
Bone-in, skin-on thighs stay juicy in the long roast, and the rendered fat flavours the potatoes.
Fresh lemon juice gives a brighter flavour than bottled juice, which can taste flat after roasting.
Turning the potatoes once lets the underside soak up the juices and brown evenly.
variations: Add 1 x 400 g can of artichoke hearts, drained, for the last 20 minutes of roasting.
Scatter 1/2 cup kalamata olives over the dish when you increase the oven temperature.
recipe.storage: Refrigerate in an airtight container for up to 3 days. Reheat in a 180°C oven until the chicken is steaming hot throughout. Potatoes soften when frozen, so freezing is not recommended.

recipe.title: French Chicken Chasseur
recipe.summary: Golden chicken braised with mushrooms, shallots, white wine and tomatoes in a glossy herb sauce.
ingredients: 8 chicken thigh cutlets, bone in, skin on (about 1 kg)

stages.title: Prepare and season
steps: Pat the chicken dry with paper towel so the skin browns rather than steams.
Season the chicken all over with the salt and black pepper.
Slice the mushrooms and finely chop the shallots and garlic.
Drain the canned diced tomatoes lightly if very watery, then measure out 200 g.
Chop the tarragon and set it aside.

stages.title: Brown the chicken
steps: Heat the olive oil and half the butter in a large deep frying pan or casserole over medium-high heat.
Cook the chicken skin-side down for 5–6 minutes, until deep golden.
Turn and brown the other side for 4 minutes, then transfer to a plate.
Pour off all but 1 tbsp of fat from the pan.

stages.title: Build the sauce
steps: Reduce the heat to medium and add the remaining butter. Cook the mushrooms for 6–7 minutes, until their liquid has evaporated and they are browned.
Add the shallots and garlic and cook for 2–3 minutes, until soft.
Stir in the tomato paste and flour and cook for 1 minute.
Pour in the white wine, scraping up the browned bits, and simmer for 3–4 minutes until reduced by half.

stages.title: Simmer and finish
steps: Add the chicken stock and the canned diced tomatoes and bring to a simmer over medium heat, about 3 minutes.
Return the chicken to the pan, skin-side up, with any juices from the plate.
Reduce the heat to medium-low, cover and simmer for 20 minutes.
Remove the lid and simmer for 5 minutes more, until the sauce thickens slightly and the chicken is cooked through with no pink near the bone and the juices run clear.
Stir through half the tarragon, then scatter the rest over to serve.

tips: Brown the mushrooms until their liquid has gone; this concentrates flavour and stops the sauce tasting watery.
Keep the chicken skin above the liquid while simmering so it stays partly crisp.
Bone-in thighs stay moist during the simmer, whereas breast can dry out.
Add the tarragon at the end, as long cooking dulls its aniseed flavour.
variations: Use flat-leaf parsley and a little thyme instead of tarragon if you don't have any.
Swap the shallots for a small brown onion, finely chopped, and cook for an extra minute.
recipe.storage: Refrigerate in an airtight container for up to 3 days or freeze for up to 2 months. Thaw overnight in the fridge and reheat gently in a covered pan until steaming hot throughout.

recipe.title: Mexican Tostadas de Frijoles
recipe.summary: Crunchy corn tortillas layered with creamy refried beans, shredded lettuce, salsa and crumbly cheese.
ingredients: 2 x 400 g cans pinto beans, drained and rinsed

stages.title: Crisp the tortillas
steps: Heat the oven to 200°C (180°C fan) and line two large baking trays with baking paper.
Arrange the tortillas in a single layer on the trays and brush both sides with 1 tbsp of the olive oil.
Bake for 8–10 minutes, turning once halfway, until golden and crisp.
Cool the tortillas on the trays for 5 minutes, as they crisp further while cooling.

stages.title: Cook the beans
steps: Heat the remaining 1 tbsp olive oil in a medium frying pan over medium heat. Cook the onion for 4–5 minutes, stirring, until soft and translucent.
Add the garlic and ground cumin and stir for 30 seconds until fragrant.
Add the pinto beans, the salt and 80 ml water. Simmer for 5 minutes, stirring occasionally, until the beans are heated through and softened.
Mash the beans roughly with a fork or the back of a wooden spoon, adding a splash more water if needed, until thick and spreadable.
Cover the pan and take it off the heat to keep the beans warm.

stages.title: Prepare the toppings
steps: Shred the lettuce, dice the tomatoes and crumble the feta.
Cut 1 lime into wedges for serving.
Slice the avocado and squeeze the juice of the other lime over it to stop it browning.

stages.title: Assemble and serve
steps: Spread the warm beans evenly over each crisp tortilla.
Top with the lettuce, tomatoes, avocado and feta, then serve straight away with the lime wedges.

tips: Brushing both sides of the tortillas with oil helps them crisp evenly and stay sturdy under the beans.
Mashing the beans while they are warm gives a spreadable layer that acts as a barrier, keeping the tortillas crisp.
Assemble just before eating, as moisture from the beans and tomato softens the tortillas within minutes.
variations: Add 1 finely chopped red chilli with the garlic for a spicier bean layer.
Swap the pinto beans for black beans and use sour cream instead of the feta.
recipe.storage: Store the bean mixture and toppings separately in airtight containers in the fridge for up to 3 days, and keep the tortillas in a dry airtight container. Reheat the beans in a pan with a splash of water over medium heat until hot, then assemble fresh.

recipe.title: Tunisian Harissa Baked Fish
recipe.summary: Flaky white fish baked over peppers and tomatoes with smoky harissa, cumin and bright lemon.
ingredients: 700 g white fish fillets, firm, cut into 4 portions
2 capsicums, red, deseeded and cut into 2 cm strips
1 red onion, cut into thin wedges
1 lemon, half juiced and half cut into wedges

stages.title: Prepare the vegetables
steps: Heat the oven to 200°C (180°C fan).
Cut the capsicums into strips and the red onion into wedges, and spread them over a large baking tray.
Drizzle the vegetables with 2 tbsp of the olive oil, then add the ground cumin and half the salt and toss to coat.

stages.title: Roast the vegetables
steps: Roast the capsicum and onion on the middle shelf for 10 minutes.
Take the tray out, stir the vegetables so they colour evenly, then roast for another 10 minutes, until softened and starting to colour at the edges.

stages.title: Coat the fish
steps: While the vegetables roast, pat the fish portions dry with paper towel and season with the remaining salt.
Stir the harissa paste with the juice of half the lemon and the remaining 1 tbsp olive oil in a small bowl.
Brush the harissa mixture all over the fish and leave it at room temperature until the vegetables are ready.

stages.title: Bake the fish
steps: Remove the tray from the oven and push the vegetables aside to make space for the fish.
Nestle the fish among the vegetables and scatter the cherry tomatoes around it.
Return the tray to the oven for 12–15 minutes, until the fish is opaque and flakes easily with a fork and the tomatoes have split.

stages.title: Cook the couscous and serve
steps: While the fish bakes, place the couscous in a heatproof bowl, pour over 250 ml boiling water, cover and stand for 5 minutes, then fluff with a fork.
Scatter the parsley over the fish and vegetables.
Serve with the couscous and the lemon wedges.

tips: Harissa strength varies a lot between jars, so taste a little first and reduce the amount if it is very hot, as the heat intensifies on the fish.
Patting the fish dry helps the harissa coating cling and brown instead of sliding off in the juices.
Roasting the capsicum and onion first gives them time to soften, since they take longer than the fish to cook.
Thicker fillets need the full 15 minutes, while thin ones can be ready in 12, so check early.
variations: Use salmon fillets instead of white fish and bake until just cooked through and flaking.
Add a drained 400 g can of chickpeas to the tray with the tomatoes for a more filling meal.
recipe.storage: Refrigerate the fish and vegetables in an airtight container for up to 2 days. Reheat gently in a 160°C (140°C fan) oven until hot through. Not recommended to freeze.

recipe.title: Australian Anzac Biscuits
recipe.summary: Golden oat-and-coconut biscuits with crisp edges, chewy centres and rich golden syrup flavour.

stages.title: Prepare the dry mix
steps: Heat the oven to 170°C (150°C fan) and line two large baking trays with baking paper.
Combine the rolled oats, plain flour, desiccated coconut and brown sugar in a large bowl.
Stir with a fork, breaking up any lumps of sugar, then make a well in the centre.

stages.title: Make the butter mixture
steps: Melt the butter and golden syrup in a small saucepan over low heat, stirring, for 2–3 minutes until smooth.
Stir the bicarbonate soda into the boiling water in a small cup, then pour it into the butter mixture. It will foam up.
Remove the pan from the heat straight away.

stages.title: Mix and shape
steps: Pour the foaming butter mixture into the well in the dry ingredients.
Stir until the mixture is evenly moistened and holds together when pressed.
Roll heaped tablespoons of mixture into balls, each about 3 cm wide, to make about 20.

stages.title: Bake and cool
steps: Place the balls on the trays, spaced 5 cm apart, and flatten each to about 1 cm thick.
Bake for 12–15 minutes, swapping the trays halfway, until deep golden brown around the edges.
Cool on the trays for 10 minutes, as the biscuits are soft when hot and firm up as they cool, then transfer to a wire rack.

tips: Rolled oats give chew and texture; instant oats turn the biscuits pasty.
Dissolving the bicarbonate soda in boiling water and adding it to the warm butter makes the mixture foam, which helps the biscuits spread and gives a crisp edge.
Bake a few minutes longer for crisp biscuits, or take them out at the lighter golden stage for chewy centres.
Leave space on the trays, as the biscuits spread while baking.
variations: Add 1 tsp finely grated orange zest to the dry ingredients for a citrus note.
Dip cooled biscuits halfway into melted dark chocolate and let it set on baking paper.
recipe.storage: Store in an airtight container at room temperature for up to 5 days. Freeze for up to 2 months.

recipe.title: Spanish Albóndigas in Tomato Sauce
recipe.summary: Juicy pork-and-beef meatballs simmered in smoky tomato sauce with paprika and garlic.

stages.title: Mix and shape the meatballs
steps: In a large bowl, combine the beef mince, pork mince, egg, breadcrumbs, half the garlic, half the parsley, 3/4 tsp of the salt and the black pepper.
Mix gently with your hands until just combined, as overmixing makes the meatballs tough.
Roll the mixture into about 24 walnut-sized balls, handling lightly and without compacting them.
Place the balls on a tray in a single layer until the pan is hot.

stages.title: Brown the meatballs
steps: Heat 2 tbsp of the olive oil in a large deep frying pan over medium-high heat.
Add half the meatballs and cook for 5–6 minutes, turning occasionally, until browned all over. They will not be cooked through.
Transfer the browned meatballs to a plate.
Brown the remaining meatballs in the same pan for 5–6 minutes, turning occasionally, until browned all over, then transfer to the plate.

stages.title: Make the tomato sauce
steps: Reduce the heat to medium and add the remaining 1 tbsp olive oil to the same pan.
Add the onion and the remaining 1/4 tsp salt and cook for 5–6 minutes, stirring often, until soft and translucent.
Add the remaining garlic and the smoked paprika and stir for 30 seconds until fragrant.
Pour in the passata and 125 ml water, scraping up the browned bits from the base of the pan.
Bring to a simmer and cook for 8 minutes, stirring occasionally, until slightly thickened.

stages.title: Simmer and serve
steps: Return the meatballs and any juices on the plate to the pan, nestling them into the sauce.
Partly cover and simmer over low heat for 20–25 minutes, turning the meatballs once, until cooked through with no pink inside and the sauce is thick.
Sprinkle with the remaining parsley and serve with the sliced baguette.

tips: Pork mince alongside beef keeps the meatballs tender and juicy, because the extra fat stops them drying out.
Browning the meatballs first builds a deeper flavour in the sauce, as the caramelised bits dissolve into it.
Smoked paprika gives the sauce its Spanish character; sweet paprika tastes noticeably milder.
Rolling the meatballs without squeezing keeps the texture light, because packed mince turns dense when cooked.
variations: Add 1/2 tsp chilli flakes with the paprika for a spicier, bravas-style sauce.
Stir 1 cup frozen peas into the sauce for the last 5 minutes of simmering.
recipe.storage: Refrigerate in an airtight container for up to 3 days, or freeze for up to 3 months. Thaw overnight in the fridge and reheat gently in a covered pan until steaming hot throughout.

recipe.title: Indian Kheer Rice Pudding
recipe.summary: Creamy slow-simmered rice pudding scented with cardamom, saffron and toasted pistachios.

stages.title: Soak the rice and prepare the flavourings
steps: Rinse the rice in a sieve under cold running water until the water runs mostly clear.
Cover the rice with cold water in a bowl and soak for 15 minutes, then drain well.
While the rice soaks, lightly crush the cardamom pods with the flat of a knife so they split open.
Roughly chop the pistachios and set aside.

stages.title: Simmer the milk with the rice
steps: Pour the milk into a large heavy-based saucepan and heat over medium heat, stirring occasionally, until small bubbles form around the edge, about 8 minutes.
Add the drained rice, crushed cardamom pods and saffron threads, and stir well.
Bring back to a gentle simmer, about 5 minutes, then reduce the heat to low.

stages.title: Cook until thick and creamy
steps: Cook over low heat for 35 minutes, stirring every 3–4 minutes and scraping the base of the pan so the milk does not catch.
When the rice is very soft and the milk has reduced to a thick, creamy consistency, stir in the sugar.
Cook for a further 5 minutes over low heat, stirring constantly, until the sugar has dissolved and the kheer coats the back of a spoon.

stages.title: Finish and serve
steps: Remove the pan from the heat and fish out the cardamom pods.
Stir in the rosewater and let the kheer rest for 10 minutes; it will thicken further as it cools.
Spoon into 4 bowls and scatter with the chopped pistachios. Serve warm.

tips: Soaking the rice softens the grains so they break down and release starch, which thickens the kheer without any cornflour.
Use a heavy-based saucepan and keep the heat low, as thin pans let the milk scorch on the base and give a burnt taste.
Add the sugar only after the rice is soft, because sugar added earlier can keep the grains firm.
Add the rosewater off the heat, as its delicate fragrance fades with prolonged cooking.
variations: Use chopped almonds instead of pistachios, toasted in a dry frying pan over medium heat for 2–3 minutes until lightly golden.
Replace the sugar with 2 tbsp honey stirred in off the heat for a softer sweetness.
recipe.storage: To serve cold, cover and chill for at least 2 hours after resting. Refrigerate in an airtight container for up to 3 days. It thickens when cold, so stir in a splash of milk and reheat gently over low heat, or serve chilled. Not suitable for freezing as the texture turns grainy.

recipe.title: Italian Marinated Artichokes
recipe.summary: Tender artichoke hearts dressed with lemon, parsley, garlic and olive oil for a bright antipasto.

stages.title: Prepare the artichokes
steps: Drain the artichoke hearts in a colander for 5 minutes, then pat them dry with paper towel.
Cut any large artichoke hearts in half or quarters so the pieces are all a similar size.
Place the artichokes in a medium bowl.

stages.title: Prepare the dressing flavours
steps: Finely grate the zest of the lemon, then juice the lemon to give about 2 tbsp juice.
Thinly slice the garlic and finely chop the parsley.
Stir the lemon zest, lemon juice, parsley and salt together in a small bowl.

stages.title: Warm the oil
steps: Heat the olive oil in a small saucepan over low heat, then add the garlic, oregano and chilli flakes.
Cook for 2 minutes, stirring, until the garlic is fragrant and just starting to soften but has not browned.
Remove from the heat and leave to cool for 5 minutes so it is warm, not hot.

stages.title: Marinate and serve
steps: Pour the warm garlic oil into the lemon and parsley mixture and stir to combine.
Pour the dressing over the artichokes and toss gently so the pieces stay whole.
Cover and leave at room temperature for 30 minutes, tossing once halfway through.
Serve at room temperature, spooning over the dressing from the bowl.

tips: Pat the artichokes dry so the dressing coats them instead of being diluted by brine.
Warming the garlic in the oil mellows its raw bite and carries the oregano and chilli flavour through the dressing.
Cool the oil before adding the lemon juice and parsley so the parsley stays bright green and the lemon tastes fresh.
Artichokes packed in brine or water suit this recipe best, as oil-packed ones make the dressing greasy.
variations: Add 1 tbsp drained capers and a handful of chopped kalamata olives with the parsley.
Stir through 1 tbsp chopped mint instead of the oregano for a fresher, brighter flavour.
recipe.storage: Refrigerate in an airtight container for up to 4 days. Bring to room temperature before serving. Not suitable to freeze.

recipe.title: Italian Caprese Stuffed Peppers
recipe.summary: Sweet roasted peppers filled with mozzarella, cherry tomatoes and basil, finished with balsamic glaze.
ingredients: 4 capsicums, halved lengthways through the stem, seeds removed
250 g mozzarella, drained and torn into small pieces
1 bunch basil, leaves picked, larger leaves torn

stages.title: Prepare the capsicums and oven
steps: Heat the oven to 200°C (180°C fan) and line a large baking tray with baking paper.
Halve the capsicums lengthways through the stems and scrape out the seeds and white membranes, keeping the stems on so the halves hold their shape.
Place the capsicums cut side up on the tray, brush the insides and edges with half the olive oil and season with half the salt.

stages.title: Roast the capsicums
steps: Roast the capsicums on the middle shelf for 20 minutes, until the edges are starting to colour and the flesh has softened slightly.
Remove the tray from the oven and leave the oven on at 200°C (180°C fan) for the second bake.

stages.title: Make the tomato filling
steps: While the capsicums roast, combine the cherry tomatoes, garlic, the remaining 1 tbsp olive oil, the remaining salt and a good grind of black pepper in a bowl.
Stir through half the basil leaves.
Tip any liquid out of the roasted capsicum halves if it has pooled, then spoon the tomato mixture into them.

stages.title: Bake with the mozzarella
steps: Scatter the torn mozzarella over the tomato filling.
Return the tray to the oven and bake for 10–12 minutes, until the cheese has melted and is lightly golden in spots and the capsicums are tender when pierced with a knife.
Meanwhile, simmer the balsamic vinegar in a small saucepan over medium heat for 2–3 minutes, until syrupy and able to coat the back of a spoon.
Let the capsicums stand for 3 minutes, then drizzle with the balsamic syrup and top with the remaining basil.

tips: Drain the mozzarella and pat it dry with paper towel, because excess whey turns the filling watery in the oven.
Pre-roasting the capsicums for 20 minutes means they are tender by the time the cheese has melted, instead of staying firm.
Keeping the stems on helps the halves sit level and stops the juices running out.
Adding half the basil after baking keeps its fresh flavour and bright green colour; it turns dark and dull if baked.
variations: Spoon 1 cup cooked quinoa into each capsicum half beneath the tomato filling to make it a more substantial meal.
Swap the mozzarella for torn bocconcini or add a spoonful of basil pesto over the tomatoes before the cheese.
recipe.storage: Refrigerate leftovers in an airtight container for up to 3 days. Reheat in a 180°C (160°C fan) oven for 10–15 minutes until hot through. Not suitable for freezing.

recipe.title: Greek Portokalopita
recipe.summary: Syrup-soaked orange and yoghurt cake made with crisp filo pieces and fragrant citrus zest.

stages.title: Dry the filo
steps: Heat the oven to 180°C (160°C fan) and line a baking tray with baking paper.
Tear the filo pastry sheets into rough 3–4 cm pieces and spread them over the tray.
Bake for 10–12 minutes until dry and crisp but not coloured.
Cool the filo on the tray for 20 minutes, then crush any large pieces slightly with your hands.

stages.title: Make the batter
steps: Grease a 20 cm square or round cake tin with the 1 tsp olive oil and line the base with baking paper.
Finely grate the zest of 2 oranges, then juice those 2 oranges and set the juice aside for the syrup.
Whisk the eggs and 100 g of the sugar in a large bowl for 2 minutes until pale and slightly thick.
Whisk in the Greek yoghurt, the 150 ml olive oil, the orange zest, the vanilla extract and the baking powder until smooth.
Fold in the cooled filo until every piece is coated, then pour the mixture into the tin and level the top.

stages.title: Bake the cake and make the syrup
steps: Bake the cake in the oven at 180°C (160°C fan) for 40–45 minutes, until the top is deep golden and a skewer inserted in the centre comes out clean. Cover loosely with foil if it browns too fast.
While the cake bakes, juice the remaining orange and combine it with the reserved orange juice, the remaining 150 g sugar and the 200 ml water in a saucepan.
Bring to a boil over medium heat, stirring until the sugar dissolves, then simmer for 8–10 minutes until lightly syrupy.
Take the syrup off the heat and leave it to cool to warm while the cake finishes.

stages.title: Soak and serve
steps: Leave the cake in its tin on a wire rack for 10 minutes, until warm rather than hot.
Pour the warm syrup slowly over the cake, a little at a time so it soaks in evenly.
Let the cake absorb the syrup for 30 minutes, then cut into 4 portions.

tips: Drying the filo makes it absorb the batter evenly, so the cake is moist and tender rather than gluey.
Pour warm syrup over a warm cake: if both are hot the cake turns soggy, and if both are cold the syrup sits on top.
Zest the oranges before juicing them, because the zest holds most of the orange flavour and is hard to grate from a squeezed fruit.
variations: Add a cinnamon stick and 2 strips of orange peel to the syrup while it simmers, then remove them before pouring.
Serve each portion with an extra spoonful of Greek yoghurt and a little orange zest.
recipe.storage: Keep covered at room temperature for 1 day, or refrigerate in an airtight container for up to 4 days. Serve at room temperature or warm briefly in the microwave.

recipe.title: Chinese Tomato Egg Stir-Fry
recipe.summary: Soft scrambled eggs folded into juicy sweet-savoury tomatoes for a quick homestyle meal.
ingredients: 3 spring onions, thinly sliced, white and green parts separated

stages.title: Cook the rice
steps: Cook the rice according to the packet, so it is ready when the stir-fry is finished.
While the rice cooks, beat the eggs in a bowl with 1/4 tsp of the salt until the whites and yolks are fully combined.
Cut the tomatoes into wedges and slice the spring onions, keeping the white and green parts separate.

stages.title: Prepare the sauce
steps: Mix the cornflour with 1 tbsp water in a small bowl until smooth.
Measure the sugar and soy sauce into a small bowl so they are ready to add.
Keep the rice covered and warm once cooked.

stages.title: Scramble the eggs
steps: Heat half the oil in a wok over medium-high heat for 1 minute until it shimmers.
Pour in the eggs and leave for 10 seconds, then gently push them from the edges to the centre.
Cook for 1–2 minutes until the eggs are just set but still soft and slightly wet in places, then transfer to a plate.

stages.title: Cook the tomatoes
steps: Add the remaining oil to the wok over medium-high heat and stir-fry the spring onion whites for 20 seconds until fragrant.
Add the tomatoes and the remaining 1/4 tsp salt and cook, stirring often, for 3–4 minutes until they soften and release their juices.
Stir in the sugar and soy sauce and cook for 1 minute.
Stir the cornflour mixture, pour it in and cook for 30 seconds until the sauce thickens slightly and turns glossy.

stages.title: Combine and serve
steps: Return the eggs to the wok and fold gently through the tomatoes for 1 minute until the eggs are cooked through and no longer wet.
Scatter over the spring onion greens and serve straight away with the rice.

tips: Take the eggs out while they are still soft, because they finish cooking when folded back into the hot tomatoes.
Cooking the eggs in hot oil makes them puff up and stay tender rather than turning rubbery.
Ripe tomatoes give the best sauce, and the sugar balances their acidity if yours are tart.
variations: Add 1 tsp sesame oil just before serving for a nutty aroma.
Use 2 tbsp tomato paste with a splash of water if your tomatoes are pale and lack flavour.
