recipe.storage: Refrigerate in an airtight container for up to 2 days. Reheat gently in a pan or microwave until steaming hot. Not recommended to freeze, as the eggs turn watery.

recipe.title: Indian Dal Tadka
recipe.summary: Creamy yellow lentils finished with sizzling cumin, garlic and chilli-spiced ghee.

stages.title: Prepare the dal and vegetables
steps: Rinse the moong dal in a sieve under cold running water until the water runs almost clear.
Finely chop the onion and chop the tomatoes.
Thinly slice the garlic and roughly chop the coriander.

stages.title: Simmer the dal and cook the rice
steps: Put the dal, turmeric, half the onion and the tomatoes in a large saucepan with 1 litre water and bring to the boil over high heat.
Reduce the heat to medium-low and simmer, partly covered, for 30 minutes, stirring occasionally, until the dal is very soft and starting to break down.
About 15 minutes before the dal is ready, cook the rice according to the packet, then keep it covered and warm.
Stir the salt into the dal and add a splash of hot water if it is thicker than a pourable soup.

stages.title: Make the tadka
steps: Heat the ghee in a small frying pan over medium heat for 1 minute.
Add the cumin seeds and cook for 30 seconds until they sizzle and smell fragrant.
Add the remaining onion and cook for 3–4 minutes, stirring, until softened and lightly browned.
Add the garlic and dried chillies and cook for 1 minute, stirring, until the garlic is golden but not dark.

stages.title: Finish and serve
steps: Pour the hot tadka over the dal and stir through briefly.
Serve the dal over the rice, scattered with the coriander, with the lemon wedges for squeezing over.

tips: Rinsing the dal removes surface starch, which reduces scum and keeps the cooked dal clean tasting.
Take the garlic off the heat as soon as it turns golden, because it turns bitter quickly once it browns.
Make the tadka just before serving so the spiced ghee is hot and fragrant when it hits the dal.
variations: Replace half the moong dal with red lentils for a creamier, thicker dal.
Stir 2 handfuls of baby spinach through the dal just before adding the tadka.
recipe.storage: Refrigerate the dal in a sealed container for up to 3 days or freeze for up to 3 months. Reheat in a saucepan over medium heat until steaming hot, adding a splash of water to loosen.

recipe.title: Thai Mango Salad
recipe.summary: Crunchy green mango, herbs and roasted peanuts tossed in a lively lime-chilli dressing.

stages.title: Toast the peanuts
steps: Heat a small frying pan over medium heat and add the peanuts.
Toast for 3–4 minutes, shaking the pan often, until golden and fragrant.
Tip onto a board, cool for a minute, then roughly chop.

stages.title: Prepare the vegetables
steps: Peel the green mangoes and cut the flesh from the stones, then cut it into thin matchsticks.
Peel the carrot and cut it into matchsticks of a similar size.
Thinly slice the shallot and the red chilli, and pick the coriander leaves from the stems.

stages.title: Make the dressing
steps: In a small bowl, stir the fish sauce, lime juice and brown sugar for about 1 minute, until the sugar has dissolved.
Taste and add a little more sugar if too sour or a little more lime juice if too sweet.

stages.title: Dress and rest
steps: Combine the mango, carrot, shallot and chilli in a large bowl.
Pour over the dressing and toss well for about 1 minute.
Leave to stand for 5 minutes, until the mango softens slightly and absorbs the dressing.

stages.title: Finish and serve
steps: Add the coriander leaves and toss gently.
Transfer to a serving plate and scatter the chopped peanuts on top.
Serve straight away.

tips: Use firm, unripe green mangoes: ripe ones turn mushy and sweet and lose the crisp bite the dressing is built around.
Toasting the peanuts brings out their oil and flavour, and chopping them just before serving keeps them crunchy.
Taste the dressing before it goes on, as fish sauce saltiness and lime sourness vary between brands and fruit.
Cut the mango and carrot into matchsticks of the same thickness so every mouthful has an even texture.
variations: Add 200 g cooked prawns for a more filling dish, tossing them through with the dressing.
Swap the carrot for thinly sliced green beans or cucumber for a different crunch.
recipe.storage: Best eaten straight away. Leftovers keep in the fridge in a covered container for up to 1 day, but the mango will soften and the peanuts will lose their crunch.

recipe.title: Mexican Nopales Salad
recipe.summary: Tender cactus paddles tossed with tomatoes, onion, coriander and lime for a tangy fresh salad.
ingredients: 400 g cleaned nopales, cut into 1 cm strips
1 bunch coriander, leaves and stems finely chopped

stages.title: Prepare the vegetables
steps: Rinse the nopales strips under cold running water and drain well.
Finely chop the tomatoes and red onion and place them in a large bowl.
Finely chop the coriander and set aside half for the dressing, keeping the other half for serving.
Juice the limes to get about 80 ml juice.

stages.title: Simmer the nopales
steps: Bring 2 litres water and the 1 tbsp salt to the boil in a large saucepan over high heat.
Add the nopales, reduce the heat to medium and simmer for 12–15 minutes, until tender but still slightly firm and bright olive green.
Drain in a colander and rinse well under cold water until the slippery coating is gone.
Drain again and pat dry with paper towel.

stages.title: Cool the nopales
steps: Spread the nopales on a tray in a single layer.
Leave for 15 minutes until completely cool, so they don't wilt the tomato and onion.

stages.title: Dress and chill
steps: Whisk the lime juice, olive oil, 1/2 tsp salt, black pepper and half the coriander in a small bowl.
Add the cooled nopales to the tomato and onion, pour over the dressing and toss to coat.
Cover and refrigerate for 15 minutes so the flavours mingle.
Scatter the remaining coriander over the salad and serve cold.

tips: Rinsing the cooked nopales well removes the sticky coating, so the salad stays crisp rather than slimy.
Cooling the nopales completely before dressing keeps the tomato firm and the lime juice tasting fresh.
Salting the cooking water seasons the nopales through, so the dressing needs only a little salt.
Cutting the strips to an even thickness means they all cook tender in the same time.
variations: Add 1 diced avocado and 100 g crumbled feta just before serving for a richer salad.
Stir in 1 finely chopped red chilli with the onion for a hotter version.
recipe.storage: Refrigerate in an airtight container for up to 2 days. Serve cold; it is not suitable to freeze.

recipe.title: Japanese Hiyayakko
recipe.summary: Chilled silken tofu topped with ginger, spring onions and soy for a clean, refreshing starter.

stages.title: Chill the tofu
steps: Leave the silken tofu in its sealed packet and refrigerate for at least 30 minutes, until very cold.
Chill four small plates or shallow bowls in the fridge at the same time.

stages.title: Prepare the toppings
steps: Peel the ginger and grate it finely, then squeeze lightly to release a little juice and keep both the pulp and juice.
Slice the spring onions as thinly as you can.
Toast the sesame seeds in a dry frying pan over medium heat for 1–2 minutes, shaking the pan, until light golden and fragrant, then tip onto a plate to cool.

stages.title: Cut and plate the tofu
steps: Open the packet and carefully tip out the tofu onto a board lined with paper towel, then gently blot away the surface liquid.
Dip a sharp knife in water and cut the block into four even pieces.
Slide each piece onto a chilled plate with a spatula, keeping the pieces whole.

stages.title: Dress and serve
steps: Pile the grated ginger and spring onions on top of each piece of tofu.
Scatter over the toasted sesame seeds.
Drizzle 1½ tsp of the soy sauce over each portion and serve straight away, while the tofu is still cold.

tips: Silken tofu is very delicate, so cutting it with a wet knife stops it sticking and tearing.
Chilled plates keep the tofu cold, which is the whole point of this dish on a warm day.
Dress with the soy sauce just before serving, because it draws water from the tofu and the plate turns watery if it sits.
Grate the ginger on the finest grater so it melts into the soy rather than leaving stringy bits.
variations: Replace the sesame seeds with a spoonful of crushed peanuts and add a few drops of sesame oil for a richer finish.
Add a few thin slices of cucumber or a little chilli flakes on top for crunch or heat.
recipe.storage: Best eaten straight away. Leftover plain tofu can be kept covered in the fridge for 1 day, but dress it only when serving.

recipe.title: British Toad in the Hole
recipe.summary: Juicy sausages baked inside a towering, crisp-edged Yorkshire pudding with rich onion gravy.

stages.title: Make the batter and slice the onions
steps: Sift 140 g of the plain flour and 1/4 tsp of the salt into a large bowl and make a well in the centre.
Add the eggs and half the milk, then whisk until thick and smooth.
Whisk in the remaining milk and 100 ml water until the batter is the consistency of pouring cream, then season with black pepper.
Thinly slice the onions and set them aside for the gravy.

stages.title: Rest the batter and brown the sausages
steps: Heat the oven to 220°C (200°C fan) and leave the batter to rest on the bench for 20 minutes while the oven heats and the sausages cook.
Once the oven is hot, put the vegetable oil in a 20 x 30 cm metal baking dish, add the sausages and roast for 12 minutes, turning once, until browned all over.
Return the dish to the oven for 3 minutes, until the oil is smoking hot and the sausages are sizzling.

stages.title: Bake the pudding and make the gravy
steps: Carefully pull the hot dish out and quickly pour the batter around the sausages. It should sizzle as it hits the oil.
Bake for 25–30 minutes without opening the oven door, until the batter is risen, deep golden and crisp at the edges, and the sausages are cooked through with no pink in the centre.
While the pudding bakes, melt the butter in a saucepan over medium heat. Add the onions and the remaining 1/4 tsp salt and cook, stirring, for 10 minutes until soft and golden.
Stir in the remaining 1 tbsp plain flour and cook for 1 minute.
Gradually stir in the beef stock and worcestershire sauce, then simmer over medium heat for 8–10 minutes, stirring occasionally, until the gravy coats the back of a spoon.

stages.title: Serve
steps: Cut the pudding into four portions with two sausages each.
Serve straight away with the onion gravy spooned over, before the batter deflates.

tips: Pouring batter into smoking-hot oil makes it puff and crisp straight away instead of turning dense and soggy.
Resting the batter lets the flour absorb the liquid, which gives a lighter, taller rise.
Keep the oven door shut for the first 25 minutes because escaping heat makes the batter collapse.
Use a metal dish rather than glass or ceramic, as it holds heat better and gives a crisper base.
variations: Add the leaves from 2 sprigs of thyme to the batter for an herbal note.
Replace the pork sausages with beef or chicken sausages, cooking until no pink remains in the centre.
recipe.storage: Refrigerate leftovers and gravy separately in sealed containers for up to 3 days. Reheat the pudding at 180°C (160°C fan) for 10–15 minutes until hot through, and warm the gravy in a saucepan until steaming.

recipe.title: British Bakewell Tart
recipe.summary: Buttery pastry layered with raspberry jam and almond frangipane, finished with flaked almonds.
ingredients: 1 sheet shortcrust pastry (about 25 cm square), thawed
100 g almonds, ground to a fine meal (or almond meal)
1 cup rice, uncooked, for weighing down the pastry (or baking beads)

stages.title: Line the tin and chill
steps: Press the pastry sheet into a 23 cm loose-bottomed tart tin, pushing it into the fluted edge and trimming the excess with a knife.
Prick the base all over with a fork.
Chill the lined tin in the fridge for 30 minutes so the pastry holds its shape.
Heat the oven to 180°C (160°C fan) while the pastry chills.

stages.title: Blind-bake the case
steps: Line the chilled pastry with baking paper and fill with the uncooked rice.
Bake for 15 minutes, then lift out the paper and rice.
Bake the empty case for a further 5 minutes until pale golden and dry, then cool in the tin for 5 minutes.

stages.title: Make the frangipane
steps: Beat the butter and caster sugar in a bowl with electric beaters for 3–4 minutes until pale and fluffy.
Beat in the eggs one at a time, then add the vanilla extract; the mixture may look slightly curdled, which is fine.
Fold in the ground almonds and plain flour until just combined.

stages.title: Assemble and bake
steps: Spread the raspberry jam evenly over the base of the warm pastry case.
Spoon the frangipane over the jam and smooth it to the edge, sealing it against the pastry.
Scatter the flaked almonds over the top.
Bake at 180°C (160°C fan) for 30–35 minutes until deep golden and set, and a skewer inserted in the centre comes out clean.
Cover the edge with foil if the pastry browns too quickly.

stages.title: Cool and serve
steps: Cool the tart in the tin for 10 minutes so the jam settles and it slices cleanly.
Remove from the tin and dust with the icing sugar before slicing.

tips: Blind-baking until dry keeps the base crisp under the wet jam and frangipane.
Spreading the jam on the warm case helps it go on evenly without tearing the pastry.
Sealing the frangipane against the pastry edge stops jam bubbling up the sides.
Resting the tart before slicing lets the filling firm up so the slices hold together.
variations: Swap the raspberry jam for cherry or apricot jam.
Add 1/2 tsp almond extract to the frangipane for a stronger almond flavour.
recipe.storage: Keep covered at room temperature for 1 day or in the fridge for up to 3 days. Bring to room temperature before serving.

recipe.title: Korean Kongnamul Guk
recipe.summary: A light, clean-tasting soybean sprout soup simmered with garlic, spring onion and anchovy broth.
ingredients: 1/4 tsp salt, plus extra to taste

stages.title: Prepare the sprouts and aromatics
steps: Rinse the soybean sprouts in cold water, drain well and discard any slimy or discoloured sprouts and loose bean husks.
Finely chop the garlic.
Thinly slice the spring onions, keeping the white and green parts together.

stages.title: Simmer the sprouts
steps: Pour the vegetable stock into a medium saucepan and bring to the boil over high heat, about 5 minutes.
Add the sprouts and garlic, then cover with the lid and reduce the heat to medium.
Simmer, covered, for 7 minutes without lifting the lid, which keeps the beany smell from developing, until the sprouts are tender but still have a little crunch.

stages.title: Season and finish
steps: Stir in the soy sauce and the salt, then simmer uncovered over medium heat for 2 minutes.
Taste and add a pinch more salt if needed.
Stir in the spring onions and sesame oil and turn off the heat.
Ladle into bowls and serve hot as a side with other dishes.

tips: Keep the lid on for the first cook: lifting it early can leave a raw, grassy bean smell in the soup.
Don't overcook the sprouts, as they lose their crunch within a few minutes of the recommended time.
Add the sesame oil at the end because heat dulls its nutty aroma.
Use a vegetable stock that tastes good on its own, as the soup is mostly broth.
variations: For a spicy version, add 1 tsp chilli flakes with the garlic.
For a hangover-style soup, add a handful of sliced kimchi with the sprouts and omit the soy sauce if the kimchi is salty.
recipe.storage: Refrigerate in a covered container for up to 2 days. Reheat gently over low heat until just hot, as boiling makes the sprouts soft. Not suitable for freezing.

recipe.title: Georgian Badrijani Nigvzit
recipe.summary: Thin fried aubergine rolls filled with fragrant walnut, garlic and coriander paste.

stages.title: Slice and salt the eggplant
steps: Trim the eggplants and slice them lengthways into 5 mm strips.
Arrange the strips in a single layer on trays and sprinkle both sides with the salt.
Leave for 20 minutes to draw out moisture and bitterness.
Rinse the strips briefly and pat them very dry with paper towel.

stages.title: Fry the eggplant
steps: Heat 1 tbsp of the oil in a large frying pan over medium-high heat.
Fry the strips in batches for 2–3 minutes each side, until soft and golden brown, adding the remaining 2 tbsp oil a little at a time as needed.
Drain the fried strips on paper towel.

stages.title: Make the walnut paste
steps: Blitz the walnuts, garlic and ground coriander in a food processor to a fine, crumbly paste.
Add the vinegar and 2–3 tbsp water, and blend until the paste is smooth and spreadable but still thick.
Stir in half the parsley.

stages.title: Cool the eggplant
steps: Spread the fried strips on a tray in a single layer.
Leave for 10 minutes, until completely cool to the touch.

stages.title: Fill and serve
steps: Spread about 1 tbsp of walnut paste over each cooled eggplant strip, leaving the ends clear.
Roll each strip up from the narrow end and place seam side down on a platter.
Scatter with the remaining parsley and the pomegranate seeds, if using, and serve at room temperature.

tips: Salting and drying the slices stops them soaking up oil, so they fry golden instead of greasy.
Cool the strips fully before spreading, or the warm eggplant makes the walnut paste oily and it slides out when rolled.
Add the water to the paste a spoonful at a time; too much makes it too loose to stay inside the rolls.
variations: Add 1/2 tsp chilli flakes to the walnut paste for a gentle heat.
Replace the parsley with coriander for a sharper herbal flavour.
recipe.storage: Refrigerate in an airtight container for up to 2 days; bring to room temperature before serving. Not suitable for freezing.

recipe.title: Indian Sabudana Khichdi
recipe.summary: Tender tapioca pearls tossed with cumin, peanuts, potatoes and lime for a lightly spiced breakfast.
ingredients: 1 potato, peeled and cut into 1 cm dice

stages.title: Rinse and soak the sabudana
steps: Rinse the sabudana pearls in a sieve under cold running water for about 1 minute, until the water runs almost clear.
Tip the pearls into a bowl and add 200 ml water, just enough to level with the pearls.
Cover and leave at room temperature for 4 hours, until the pearls are soft and can be squashed easily between two fingers.
Drain in a sieve and leave for 15 minutes so the pearls are dry and separate.

stages.title: Prepare the flavourings
steps: Peel the potato and cut it into 1 cm dice.
Finely chop the green chilli and the coriander.
Coarsely crush the roasted peanuts.
Toss the drained pearls with the crushed peanuts and the salt.

stages.title: Cook the potato and spices
steps: Heat the ghee in a large non-stick frying pan over medium heat.
Add the cumin seeds and cook for 30 seconds, until they sizzle and smell fragrant.
Add the potato and cook, stirring often, for 8–10 minutes until golden and tender when pierced with a knife.
Stir in the green chilli and cook for 1 minute.

stages.title: Cook the sabudana
steps: Reduce the heat to medium-low and add the pearl and peanut mixture to the pan.
Cook, stirring gently, for 5–7 minutes until the pearls turn translucent and are soft all the way through.
Remove the pan from the heat.

stages.title: Finish and serve
steps: Stir in the lime juice and taste for salt.
Scatter over the coriander and serve straight away while warm.

tips: Soak the pearls in just enough water rather than a full bowl, as excess water makes them gluey and they clump in the pan.
Rest the drained pearls for 15 minutes so surface moisture dries off, which helps them stay separate when fried.
Cook the potato until tender before adding the pearls, because the pearls need only a short time and won't soften the potato.
Add the lime juice off the heat so it stays fresh and sharp.
variations: Add 1/2 tsp white sugar with the salt for the sweet-sour balance common in Maharashtrian versions.
Replace the potato with 1 small diced sweet potato and cook it until just tender.
recipe.storage: Best eaten fresh as the pearls firm up when cold. Refrigerate leftovers in an airtight container for up to 2 days and reheat in a pan over low heat with a splash of water until steaming hot.

recipe.title: Greek Revithada
recipe.summary: Chickpeas slowly baked with onion, bay leaf and lemon until creamy in a fragrant olive-oil broth.
ingredients: 1 tsp salt, plus extra to taste

stages.title: Soak the chickpeas
steps: Place the dried chickpeas in a large bowl and cover with cold water by about 10 cm, as they will swell to double their size.
Leave to soak at room temperature for 8 hours or overnight.
Drain the chickpeas in a colander and rinse well under cold running water.

stages.title: Assemble the casserole
steps: Heat the oven to 160°C (140°C fan).
Thinly slice the onions.
Put the drained chickpeas, onions, bay leaves and half the olive oil (50 ml) into a large heavy casserole dish with a tight-fitting lid.
Pour in 1 litre water, which should cover the chickpeas by about 3 cm.

stages.title: Bring to the boil
steps: Set the casserole over medium-high heat on the stovetop and bring to the boil, about 5 minutes.
Reduce to a gentle simmer and skim off the white foam from the surface for about 5 minutes, until little new foam forms.

stages.title: Bake until tender
steps: Cover the casserole with the lid and transfer to the oven.
Bake for 3 hours, until the chickpeas are completely tender and crush easily between your fingers.
Check the liquid after 1½ hours and again near the end. If the chickpeas are poking out, top up with boiling water so they stay just covered.
Do not add salt during baking, as it can keep the chickpeas firm.

stages.title: Season and rest
steps: Remove the casserole from the oven and discard the bay leaves.
Stir in the salt, a good grind of black pepper, the lemon juice and the remaining 50 ml olive oil.
Mash a handful of chickpeas against the side of the dish with a spoon for about 1 minute, until the broth turns thick and creamy like a loose stew.
Rest, covered, for 15 minutes, then taste and add more salt if needed before serving.

tips: Soaking the chickpeas overnight gives even cooking and a creamy centre, so they don't split before the middles soften.
Add salt only once the chickpeas are tender, because salting early can toughen their skins.
Slow baking in a tightly lidded pot makes a thick, silky broth without stirring, and the oil emulsifies with the starch released by the chickpeas.
Stirring in lemon juice after baking keeps its flavour bright, as long cooking would dull it.
variations: Add 1 tsp dried oregano and a sprig of rosemary with the bay leaves for a more herbal broth.
Stir in a few handfuls of baby spinach after baking and let it wilt in the hot broth for 2–3 minutes.
recipe.storage: Cool and refrigerate in a covered container for up to 3 days, or freeze for up to 3 months. Reheat in a saucepan over medium heat with a splash of water until piping hot.

recipe.title: Italian Ricotta Gnocchi
recipe.summary: Pillowy ricotta dumplings tossed in brown butter and sage for a delicate, comforting pasta dish.

stages.title: Drain the ricotta
steps: Line a sieve with a clean tea towel or paper towels and sit it over a bowl.
Tip in the ricotta, then cover and leave to drain in the fridge for 25 minutes, until noticeably drier and crumbly.

stages.title: Make the dough
steps: Tip the drained ricotta into a large bowl and add the egg, the parmesan, 1/2 tsp of the salt and the black pepper.
Stir with a fork until smooth, then add 100 g of the flour.
Fold gently just until a soft, slightly sticky dough forms, as overmixing makes the dumplings tough.

stages.title: Shape the dumplings
steps: Dust a bench and a tray generously with some of the remaining 40 g flour.
Divide the dough into 4 pieces and roll each into a rope about 2 cm thick, dusting lightly as needed.
Cut each rope into 2–3 cm pieces and place them on the floured tray in a single layer.

stages.title: Chill and heat the water
steps: Refrigerate the tray, uncovered, for 10 minutes so the dumplings firm up and hold their shape in the water.
Meanwhile, bring a large pot of water to the boil over high heat and add the remaining 3 tsp salt.

stages.title: Cook the dumplings
steps: Reduce the water to a gentle simmer.
Cook the dumplings in 2 batches for 2–3 minutes each, until they float to the surface and are firm and cooked through when one is cut open.
Lift them out with a slotted spoon onto a plate, keeping them in a single layer.

stages.title: Brown the sage butter
steps: Melt the butter in a large frying pan over medium heat until foaming, about 1 minute.
Add the sage leaves and cook for 1–2 minutes, until the butter smells nutty and turns golden-brown and the leaves are crisp.
Add the cooked dumplings and toss gently for 1 minute, until coated and lightly golden. Serve straight away.

tips: Draining the ricotta removes excess moisture, so you need less flour and the dumplings stay light rather than rubbery.
Cook one test piece first. If it falls apart, mix in another tablespoon of flour before shaping the rest.
Chilling the shaped dough helps it set, so the pieces are less likely to break up in the simmering water.
Keep the water at a gentle simmer, as a rolling boil can break up these soft dumplings.
variations: Stir 100 g blanched, squeezed-dry and finely chopped baby spinach into the dough for a spinach and ricotta version.
Add a pinch of chilli flakes and the finely grated zest of 1 lemon to the browned butter for a sharper finish.
recipe.storage: Refrigerate cooked gnocchi in an airtight container for up to 2 days. Reheat in a frying pan over medium heat with a little butter until hot through. Uncooked shaped gnocchi can be frozen on a tray, then bagged, and cooked from frozen for 3–4 minutes.

recipe.title: Brazilian Farofa
recipe.summary: Toasted cassava flour with buttery onions and bacon for a crunchy savoury accompaniment.

stages.title: Prepare the ingredients
steps: Finely dice the bacon and finely chop the onion.
Finely chop the parsley and set it aside.
Measure the cassava flour into a bowl so it is ready to add.

stages.title: Crisp the bacon
steps: Heat a large frying pan over medium heat, then add the bacon to the dry pan.
Cook for 6–8 minutes, stirring often, until the fat has rendered and the bacon is golden and crisp.
Lift the bacon out with a slotted spoon onto a plate, leaving the rendered fat in the pan.

stages.title: Soften the onion
steps: Return the pan to medium heat and add the butter to the bacon fat.
When the butter has melted and is foaming, add the onion.
Cook for 5–6 minutes, stirring, until soft and translucent but not browned.

stages.title: Toast the flour and finish
steps: Reduce the heat to medium-low and add the cassava flour to the pan.
Stir constantly for 4–5 minutes, until the flour is lightly toasted, golden and sandy, with no raw floury smell.
Stir in the bacon, the parsley, the salt and a few grinds of black pepper.
Taste and add more salt if needed, then serve warm.

tips: Use a large pan so the flour spreads thin and toasts evenly instead of steaming into clumps.
Keep the heat at medium-low once the flour goes in, because cassava flour scorches quickly and turns bitter.
Bacon is salty, so add the salt only at the end, after tasting.
variations: Stir in 2 chopped hard-boiled eggs with the parsley for a more traditional, heartier farofa.
Use 2 thinly sliced spring onions in place of the parsley for a sharper flavour.
recipe.storage: Cool completely and keep in an airtight container in the fridge for up to 2 days. Reheat in a dry frying pan over medium-low heat for 2–3 minutes, stirring, until warm and crumbly again.

recipe.title: Austrian Topfenstrudel
recipe.summary: Flaky pastry wrapped around sweetened lemon ricotta with raisins and a golden buttery crust.

stages.title: Drain the ricotta and heat the oven
steps: Tip the ricotta into a sieve lined with paper towel, press gently, then leave it to drain over a bowl for 10 minutes.
While it drains, heat the oven to 190°C (170°C fan) and line a baking tray with baking paper.
Finely zest the lemon and set the zest aside.

stages.title: Make the filling
steps: Tip the drained ricotta into a large bowl and discard the liquid.
Add the egg, caster sugar and lemon zest, then stir until smooth and thick.
Fold in the sultanas until evenly spread through the mixture.

stages.title: Fill and shape the strudel
steps: Lay the puff pastry sheet on the lined tray and spoon the filling in a log down the centre, leaving a 3 cm border at each end.
Fold the long sides over the filling so they overlap slightly, then pinch the ends closed and tuck them under.
Turn the roll seam-side down and brush all over with half the melted butter.

stages.title: Bake the strudel
steps: Bake in the centre of the oven for 30–35 minutes, until the pastry is deep golden and puffed and the filling feels set when pressed gently.
Brush the hot strudel with the remaining melted butter.

stages.title: Rest and serve
steps: Leave the strudel on the tray to rest for 15 minutes so the filling firms up for slicing.
Dust with the icing sugar.
Cut into thick slices with a serrated knife and serve warm.

tips: Draining the ricotta keeps the filling thick, so it won't leak out and make the pastry base soggy.
Tucking the ends under stops the filling escaping as the pastry puffs.
Resting lets the egg-set filling firm up, so slices hold their shape instead of slumping.
Brushing with butter twice gives a glossy golden crust and richer flavour.
variations: Soak the sultanas in 2 tbsp warm water for 10 minutes and drain before folding in, for plumper fruit.
Replace the sultanas with 100 g chopped dried apricots for a tarter filling.
recipe.storage: Cool completely, then refrigerate covered for up to 2 days. Reheat slices at 160°C (140°C fan) for 10 minutes until warmed through and the pastry crisps.

recipe.title: Vietnamese Bun Cha
recipe.summary: Caramelised pork patties with rice vermicelli, fresh herbs and a tangy fish-sauce dipping broth.

stages.title: Marinate the pork
steps: Finely chop the garlic and thinly slice the spring onions.
In a bowl, combine the pork mince, half the garlic, the spring onions, 1 tbsp fish sauce, 1 tbsp sugar and 1/2 tsp black pepper. Mix well with your hands for about 1 minute, until sticky.
Shape the mixture into 16 small flat patties, about 5 cm wide.
Cover and refrigerate for 30 minutes so the flavours soak in and the patties hold their shape.

stages.title: Make the dipping broth
steps: Cut one carrot into thin matchsticks and slice the other into thin rounds. Keep the matchsticks for serving.
In a bowl, stir the remaining 2 tbsp sugar into 250 ml warm water for about 1 minute, until completely dissolved.
Add the remaining 2 tbsp fish sauce, the juice of the 2 limes, the rice vinegar and the remaining garlic.
Stir the sliced red chilli and the carrot rounds into the broth and set aside to pickle lightly while you cook.

stages.title: Cook the patties
steps: Heat the vegetable oil in a large frying pan over medium-high heat.
Cook half the patties for 3–4 minutes per side, until deeply browned and cooked through with no pink in the centre.
Transfer the cooked patties to a plate, then cook the remaining patties over medium-high heat for 3–4 minutes per side, until deeply browned and no longer pink in the centre.
Add the patties to the dipping broth.

stages.title: Prepare the noodles and herbs
steps: Cook the rice vermicelli according to the packet, then drain and rinse under cold water until cool.
Pick the mint leaves and tear the lettuce into bite-sized pieces.
Arrange the noodles, lettuce, mint and carrot matchsticks on a platter.

tips: Resting the patties in the fridge lets the fish sauce and sugar season the pork and helps the patties hold together in the pan.
Cook in batches so the pan stays hot; crowding steams the pork and stops it browning and caramelising.
Dissolve the sugar fully in warm water before adding the fish sauce and lime, so the broth is balanced and not gritty.
variations: Add thin slices of pork shoulder marinated in the same mix and cook them for 2–3 minutes per side until browned and cooked through.
Cook the patties on a barbecue grill over medium-high heat for the same time for a smokier flavour.
recipe.storage: Store patties, broth, noodles and herbs separately in the fridge for up to 2 days. Reheat the patties in a pan over medium heat until hot through and serve with cold noodles.

recipe.title: Japanese Sunomono
recipe.summary: Cool cucumber ribbons dressed in sweet rice vinegar with sesame and delicate wakame seaweed.

stages.title: Salt the cucumber
steps: Slice the cucumbers as thinly as you can with a mandoline or sharp knife, then place in a bowl.
Sprinkle the cucumber with the salt and toss well.
Leave to stand for 10 minutes, until the cucumber softens and releases liquid.

stages.title: Rehydrate the wakame
steps: Place the wakame in a bowl and cover with 500 ml cold water.
Soak for 5 minutes, until soft, glossy and fully expanded.
Drain the wakame, squeeze out the excess water and cut any long pieces into bite-sized lengths.

stages.title: Make the dressing
steps: Whisk the rice vinegar, sugar and soy sauce in a small bowl for about 1 minute, until the sugar dissolves.
Toast the sesame seeds in a dry frying pan over medium heat for 2–3 minutes, shaking often, until lightly golden, then tip onto a plate.

stages.title: Dress and chill
steps: Rinse the cucumber under cold water to remove the surface salt, then squeeze small handfuls firmly to remove as much liquid as possible.
Combine the cucumber and wakame in a bowl, pour over the dressing and toss gently.
Cover and chill in the fridge for 10 minutes.
Serve cold in small bowls, sprinkled with the toasted sesame seeds.

tips: Salting draws water out of the cucumber, so it stays crisp and doesn't dilute the dressing.
Rinsing the salted cucumber before squeezing stops the dish tasting too salty.
Squeezing the wakame dry keeps the dressing sharp and balanced rather than watery.
Toasting the sesame seeds brings out their nutty flavour, which balances the tang of the vinegar.
variations: Add 100 g cooked and peeled prawns, tossed through with the dressing, for a seafood version.
Add 1 tsp finely grated ginger to the dressing for a sharper, warmer flavour.
recipe.storage: Best eaten within a few hours. Keep leftovers covered in the fridge for up to 1 day; the cucumber will soften. Not suitable for freezing.

recipe.title: Indian Dhokla
recipe.summary: Fluffy steamed chickpea cakes topped with mustard seeds, curry leaves and fresh coriander.

stages.title: Make the batter
steps: Sift the chickpea flour into a large bowl so there are no lumps.
Add the yoghurt, 120 ml water, turmeric, salt and half the sugar.
Whisk for 2 minutes until completely smooth and thick like pancake batter.
Brush a 20 cm round cake tin with 1 tbsp of the oil so the dhokla releases cleanly.

stages.title: Rest the batter and heat the steamer
steps: Cover the bowl and rest the batter for 10 minutes so the flour hydrates.
Meanwhile, pour 3 cm water into a large wide pot with a rack and bring to the boil over high heat.
Lower the heat to medium so the water keeps simmering steadily.

stages.title: Steam the dhokla
steps: Whisk the fruit salt into the rested batter for 10 seconds until it turns frothy and slightly paler.
Pour the batter straight into the greased tin and set it on the rack in the pot.
Cover with a lid and steam over medium heat for 15–18 minutes, until the dhokla is risen and a skewer inserted in the centre comes out clean.

stages.title: Cool the dhokla
steps: Lift the hot tin out carefully and cool for 10 minutes so the cake firms up.
Run a knife around the edge and turn the dhokla out onto a board.

stages.title: Temper and serve
steps: Heat the remaining 2 tbsp oil in a small frying pan over medium heat for 1 minute, then add the mustard seeds and cook until they start to pop, about 30 seconds.
Add the curry leaves and chilli and stir for 15 seconds.
Pour in 2 tbsp water and add the remaining sugar, then simmer for 1 minute until the sugar dissolves.
Cut the dhokla into squares, spoon the tempering over the top and scatter with the coriander.

tips: Add the fruit salt only just before steaming, because it reacts with the yoghurt straight away and the bubbles that make the dhokla light are lost if the batter waits.
Sifting the chickpea flour prevents lumps, which would steam into dense pockets.
Wrapping the pot lid in a clean tea towel stops condensation dripping onto the surface and leaving it soggy.
variations: Stir 2 tbsp finely grated ginger into the batter for a sharper, warmer flavour.
Replace the chilli in the tempering with 1 tsp sesame seeds for a milder, nutty finish.
recipe.storage: Refrigerate the dhokla in a covered container for up to 2 days. Reheat in a steamer or microwave for 1–2 minutes until hot, and add the tempering fresh if you can.

recipe.title: American Key Lime Pie
recipe.summary: Tangy lime custard in a buttery biscuit crust topped with softly whipped cream.

stages.title: Make the biscuit crust
steps: Heat the oven to 175°C (155°C fan).
Blitz the digestive biscuits in a food processor to fine crumbs, or crush them in a zip-lock bag with a rolling pin.
Mix the crumbs with the melted butter until they look like damp sand.
Press the mixture firmly over the base and up the sides of a 20 cm pie dish, using the back of a glass to compact it.

stages.title: Bake the crust
steps: Bake the crust for 10 minutes, until lightly golden at the edges and firm to touch.
Remove from the oven and leave on a rack while you make the filling. Keep the oven on.

stages.title: Make the filling
steps: Whisk the egg yolks in a bowl for 1–2 minutes until pale and slightly thick. Use pasteurised eggs if serving young children, pregnant or elderly people, as the filling is only lightly baked.
Whisk in the condensed milk until smooth.
Add the lime juice and lime zest and whisk until combined; the mixture will thicken slightly.
Pour the filling into the warm crust.

stages.title: Bake the filling
steps: Bake for 15 minutes, until the edges are set and the centre still wobbles slightly when the dish is gently shaken.
Cool the pie in the dish on a rack for 30 minutes before chilling.

stages.title: Cool and chill the pie
steps: Cool the pie on the rack for 30 minutes, until no longer warm to touch, then cover loosely with plastic wrap.
Refrigerate for 3 hours, or overnight, until completely firm in the centre.
Put the bowl you will use for the cream in the fridge for the last 15 minutes.

stages.title: Whip the cream and serve
steps: Whisk the thickened cream and icing sugar in the chilled bowl until soft peaks form, about 2–3 minutes.
Spread or pipe the cream over the chilled pie.
Cut with a hot, dry knife, wiping the blade between slices, and serve cold.

tips: Whisking the yolks before adding the condensed milk gives a smoother, silkier filling.
Baking the filling only until the centre still wobbles means it finishes setting as it chills, so it stays creamy instead of turning rubbery.
Pressing the crumbs firmly with a glass stops the crust crumbling when you cut the slices.
Cutting with a hot, dry knife gives clean slices through the set filling.
variations: Replace the lime juice and zest with lemon for a lemon condensed milk pie.
Use gingernut biscuits instead of digestives for a spicier crust.
recipe.storage: Refrigerate, covered, for up to 3 days. Serve cold. Freezing is not recommended as the cream topping becomes watery.

recipe.title: Vietnamese Goi Cuon
recipe.summary: Fresh rice-paper rolls packed with prawns, vermicelli, lettuce and mint, served with peanut sauce.
ingredients: 300 g cooked prawns, peeled and halved lengthways
2 limes, 1 juiced and 1 cut into wedges
60 ml warm water, for the sauce

stages.title: Soak the vermicelli
steps: Place the vermicelli in a heatproof bowl and cover with boiling water from the kettle.
Leave to soak for 5–6 minutes, until soft and no longer firm in the centre.
Drain in a colander, rinse under cold water until cool, then drain well and set aside.

stages.title: Prepare the fillings
steps: Cut the cucumber and carrot into thin batons about 8 cm long.
Tear the lettuce into 12 pieces and pick the mint and coriander leaves.
Halve the cooked prawns lengthways, then arrange all the fillings on a board within easy reach.

stages.title: Make the peanut sauce
steps: In a small bowl, whisk the peanut butter, hoisin sauce, soy sauce and sweet chilli sauce together.
Gradually whisk in 60 ml warm water until smooth and pourable like thin cream.
Squeeze in the juice of 1 lime, stir, and cut the other lime into wedges for serving.

stages.title: Roll the rolls
steps: Fill a wide shallow dish with warm tap water and dip 1 rice paper sheet for 10–15 seconds, until just pliable but still slightly firm. It will keep softening as you work.
Lay the sheet on a clean damp tea towel and place a lettuce piece on the lower third, then top with a small handful of vermicelli, cucumber, carrot, mint and coriander.
Fold the bottom edge over the filling, then fold in both sides.
Roll up firmly halfway, lay 2 prawn halves cut side down along the fold, then finish rolling tightly.
Repeat with the remaining sheets and fillings, covering the finished rolls with a damp tea towel.

stages.title: Serve
steps: Cut the rolls in half on an angle if you like.
Serve straight away with the peanut sauce and lime wedges.

tips: Dip the rice paper only briefly, because it keeps softening as it sits and over-soaked sheets tear and stick.
Rinse the vermicelli in cold water so it does not clump and the rolls do not turn warm and gummy.
Place the prawns near the fold so they show through the translucent wrapper.
Keep finished rolls under a damp tea towel so the wrappers do not dry out and crack.
variations: Replace the prawns with 200 g firm tofu, cut into batons and pan-fried over medium-high heat for 6–8 minutes until golden, and use a vegetarian hoisin sauce (check the label).
Add thin slices of ripe avocado or mango for a sweeter filling.
recipe.storage: Best eaten straight away. Wrap leftover rolls individually in plastic wrap and refrigerate for up to 1 day; the wrappers will toughen. Keep the sauce in a sealed container in the fridge for up to 3 days.

recipe.title: Italian Focaccia
recipe.summary: Fluffy olive-oil bread with a crisp golden crust, rosemary and flaky sea salt.

stages.title: Mix the dough
steps: In a large bowl, combine the bread flour, instant yeast and the 10 g salt.
Pour in the warm water and 1 tbsp of the olive oil.
Mix with a wet hand or spoon for 2–3 minutes, until no dry flour remains and the dough is very sticky.

stages.title: Rest and fold
steps: Cover the bowl with a damp tea towel and rest for 30 minutes.
With a wet hand, lift one edge of the dough and fold it over to the middle. Turn the bowl and repeat 8 times around the dough, then cover and rest for 30 minutes.
Fold the dough the same way again, cover and rest for a further 30 minutes, until puffy and bubbly. That makes 2 sets of folds and 90 minutes in total.

stages.title: Second rise in the tray
steps: Pour 2 tbsp of the olive oil into a 20 x 30 cm baking tray and spread it over the base and sides.
Tip the dough into the tray and turn it once to coat in oil. Gently stretch it towards the corners, stopping if it springs back.
Cover and leave in a warm spot for 40 minutes, until doubled in size, airy and jiggly.
About 15 minutes before the end of the rise, heat the oven to 220°C (200°C fan).

stages.title: Dimple and bake
steps: Drizzle the remaining 1/2 tbsp olive oil over the dough and oil your fingertips.
Press your fingertips straight down to the base of the tray all over the dough to make deep dimples.
Scatter over the rosemary leaves and the flaky sea salt.
Bake on the middle shelf for 22–25 minutes, until deep golden on top and the base is crisp and sounds hollow when tapped.

stages.title: Cool
steps: Leave the focaccia in the tray for 5 minutes, then slide it onto a wire rack.
Cool for 5 minutes more, then cut into squares and serve warm.

tips: A wet, sticky dough traps more steam, which gives the open, airy crumb, so resist adding extra flour.
Folding the dough builds strength without kneading, so it holds its bubbles.
Pressing the dimples right to the tray lets oil pool in them and crisps the base.
Use warm water, not hot, as hot water can kill the yeast.
variations: Press halved cherry tomatoes and pitted kalamata olives into the dimples before baking.
Replace the rosemary with thyme leaves and thinly sliced garlic, adding the garlic just before baking so it doesn't burn.
recipe.storage: Keep in an airtight container at room temperature for 2 days. Freeze sliced pieces for up to 2 months and reheat in a 180°C (160°C fan) oven for 8–10 minutes until warmed through and crisp.

recipe.title: Turkish Lahmacun
recipe.summary: Thin crisp flatbreads topped with warmly spiced minced lamb, tomato, pepper and parsley, finished with lemon.

stages.title: Make the dough
steps: Combine the flour, yeast, sugar and 1/2 tsp of the salt in a large bowl, then stir in 1 tbsp of the olive oil and the 180 ml warm water until a shaggy dough forms.
Knead on a lightly floured bench for 8–10 minutes, until smooth and elastic.
Brush a large bowl with the remaining 1 tbsp olive oil, add the dough and turn it to coat, then cover with a damp tea towel.

stages.title: Prove the dough and heat the oven
steps: Leave the covered dough in a warm spot for 60 minutes in total, until doubled in size and it springs back slowly when pressed.
After the dough has proved for 45 minutes, heat the oven to 250°C (230°C fan) with two large oven trays inside.
Let the trays heat for the final 15 minutes while the dough finishes proving.

stages.title: Make the topping
steps: Combine the lamb mince, tomatoes, capsicum, onion and garlic in a bowl.
Add the tomato paste, paprika, cumin, chilli flakes, two-thirds of the parsley, the remaining 1/2 tsp salt and some black pepper.
Mix well with your hands until a spreadable paste forms.

stages.title: Shape and top
steps: Divide the risen dough into 4 equal pieces and roll each on a floured bench into a thin oval about 3 mm thick.
Spread a very thin layer of the lamb mixture over each oval, right to the edges.
Place each oval on a sheet of baking paper so it can be slid onto the hot trays.

stages.title: Bake and serve
steps: Slide 2 lahmacun with their baking paper onto the hot trays and bake for 6–8 minutes, until the edges are crisp and golden and the lamb is cooked through with no pink remaining.
Bake the remaining 2 lahmacun the same way for 6–8 minutes, until the edges are crisp and golden and the lamb is cooked through with no pink remaining.
Scatter with the remaining parsley and serve hot with lemon wedges, squeezing the juice over before rolling up.

tips: Spreading the topping very thinly lets the lamb cook through before the base over-browns.
Preheating the trays gives the base an instant blast of heat so it turns crisp rather than doughy.
Finely chopping the vegetables stops them releasing excess water, which would make the base soggy.
Rolling the dough thin gives the traditional crisp edge and a flexible centre that folds without cracking.
variations: Use beef mince instead of lamb.
Serve with a salad of rocket, sliced red onion and sumac, rolled up inside the lahmacun.
recipe.storage: Refrigerate cooled lahmacun in an airtight container for up to 3 days or freeze for up to 2 months. Reheat in a 200°C (180°C fan) oven for 5 minutes until hot through and crisp.

recipe.title: Japanese Yaki Onigiri
recipe.summary: Grilled rice triangles with crisp soy-glazed surfaces and tender centres.

stages.title: Season the rice
steps: Spread the warm rice on a tray and leave it for 5 minutes, until it is comfortable to handle but still sticky.
Sprinkle the salt over the rice and mix it through with a rice paddle or spoon, then fold through the sesame seeds.

stages.title: Shape the triangles
steps: Wet your hands with cold water so the rice does not stick.
Divide the rice into 8 equal portions of about 75 g each.
Cup one portion in your palm and press it firmly into a compact triangle about 2 cm thick, turning and pressing until the grains hold together with no cracks.
Repeat with the remaining portions, rewetting your hands as needed.

stages.title: Make the glaze
steps: Stir the soy sauce, mirin and sesame oil together in a small bowl.
Set the bowl and a pastry brush next to the stove so the glaze is ready when the onigiri are crisp.

stages.title: Grill the onigiri
steps: Heat half the vegetable oil in a large non-stick frying pan over medium heat.
Add 4 onigiri and cook for 4–5 minutes on each side, without moving them, until golden and crisp and they release easily from the pan.
Brush the top of each with some of the glaze, turn and cook for 30 seconds until the glaze sizzles and darkens.
Brush the other side, turn again and cook for 30 seconds more, then remove to a plate.

Wipe the pan, heat the remaining vegetable oil over medium heat for 1 minute, then cook the remaining 4 onigiri for 4–5 minutes each side until golden and crisp, glazing them the same way for 30 seconds per side until the glaze darkens.

tips: Shape the rice while it is still warm, as the starch is stickiest then and the triangles hold together in the pan.
Leave the onigiri undisturbed while the first side crisps; moving them early tears the crust and they fall apart.
Brush the glaze on only at the end because the sugar in mirin burns quickly over direct heat.
variations: Press a teaspoon of miso paste mixed with a little mirin into the centre of each triangle before shaping for a salty filling.
Skip the glaze and brush the crisped onigiri with 1 tbsp miso paste thinned with 1 tbsp mirin instead.
recipe.storage: Refrigerate cooled onigiri in an airtight container for up to 2 days. Reheat in a dry non-stick pan over medium heat for 2–3 minutes each side until hot through.

recipe.title: Mexican Chilaquiles Verdes
recipe.summary: Crisp tortilla triangles softened in tangy green salsa, topped with fried eggs, crema and fresh coriander.
ingredients: 8 corn tortillas, each cut into 6 triangles
1 jalapenos, halved and seeded for less heat
1 onion, half roughly chopped, half finely diced
1 bunch coriander, stems and leaves separated, leaves roughly chopped

stages.title: Bake the tortilla triangles
steps: Heat the oven to 200°C (180°C fan) and line two large baking trays with baking paper.
Spread the tortilla triangles in a single layer on the trays and toss with 1 tbsp of the olive oil.
Bake for 12–15 minutes, turning once halfway, until golden and crisp.
Sprinkle with a pinch of the salt and set aside.

stages.title: Simmer and blend the green sauce
steps: Put the tomatillos, jalapenos, the roughly chopped half of the onion, the garlic and the coriander stems in a medium saucepan with 250 ml water.
Bring to the boil over high heat, then reduce to medium-low and simmer for 10 minutes, until the tomatillos are soft and dull olive green.
Tip into a blender with the cooking liquid and blend until smooth.
Stir in the remaining salt, tasting as you go.

stages.title: Reduce the sauce and toss
steps: Heat a large frying pan over medium heat and pour in the blended tomatillo sauce.
Simmer for 5 minutes, until slightly thickened and coating the back of a spoon.
Add the baked tortilla triangles and toss for 1 minute, until coated but with some edges still crisp.
Remove from the heat and divide among 4 plates.

stages.title: Fry the eggs and serve
steps: Heat the remaining 1 tbsp olive oil in a large non-stick frying pan over medium heat.
Crack in the eggs and fry for 3–4 minutes, until the whites are set and the yolks are runny, or cooked through if you prefer.
Top each plate with an egg, then scatter over the finely diced onion and the coriander leaves.
Spoon the sour cream over the top and serve straight away.

tips: Baking the tortillas rather than frying keeps them dry and sturdy, so they hold some crunch under the sauce.
Simmer the tomatillos only until soft; overcooking dulls the sauce's bright, tangy flavour.
Toss the triangles through the sauce just before serving, because they soften within minutes.
Slightly stale tortillas crisp better than fresh ones because they have less moisture to bake off.
variations: Stir shredded cooked chicken through the sauce with the tortilla triangles for a heartier brunch.
Swap the sour cream for crumbled feta for a saltier, sharper finish.
recipe.storage: Keep leftover green sauce in an airtight container in the fridge for up to 4 days and reheat gently in a pan. Assembled chilaquiles are best eaten straight away as the tortilla goes soft.

recipe.title: Mexican Sopa de Tortilla
recipe.summary: Smoky tomato-chilli soup topped with crisp tortilla strips, avocado, lime and fresh coriander.
ingredients: 4 corn tortillas, cut into 1 cm strips

stages.title: Soak the chilli and cut the tortillas
steps: Remove the stem and seeds from the dried ancho chilli, then tear it into pieces and place in a heatproof bowl.
Pour over 250 ml boiling water and soak for 15 minutes, until the chilli is soft and pliable.
Meanwhile, cut the corn tortillas into 1 cm strips, then roughly chop the onion and peel the garlic.

stages.title: Blend the base
steps: Put the soaked chilli in a blender with 2 tbsp of its soaking water, discarding the rest of the water.
Add the canned tomatoes (800 g, with their juice), the onion and the garlic.
Blend for 1 minute until smooth.

stages.title: Fry the puree and simmer the soup
steps: Heat the olive oil in a large saucepan over medium heat.
Pour in the blended puree carefully, as it will spit, and cook, stirring often, for 5 minutes until it darkens and smells fragrant.
Stir in the ground cumin and salt and cook for 30 seconds.
Add the chicken stock and bring to a simmer over medium heat, then reduce the heat to low and simmer gently for 30 minutes, until slightly thickened.

stages.title: Crisp the tortilla strips
steps: While the soup simmers, heat the oven to 200°C (180°C fan) and line a baking tray with baking paper.
Toss the tortilla strips with the vegetable oil on the tray and spread them in a single layer.
Bake for 8–10 minutes, turning once, until golden and crisp. They will crisp further as they cool.

stages.title: Serve
steps: Taste the soup and add a little more salt if needed.
Ladle the soup into four bowls.
Top with the crisp tortilla strips, diced avocado and coriander leaves, and serve with the lime wedges to squeeze over.

tips: Soaking the chilli in hot water softens its tough skin so it blends smoothly without leaving flecks in the soup.
Frying the puree until it darkens cooks off the raw tomato taste and deepens the flavour of the soup.
Add the tortilla strips at the table so they stay crisp rather than going soft in the broth.
variations: Stir 2 cups of shredded cooked chicken into the soup for the last 5 minutes of simmering to make it more filling.
Top each bowl with crumbled feta and a spoonful of sour cream for a creamy finish.
recipe.storage: Refrigerate the soup without toppings in an airtight container for up to 2 days, or freeze for up to 3 months. Reheat gently over medium heat until steaming hot. Store the tortilla strips separately in an airtight container.

recipe.title: Danish Smorrebrod with Smoked Salmon
recipe.summary: Open rye sandwiches topped with smoked salmon, lemony cream cheese, cucumber and dill.
ingredients: 1 bunch dill, fronds picked and roughly chopped

stages.title: Prepare the toppings
steps: Cut the cucumber into thin ribbons or slices with a vegetable peeler or sharp knife, then sprinkle with the salt and leave in a bowl for 10 minutes.
Finely grate the zest of the lemon, then juice half of it and cut the other half into 4 wedges.
Pick the dill fronds from the stalks and roughly chop them, reserving 4 small sprigs for garnish.

stages.title: Make the lemon dill cream cheese
steps: Beat the softened cream cheese in a bowl with a spoon until smooth.
Stir in the lemon zest, 2 tsp lemon juice and the chopped dill.
Season with black pepper and taste, adding a little more lemon juice if you want it sharper.

stages.title: Assemble the smorrebrod
steps: Pat the salted cucumber dry with paper towel to remove the liquid.
Spread each slice of rye bread thinly with butter, right to the edges, so the cream cheese does not soak in.
Spread the lemon dill cream cheese over the butter in an even layer.
Fold or drape the smoked salmon over the cream cheese in loose waves, then top with the cucumber.
Garnish each slice with a dill sprig and a grind of black pepper, and serve with a lemon wedge for squeezing over.

tips: Buttering the rye to the edges creates a barrier that keeps the bread from going soggy under the cream cheese.
Salting the cucumber draws out water, so the topping stays crisp and does not make the salmon wet.
Dense, dark rye holds up to the toppings; soft sliced bread collapses and is hard to eat with a knife and fork.
Softened cream cheese blends smoothly with the lemon and dill without lumps, so take it out of the fridge 20 minutes ahead.
variations: Replace the salmon with sliced hard-boiled eggs and thinly sliced radishes, cooking the eggs in simmering water for 10 minutes until the yolks are firm.
Swap the cream cheese for sour cream mixed with a teaspoon of horseradish-style mustard such as dijon for a sharper topping.
recipe.storage: Best eaten straight away. Keep any leftover lemon dill cream cheese covered in the fridge for up to 2 days and assemble fresh.

recipe.title: Mexican Esquites
recipe.summary: Sweet charred corn tossed with lime, chilli, creamy dressing and crumbled cotija cheese.
ingredients: 500 g corn kernels, drained and patted dry if canned, or thawed if frozen

stages.title: Prepare the corn and toppings
steps: Drain the corn well if canned, or thaw it if frozen, then pat it very dry with paper towel so it chars rather than steams.
Zest the lime finely, then juice it and keep the zest and juice separate.
Crumble the feta into small pieces and roughly chop the coriander.
Stir the mayonnaise, lime zest, half the lime juice and half the chilli powder together in a large bowl.

stages.title: Char the corn
steps: Heat the butter in a large frying pan over high heat until it foams.
Add the corn in a single layer and cook for 3 minutes without stirring, until browned underneath.
Stir, then cook for another 4–5 minutes, stirring only every minute or so, until the kernels are charred in spots and lightly popping.
Stir in the salt and the remaining lime juice, then remove the pan from the heat.

stages.title: Dress and serve
steps: Tip the hot corn into the bowl with the mayonnaise mixture and toss until evenly coated.
Spoon into 4 small bowls or cups.
Top with the feta, coriander and the remaining chilli powder, and serve warm.

tips: Drying the corn thoroughly lets it brown and char instead of steaming, which gives the smoky flavour esquites are known for.
Leaving the corn undisturbed for the first 3 minutes builds charred patches; constant stirring keeps the pan temperature down.
Dress the corn while still hot so the mayonnaise loosens slightly and coats every kernel.
Feta is a salty, crumbly stand-in for cotija; it is already salty, so taste before adding more salt.
variations: Add 1 finely chopped red chilli or a few slices of pickled jalapenos to the pan for a hotter version.
Swap half the mayonnaise for sour cream for a tangier, lighter dressing.
recipe.storage: Best eaten straight away. Refrigerate leftovers in an airtight container for up to 2 days and reheat in a frying pan over medium heat for 2–3 minutes, or eat cold as a salad.

recipe.title: Egyptian Ful Medames
recipe.summary: Warm mashed fava beans with cumin, lemon, garlic and olive oil, scooped up with flatbread.

stages.title: Prepare the toppings
steps: Finely chop the tomatoes and discard the watery seeds if very wet.
Pick and finely chop the parsley leaves.
Crush the garlic with the salt into a rough paste.
Juice the lemons; you need about 80 ml juice.

stages.title: Simmer the beans
steps: Tip the fava beans and their liquid from both cans into a medium saucepan.
Add 100 ml water and bring to a simmer over medium heat, then cook for 8–10 minutes, stirring occasionally, until the beans are hot and the liquid has reduced slightly.
Stir in the ground cumin and black pepper and cook for 1 minute.

stages.title: Mash and season
steps: Reduce the heat to low and mash about half the beans against the side of the pan with a fork or the back of a wooden spoon, leaving the rest whole.
Stir in the garlic paste, 1 tbsp of the olive oil and two-thirds of the lemon juice.
Simmer for 3–4 minutes, stirring, until thick and creamy but still spoonable; add a splash of water if it looks dry.

stages.title: Warm the bread and serve
steps: Warm the pita bread in a dry frying pan over medium heat for 1 minute each side, until soft and lightly toasted.
Divide the beans among four bowls.
Top with the tomatoes, parsley and chilli flakes, then drizzle with the remaining 2 tbsp olive oil and the remaining lemon juice.
Serve straight away with the warm pita bread.

tips: Canned fava beans are already cooked, so a short simmer is enough to heat them and thicken the liquid; longer cooking turns them dry and dull.
Mashing only half the beans makes a creamy base while keeping some whole beans for texture.
Crushing garlic with salt breaks it into a paste that spreads evenly instead of leaving raw chunks.
Keeping some lemon juice for the end preserves its fresh flavour, which fades with long simmering.
variations: Top each bowl with a chopped hard-boiled egg, boiled for 10 minutes until the yolk is firm.
Stir 2 tbsp tahini in with the garlic paste for a richer, nuttier bowl.
recipe.storage: Refrigerate the beans without toppings in an airtight container for up to 3 days. Reheat in a saucepan over low heat with a splash of water until hot, stirring often. Add fresh tomato and parsley when serving.

recipe.title: Italian Caprese Panini
recipe.summary: Toasted ciabatta layered with creamy mozzarella, ripe tomatoes, basil and a little pesto.

stages.title: Slice the fillings
steps: Slice the mozzarella into 5 mm thick slices.
Slice the tomatoes into 5 mm thick rounds, discarding the end pieces.
Pick the basil leaves from the stems and set them aside.

stages.title: Drain the mozzarella and tomato
steps: Lay the mozzarella and tomato slices in a single layer on a tray lined with paper towel.
Sprinkle the tomato with the salt and leave for 10 minutes to draw out the liquid.
Pat the slices dry with more paper towel just before using.

stages.title: Assemble the paninis
steps: Cut each ciabatta roll in half horizontally.
Spread the pesto over the cut sides of every roll, using 1 tbsp per roll.
Layer the mozzarella, tomato and basil leaves over the bottom halves, grinding over black pepper, then close the rolls.
Brush the outsides of the rolls lightly with the olive oil.

stages.title: Toast the paninis
steps: Heat a panini press or sandwich press to medium-high.
Toast 2 paninis at a time for 4–5 minutes, until the rolls are golden with crisp grill marks and the mozzarella has softened and started to melt.
Repeat with the remaining 2 paninis, then rest all four for 1 minute before cutting in half and serving.

tips: Salting and drying the tomato slices removes surface moisture, which keeps the rolls crisp instead of soggy.
Fresh mozzarella in brine holds a lot of water, so patting it dry stops it leaking out as it melts.
Pressing the paninis lightly rather than hard keeps the filling from squeezing out the sides.
variations: Swap the basil pesto for a sun-dried tomato pesto and add a handful of rocket after toasting.
Add 2 slices of ham to each roll for a heartier panini.
recipe.storage: Best eaten straight after toasting. Refrigerate leftovers in an airtight container for up to 1 day and reheat in a sandwich press until hot through, though the rolls will be less crisp.

recipe.title: Greek Gemista Stuffed Tomatoes
recipe.summary: Oven-baked tomatoes and peppers filled with herbed rice, pine nuts and sweet onions.

stages.title: Hollow the vegetables
steps: Heat the oven to 190°C (170°C fan).
Slice the tops off the tomatoes and capsicums and keep the tops. Remove the seeds and membranes from the capsicums.
Scoop the flesh out of the tomatoes with a spoon, leaving a shell about 1 cm thick. Chop the pulp roughly and keep it with its juices in a bowl.
Stand the tomato and capsicum shells upright, snugly together, in a baking dish.

stages.title: Cook the filling
steps: Heat 2 tbsp olive oil in a frying pan over medium heat. Cook the onion for 4–5 minutes, stirring, until soft and translucent.
Add the garlic and pine nuts and cook for 1 minute, stirring, until the pine nuts start to turn golden.
Stir in the rice, the chopped tomato pulp and juices, the salt and the black pepper. Cook for 2–3 minutes, stirring, until the juices start to bubble.
Remove the pan from the heat and stir through the parsley and mint.

stages.title: Fill the vegetables
steps: Spoon the filling into the shells until they are about three-quarters full, so the rice has room to expand.
Put the tops back on the tomatoes and capsicums.
Pour the vegetable stock into the base of the dish around the vegetables.
Drizzle the remaining 1 tbsp olive oil over the tops.

stages.title: Bake covered
steps: Cover the dish tightly with foil.
Bake for 40 minutes, until the vegetables have softened and the rice has absorbed most of the stock.

stages.title: Uncover, brown and rest
steps: Remove the foil and bake for a further 15 minutes, until the tops are browned and the stock in the dish has reduced to a few spoonfuls.
Taste a grain of rice from the centre of one capsicum; it should be tender with no firm centre. If it is still firm, cover with foil and bake for 5 minutes more, then test again.
Rest the dish for 10 minutes before serving, spooning the pan juices over each vegetable.

tips: Fill the shells only three-quarters full, because the rice swells as it cooks and will push the tops off if packed in.
Pack the vegetables tightly in the dish so they hold each other upright and cook in the shared steam.
Frying the rice briefly with the onion and oil before baking coats the grains, which helps them stay separate rather than gluey.
Resting the dish before serving lets the juices settle, and the flavours are better warm than piping hot.
variations: Add 2 tbsp sultanas to the filling with the rice for a sweeter, more traditional taste.
Add 1 potato, cut into wedges, to the dish around the vegetables so it cooks in the stock and tomato juices.
recipe.storage: Refrigerate in an airtight container for up to 3 days. Reheat covered in a 180°C (160°C fan) oven for 15–20 minutes until hot throughout. Also good at room temperature.
